Belgien, Spanien, Italien, Frankreich…: Die Wut der Jugend auf einen verrottenden Kapitalismus wächst


„

Die Lage in Frankreich findet in mehreren anderen Ländern des Kontinents Widerhall, die von aufkeimenden Mobilisierungen der Jugend erschüttert werden, die in die Fußstapfen der französischen Oberschulen treten. Verschuldung, Abbau öffentlicher Dienstleistungen, Militarisierung und Unterdrückung der Jugend: Gegen die Pläne der europäischen Bourgeoisie formiert sich erster, vielversprechender Widerstand. (…)


Der alte Kontinent beginnt im Rhythmus der Jugendrevolten zu beben – in deutschen, belgischen, italienischen, französischen und spanischen Oberschulen [bzw. an den weiterführenden Schulen, Anm. d. Ü.]. Und obwohl diese Bewegungen nicht das gleiche Ausmaß haben, spiegeln sie doch das tiefere Unbehagen wider, das ganze Schichten der Arbeiter:innenklasse in ihren Ländern betrifft. Ob bewusst oder unbewusst – diese internationalistische Konvergenz der Jugend weist den Weg im Kampf gegen die schreckliche Zukunft, die der Kapitalismus ihr in den kommenden Jahren bereithält. (…) Diese Welle, die die wichtigsten kapitalistischen Länder Kontinentaleuropas erfasst, drückt etwas sehr Tiefgreifendes aus. Sie geht über den Rahmen einer bloßen konjunkturellen Reaktion auf eine Offensive einer Regierung hinaus, sondern spiegelt einen starken Trend zur Mobilisierung der Jugend gegen die gesamte Gesellschaft und die Zukunft wider, die ihr von den herrschenden Klassen vorgesetzt wird. Ob in Spanien, Deutschland, Italien, Frankreich oder Belgien: Auch wenn sich die Mobilisierungen der europäischen Jugend auf unterschiedliche Forderungen stützen, prangern sie doch ein und dasselbe kapitalistische System an, das am Ende seiner Kräfte ist und unfähig ist, der Jugend des Kontinents auch nur die geringste Perspektive auf Emanzipation zu bieten.

author: Novara Media
title: China’s Century of Revolutions
content:
For a century, China underwent a series of invasions, revolutions and counter-revolutions. In China, it’s known as the Century of Humiliation.


It was a time of immense upheavals: from the Opium Wars of 1839, through the Taiping Rebellion, the Xinhai Republican Revolution, a Civil War, an invasion by the Japanese which merged into the Second World War; the resumption of the Civil War and, eventually coming to an end with the Communist Revolution of 1949.


Each one transformed the country more comprehensively than seemed possible beforehand.


Rebecca Karl is the author of

China’s Revolutions in the Modern World

, which tells us not only what happened, but how its participants tried to make sense of it all, and why that still matters for understanding China now – after all, the Chinese Communist Party haven’t forgotten any of it.


She joined Richard Hames to discuss the century that destroyed imperial China and set the stage for the largest revolution in history.


There is much more to explore on the map we’re making for this series, which shows all the people, ideas and event that define China’s history, present, and future. Get it

here

.

title: Various Authors - Products of Desire
content:
Author

: Various Authors

Title

: Products of Desire

Subtitle

: On Loving the Unreal

Date

: 2019

Source

: <

littleblackcart.com/index.php?dispatch=products.view&product_id=625

> [Even though the website says the book is in stock, the book publisher is no longer.]


 


 This work features excerpts from three pieces which explore the ways a desire for the impossible changes the way we see reality itself. Patrick Galbraith explores affection for anime characters as resistance to society, J. Keith Vincent looks at the queerness of a desire that “decouple[s] sexual desire from social identities and naturalized bodies”, and Toshio Okada (of Gainax fame) and Kaichiro Morikawa debate fans as anti-social vs. fans as customers.


 


Moe:

 Exploring Virtual Potential in Post-Millennial Japan


 Original article at

https://www.academia.edu/3665389/Moe_Exploring_ Virtual_Potential_in_Post-Millennial_Japan


Making it Real: Fiction, Desire, and the Queerness of the Beautiful Fighting Girl by Keith Vincent, from

Beautiful Fighting Girl

 by Tamaki Saitou, tr. Keith Vincent and Dawn Lawson, University of Minnesota Press, 2011


Otaku Talk


 original article located at

https://www.gwern.net/docs/eva/2004-okada


** Products of Desire


**On Loving the Unreal**


 


 I hesitated to make this pamphlet because it’s about something so ridiculous yet intimate. Despite the often academic prose of these articles, it’s hard not to feel a bit exposed by their contents. If you’ve ever seen one of those iconic images of a fan’s bedroom— those immaculately decorated exemplars of horror vacui with every inch covered in (often lewd) posters and (often expensive) figures—this is the territory we’re stepping into. In a way, however abstract the writing may sometimes be, I’m inviting you into my bedroom. At the heart of this writing is always this space of intense desire. Perhaps this is a space you’re already familiar with—maybe it’s your bedroom too, or maybe you’ve only caught glimpses of it in the shadier portions of the internet. Perhaps you just felt weird watching Disney’s Robin Hood when you were younger.


 The desire discussed here is focused on otaku (anime fans) because of the richness of critical examinations surrounding them (as well as because of the specific interests of this author), but the ideas discussed could apply to cartoon fans in general, to furries, or to any of the many circles in which deep affection is felt for the unreal. The point is to explore that desire, however briefly, to see what it does and where it goes.


 A subject of interest to two of the authors contained herein is how love for the unreal implicates any stable concept of reality itself. For J. Keith Vincent, writing about Tamaki Saitou’s

[1]

 Beautiful Fighting Girl (Saitou himself drawing on Lacanian theories around perceiving reality), there is a queerness to this attraction that “decouple[s] sexual desire from social identities and naturalized

bodies”. Patrick

 Galbraith’s

[2]

 treatment of moe (pronounced mo-ay and defined by him in short as an intense emotional response to a fantasy character) finds in this desire for the unreal a “certain refusal” of dominant forms of life founded in the home and family, and connects this (however briefly) to Lee Edelmen’s refusal of “reproductive futurism”. Vincent’s piece offers a more comfortable vision of the desiring subject (ultimately “there is a little otaku in all of us”) to Galbraith’s more expansive and transgressive moe, but both give us different and insightful takes on similar subject matter.


 Our final piece, an excerpt from a discussion between Toshio Okada

[3]

 and Kaichiro Morikawa

[4]

 and moderated by Takashi Murakami

[5]

, further highlights a tension that the reader will see in both of the aforementioned pieces: the question of how different these people actually are, despite their exotic tastes. The otaku’s response to dominant reality is debated—Morikawa claiming that moe, rather than more clearly political or utopian thinking in science fiction, “has replaced the future.” Morikawa also characterizes otaku as those who gravitate towards socially unacceptable things. Okada however describes them as merely a different kind of consumer: “tough customers who demand high standards,” discerning consumers who value quality.


 In the end, the desires featured in these articles don’t appear to be a way out—in some cases far from it. We are presented again and again with …

title: the reason why you don’t see women raping or sexually exploiting men as often as the other way…
content:
the reason why you don’t see women raping or sexually exploiting men as often as the other way around, isn’t because women have the divine aura of femininity that prevents them from thinking rapist thoughts, or because cis women lack the Evil Rape Organ or whatever. it is because rape isn’t really purely individual form of violence, but a systemic one. it is also not necessarily done only for personal sexual gratification, but a reassertion of social position through violence.

women hold a lower position compared to men within patriarchy. if you hold a position lower than someone else, then violence against them is not typically something you can get away with, nor can you assert your power over them if you don’t have it.

this is also why the vast majority of cases of women raping or sexually exploiting men are done when a woman holds a higher social position than the man in question. you see this with disparity in class, age (in the case of women sexually abusing children), between white and racialised, and between imperialist and imperialised. most notable examples are the women abusing and torturing prisoners in Abu Ghraib as much as their male colleagues, or the female Israeli prison guards torturing Palestinians.

and of course, women sexually exploiting or abusing other women is done on similar grounds. it is more common for cis women to sexually exploit or abuse trans women than the other way around for example.

Корреспондент газеты Avanti! из Йези, сообщая о публичном выступлении против принудительной ссылки[1], которую я провёл в этом городе, пишет: «… Он добавил (оратор), что огромная вина (за рабскую покорность, с которой народ терпел притеснения правительства и капиталистов) лежит на анархической партии и республиканской партии, которые, проповедовав столь долго революцию, осознают невозможность её совершить, поскольку народ, совершенно несознательный, за ними не пойдёт»[2].

Так оно и было – это действительно то, что я сказал; но курсив, разумеется, корреспондент добавил от себя, и этот курсив в социал-демократической газете служит для того, чтобы хорошенько отметить (и, возможно, похвастаться), что я, критикуя мою партию и республиканскую, исключал из критики социал-демократов.

Это требует некоторого объяснения.

В Йези я говорил о разочарованиях, последовавших за надеждами, возбуждёнными итальянской национальной революцией, и говорил о том, как, с одной стороны, экономическое положение пролетариата становилось всё более тяжёлым, а с другой – постепенно утрачивалась та небольшая свобода, которую завоевала революция, вплоть до возвращения в состояние, равное или худшее тому, в котором находились при павших правительствах.

И я старался объяснить этот факт двумя рядами причин.

Во-первых, тенденцией, которую имеют общественные учреждения развиваться в определённом направлении и производить свои естественные следствия: тенденцией политической власти всегда расширять свою сферу действия и становиться всё более угнетающей; и тенденцией частной собственности захватывать все средства производства, всё более усиливать эксплуатацию работника и обращать во вред пролетариату все новые достижения науки и общественного прогресса.

Во-вторых, отсутствием народного сопротивления. И в этом отсутствии сопротивления, оставляя в стороне другие причины общего порядка, не входившие в цель того моего публичного выступления, я обвинял республиканцев и анархистов.

И те и другие, сознавая коренную несправедливость определённых учреждений и те дурные последствия, которые они фатально должны были принести, заботились только о полном и внезапном разрушении этих учреждений, презирая всё, что могло бы смягчить эти дурные последствия, – более того, желая, чтобы они проявились как можно острее, в надежде, что это вызовет и ускорит падение учреждений.

Республиканцы, естественно враждебные монархии, все беды возводили к конституционному [монархическому] режиму и либо не считали возможным, либо по тактике делали вид, что презирают любое улучшение, любую реформу, отправной точкой которой не было бы упразднение монархии.

Анархисты, противники всякого правительства и, следовательно, монархии, и противники частной собственности, ждали – по идее, аналогичной идее республиканцев, – всякого блага от радикального преобразования общественной организации, презирая улучшения, к которым может быть восприимчив нынешний режим, и, может быть, желая – всё в той же надежде ускорить конфликт – роста угнетения и нищеты.

Так вся деятельность двух партий сводилась к проповеди революции. Что же касается того, чтобы сделать её возможной и подготовить её, то они не умели делать ничего другого, как только вербовать в соответствующие организации приверженцев, по необходимости немногочисленных, и собирать оружие, которое из-за отсутствия средств и бдительности правительства всегда было мало и плохо и в конце концов обычно либо конфисковывалось, либо ржавело и становилось непригодным. К этому, мадзинисты сначала, а анархисты потом, добавляли развлечение с той или иной более или менее безобидной бомбой.

Между тем приверженцы, оттого что ждали революцию, ничего не делая, в конце концов совсем засыпали; а массы народа – …

author: heinhtetkyaw
title: The Last Defense of the Lake: From Environmental Conservation to Political Revolution
content:
For over seven decades, Myanmar was consumed by the world’s longest civil war, but the Intha (Insaku), the "Children of the Lake/The People of The Lake," remained a peaceful exception. Nestled among high mountain peaks in Shan State, they lived peacefully with nature on the still waters of Inle Lake, famous worldwide for their stilt houses, floating gardens (ye-chan), and iconic leg-rowing fishermen, or at least that's what the state and tourism agency’s narrative for their brand image. The iconic leg-rowing fishermen have become a brand of Myanmar's tourism campaign since 1996, when the military was promising market reform and democracy.

Although recognized as one of Myanmar's 135 distinct indigenous groups, the Intha remain a "minority within a minority" in Southern Shan State, distinct in language and history from their Shan, Pa'O, Lisu, Taungtha, Kareni, and Danu neighbors, and their language is a branch of Widely accepted theories suggest their ancestors migrated from Lower Burma, Dawei, a long time ago, or a group of Tibeto-Burman who were still left behind. At the same time, the rest moved forward to the Irrawaddy Valley. Applying James C. Scott’s concept of “Zomia,” which describes upland societies that historically avoided centralized state control, the Intha experience can be understood as a form of aquatic adaptation. Rather than escaping into mountains, they survived on an economically marginal lake environment surrounded by hills. Their oral histories and religious traditions contain accounts of resistance against local feudal authorities. Even during British colonial rule, the region was viewed less as a profitable administrative center and more as a scenic recreational area. This delicate socio-ecological balance began to shatter after the 2010 political reforms. Under President Thein Sein’s administration, military-tied tycoons and international investors targeted the lake's eastern shore for a massive "Hotel Zone" project. The infrastructure building has leveled hillsides, drained wetlands, and seized land with minimal compensation for the local population, leading to severe ecological damage, driving local fish populations toward extinction, and destroying traditional livelihoods. Although Inle Lake was designated Myanmar's first UNESCO Biosphere Reserve in 2015, the surrounding Inlay Lake Wildlife Sanctuary had already been recognized as an ASEAN Heritage Park in 2003. It was later designated Myanmar's fifth Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2018. Despite these international conservation recognitions, environmental degradation driven by deforestation, unsustainable agriculture, tourism development, and weak conservation governance has continued. One of the most controversial cases involved Myanmar Naing Group Co., Ltd., owned by U Tun Naing Shwe, son of former military ruler Than Shwe, which proposed to construct a luxury hotel on land that had previously been part of the Inle Lake Wildlife Sanctuary. The proposal sparked widespread opposition from local communities, environmental organizations, and government agencies, becoming a prominent example of the conflict between tourism development and environmental conservation around Inle Lake. Many farmers and fishermen lost their way of life; many were forced to migrate abroad for work. Those who stayed were pushed into minimum-wage work in construction and the hospital sector. Some local activists and scholars have criticized the commercialization of Inle Lake’s cultural practices, arguing that activities such as staged leg-row fishing and ethnic performances risk transforming living traditions into tourist spectacles rather than preserving their original social meaning. The commercialization of agriculture and watershed degradation has intensified the ecological crisis at Inle Lake. Historically, the lake’s unique wetland ecosystem allowed the Intha to develop floating-garden agriculture, with tomatoes becoming one of the region’s most important economic crops. However, expanding domestic and regional markets encouraged increased use of chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and commercial seeds, contributing to nutrient pollution and ecological stress. At the same time, state land policies allowed customary lands in Shan State to be classified as vacant or wasteland and allocated to large-scale investors and military-linked companies. author: Patrick William Kelly
title: The Person They Never Asked About
content:
A

fter lights out at the state forensic hospital, a worker would peer through my door’s square window every fifteen minutes. He would quickly flick the overhead light on and off—just long enough to record whether I was breathing and in what position I was sleeping. Sometimes I could hear him whispering the data aloud to a partner making rounds alongside him, recounting our bodily orientations like buried bodies in a graveyard:


Left side. Right side. Back.


They knew the position in which my body slept every fifteen minutes for ten months. But they rarely asked me a personal question about my life.


I spent fourteen months in county jails and a state psychiatric hospital after accepting a not-guilty-by-reason-of-mental-disease plea on eight felony stalking charges arising from a psychotic manic episode. I had a doctorate from the University of Chicago and a book with Cambridge University Press. I had also been misdiagnosed by four different hospital systems, prescribed the wrong class of medications for four years, and carried an undetected neurosyphilis infection that inflamed my brain while every clinician I encountered looked somewhere else. By the time I arrived at Mendota Mental Health Institute, Wisconsin’s forensic psychiatric hospital, in January of 2025, the system had demonstrated an extraordinary capacity to observe and document me and an almost total incapacity to know me.


The maximum-security units were arranged in a hub-and-spoke design. A central core provided sightlines into four radiating wards, each terminating in a nurse’s station enclosed in tinted glass from which staff monitored and documented; from the dayroom, we could often see them behind the glass looking down at their phones. Exchanges with psychiatric care technicians (PCTs) occurred only through a narrow request portal, whose hours had shrunk over the years to ten or fifteen minutes per hour. The portal was a test: could you wait and follow the rules? Could you manage your frustration with the demands of bureaucratic order while practicing the skills of emotional regulation? These were the questions the watchtower was built to answer. Whether you were suffering, or confused, or intellectually alive, or desperately lonely—these were questions the watchtower had no room for.


Goffman argued in

Asylums

 that total institutions mortify the self through a process in which “all acts of resistance by the so-called mentally ill” become “just further evidence, in the eyes of the staff, of their mental incompetence and illness.” Mendota was not a mid-century asylum—it was cleaner, better staffed, and far more humane. But the structural logic Goffman recognized had not vanished; it had just been refined. I intend this less as a polemic than as an honest portrayal—a careful account, from the inside, of a system that has developed a more sophisticated capacity to measure a human being than to know one.


II.


Through the wall of my room at Mendota, my neighbor Johnnie—a man with schizophrenia—was the conductor of a full symphony of voices no one else could hear. In one movement alone, he shifted seamlessly from polite dialogue to laughter to verbal combat. Then came the machine-gun of counting: “One-one, two-two, three-three”—up to twenty, silence, followed by another cartridge. Each number landed twice, as if repetition could nail it to the fabric of reality. In a world where thoughts bled into voices and voices blurred into persecution, counting seemed to provide Johnnie with an anchor—a metronome to ward off psychic freefall. What looked like madness from the outside was, from within, a courageous effort at coherence.


He often cornered me in the hallway to announce an epiphany, “Vocationally, spiritually, politically, logistically, the zebra is the outright leader of the animal kingdom—correct, Patrick?” I learned that polite agreement was the kindest response. Johnnie called me by name, and the institution did not always manage that.


In a psychology group one afternoon, our therapist asked us why it was so hard to be happy. We sat in a semicircle—six men adjudicated dangerous to themselves or others, parsing the nature of happiness like students in a high school ethics class. At the end of the session, Johnnie shot up his hand. “I’d just like to say it’s important to remember the following: we’re not sick, we need a sheikh!” The room burst into scattered laughter. And for a brief instant, the cage dissolved.


Johnnie’s …

author: webadmin
title: All Warning, No Action?
content:
As more hunts receive police warnings and notices, are they a route to meaningful action, or a substitute for it?


Many of you cannot have failed to notice that we are writing more and more about hunts being issued with Community Protection Warnings (CPWs) and, occasionally, the CPW’s big sister, the Community Protection Notice (CPN). The former of course precedes the latter.


What in the puck is this? The Puckeridge and Essex Hunts have had 3 CPWs and a CPN and they still ignore them. Image: East Herts Hunt Sabs.


The Community Protection Notice system, including the requirement to issue a warning first, was introduced in 2014 by David Cameron’s Conservative-led coalition government, under then Home Secretary Theresa May as part of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime & Policing Act 2014.


The irony that these measures are now being used, more and more, to regulate the conduct of fox hunts, an activity that has recently been publicly defended by Cameron, is not lost on us.


A CPW is not a criminal conviction. Ignoring one is not, in itself, a criminal offence, and there is no automatic penalty for failing to comply. If the behaviour continues, the police can escalate matters by issuing a CPN. Unlike a warning, a CPN imposes legally enforceable requirements, and breaching those requirements without reasonable excuse is a criminal offence.


Warning, Warning, Warning. No Action


Most recently, Kernow Hunt Sabs revealed that one of their local hunts, the Four Burrow Hunt, has received a Community Protection Warning. One important point is that Devon & Cornwall Police have not issued a press release on the conditions or areas affected, although details have been

published elsewhere

.


Masked terrier-men on Dartmoor having just been caught about to dig a fox out of a badger sett. Image: Plymouth and West Devon Hunt Saboteurs 2026.


The same police force has been busy issuing these warnings. Plymouth & West Devon Hunt Saboteurs also announced that one has been issued to the Dartmoor Hunt. Although Devon & Cornwall police confirmed its existence in response to a Freedom of Information request, they have not published details of the locations concerned or the conditions the hunt must comply with.


The Dartmoor Hunt killing a fox in March 2026. Image: Devon County Hunt Saboteurs


Earlier this year, the force also issued a warning to the North Cornwall Hunt. While its

press release

 did not name the hunt, referring instead to a ‘hunt group within their force area’, it did provide comprehensive details of the locations and conditions covered by the warning.


Yet their wider record on handling hunt-related offences leaves a lot to be desired, particularly in relation to the

Eggesford Hunt where previous investigations and prosecutions

 have raised serious questions. Answers are still needed.


A look at other police forces issuing CPWs and CPNs reveals a myriad of problems.


Albrighton & Woodland Hunt – Still Waiting After All These Years


In March 2024, Staffordshire Police issued the Albrighton and Woodland Hunt with a Community Protection Warning following repeated incidents involving uncontrolled hounds, trespass and the killing of wildlife.


Less than a year later, on 15 February 2025, hounds were photographed loose on the A458 near the Enville Estate, bringing traffic to a standstill.


Ambulances held up by hound carnage on the A458. Image: Locals Opposed to the Albrighton and Woodland Hunt.


The A458 incident is not the only incident involving the hunt while its CPW remained in place. In June 2026, Albrighton and Woodland Huntsman

Paul Larby and whipper-in Phillipa Ward

 were sentenced following their convictions for assaulting a female member of Shropshire Wildlife Monitors in 2024.


This was not even the first CPW for this hunt. Staffordshire Police had already issued one in February 2019. Five years later, following further incidents involving uncontrolled hounds, trespass, property damage and the killing of a fox and muntjac deer, the police’s response was…to issue another warning!


The current warning is in effect until March 2027.


Despite further documented incidents, including two assault convictions involving hunt staff, and a previous CPW, the hunt still remains subject to a warning rather than an enforceable Community Protection Notice.


Shropshire Hunts – Warnings Keep Coming


The Albrighton and Woodland is far from the only hunt in the region to have attracted police attention. The …

title: Preparativos Zapatistas para el Encuentro Abrazo con familias Buscadoras. Parte I: Jóvenes Teatristas
content:
Música: Caifanes, «Antes de que nos olviden» Imágenes: Terci@s Compas Zapatistas

Estaba yo como quien dice, así nomás, acaso estoy pensando nada. Pero tenía yo mi mejor cara del más caifán de los caifanes, el más banda y chido de la banda y de los chidos. Así estoy pues y ahí nomás lo miro que viene caminando el Riko, que no así se llama mero de bautizo, sino que así se puso porque, dice, es el más chulo del barrio, de la broza, de la plebe, y que todas las morras pues suspiran por él merengues. Riko o “Rikolin” se autodenomina, dice que el otro día pelearon por él dos chavas, pero yo lo sé que sí pelearon, pero no por él, sino porque la de la miscelánea no le dio cabal el cambio a la otra. Pero el Riko Rickolin jura y perjura que fue por el privilegio de sus encantos. Bueno, de ahí que llega y me dice: “¿Qué pues mi capi? ¿andas de incónito?”. “Incógnito”, se dice “incógnito”, le corrijo. “Eso”, dice el Riko, y sigue “¿y qué jais de la wuirinais”. El Riko cree que habla con caló de barrio, pero ni mais palomas naranjas podridas. “Pos aquí pichiluqueando”, le respondo para seguirle la corriente. El Riko ve que no hay nadie más y abandona la pose ligadora número 69 de su catálogo, y me pregunta “¿y que piensas de eso?”. “¿Cuál eso?” “Pos eso” “No sé qué es eso”. “Pos lo que se anda rumoreando por ahí, el chisme pues. O como dicen las jóvenas zapatudas: “la información compartida”. O sea que mismo chisme, pero más elegante.” “No sé qué cosa se anda rumorando”. “Pos eso, que un tokin” “¿Cuál tokín?” “Oh pues, tokín dícese de cuando hay una tocada, unas rolas, un concierto pues. O sea que no es un tokín de prexta pá la orquexta, sino tokin musical”. “Ah, ya. No, no sé nada”, digo fingiendo desinterés, porque sé que eso provoca más al Riko. El Riko se sienta en la banqueta y me susurra: “un concierto, no mero sé dónde ni cuándo, pero un concierto. Quesque los meros Caifanes, y que mi novia la Ely Guerra, y que la Vivir Quintana, y que los Contingentes Jaraneros, y que el Kevin Kaarl, y que el Meme del Real. Juntos, pero no revueltos.

O sea que el todo y las partes, como quien dice.”

“Y ¿dónde, cuándo, cómo, por qué?”, lo apremio.

“A saber”, dice el Riko, encendiendo lo que creo es un cigarrillo, “creo que no lo dicen luego porque tienen miedo de que les caiga la justicia”.

“¿Por qué les caería la justicia? ¿Para qué es pues el concierto?” “Pos para el encuentro-abrazo con las familias buscadoras” “¿Y eso que tiene de malo? ¿Por qué les va a caer la tira?” “Okela, pos por el Meme, ¿no sabes que ya prohibieron los memes? Y pos luego la tira no muy le sabe a nada, y creo que se levantan a todos… y todas, no olvidar la paridad de género. Pa no fallarle, dicen”. “Ah, pos está cabreras”, digo ya entrando en ambiente. “Pero si no se sabe cuándo y dónde, ¿cómo le va a hacer la banda para caerle’”, pregunto.

“Ni idea”, dice el Riko, “pero creo no tarda, porque si no, pues de balde una tocada si nadie sabe dónde y cuándo.

Pero el asunto, mi estimado capitán balín, es que nadie cobra, o sea ni los que le hacen de musiqueros, ni quienes organizan, ni quienes producen, ni quienes ponen el local. Sacan el gasto, nada de ganancia propia, todo para el encuentro. Por solidaridad de la buena. Es más, ni yo les voy a cobrar. Voy a ir a apersonarme gratis. Para darle como quien dice brillo y realce al evento. Todo el varo es para el encuentro con buscadoras. Todo cabal, todo planchado.”

“Nah, no te creo”, le dije para ver si soltaba algo más.

El Riko se pone de pie y sentencia:

“Ése es el problema, que ya nadie cree en nada. No creen en la solidaridad desinteresada, en la bondad, en la nobleza, en la humanidad … ni en la buena música. Porque eso, la solidaridad, debe ser siempre una fiesta. Y una fiesta sin música es como tener el cigarro, pero no el encendedor. ¿Cómo te prendes, pues?”.

Se va el Riko rumbo al puesto de tamales. La ñora le dice “¿Qué pasó ése mi Riko? ¿Va a querer de chivo los tamales?” y sonríe con picardía. El Riko aguanta el golpe y pide dos champurrados.

author: By Darren Thompson, Contributor
title: Mining in the Sacred and Stolen Black Hills, Then and Now
content:
The colonization of the Black Hills by the U.S. government is one of the most well-known land thefts in American history. Since gold was discovered in the sacred lands of Paha Sapa or Ȟe Sápa, also known as the Black Hills, more than 150 years of tragedy, land exploitation, and legal issues followed and continue to this day.


When rumors began to spread in the 19th century that gold was found in the Black Hills, U.S. Army General George Armstrong Custer led a 1,000 man expedition in 1874 to find out for himself. When the discovery became public, thousands rushed to the Black Hills — trespassing on Indian Territory — to also find out for themselves.


The Black Hills were then a part of the Great Sioux Reservation and belonged to the Great Sioux Nation as promised in the Fort Laramie Treaty of 1868 which reserved lands for the exclusive use and occupation by the Great Sioux Nation, including the Black Hills. Any cession of any part of the reservation required a new treaty executed and signed by at least three-fourths of all adult male Indians occupying the land.


One of the provisions of the 1868 Treaty was that white men were forbidden from stepping foot on the reservation, except for officials of the U.S. government. 


The discovery of gold led to thousands of white men trespassing in the Black Hills with the U.S. government rushing to colonize the area and take ownership.


Map of a reconnaissance of the Black Hills, July and August, 1874, with troops under command of Lt. Col. G.A. Custer, 7th Cavalry

via

 Library of Congress.


The Lakota — also known as the Great Sioux Nation — and the Cheyenne refused to cede ownership, resulting in many confrontations which ultimately culminated in the Battle of the Little Bighorn (also called Custer’s Last Stand and the

Battle of the Greasy Grass

).


On June 25-26, 1876, the U.S. Army’s 7th Cavalry — led by Gen. George Custer — was completely defeated by an encampment of thousands of Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho people along the Little Bighorn River in Montana.


Painting of the Battle of the Greasy Grass or Little Bighorn by

Martin Pate

 exhibited in Journey Museum in Rapid City.


After the U.S. defeat at the Battle of the Little Bighorn, Congress responded by cutting off all rations for the Sioux until all hostiles were terminated or imprisoned and the tribe would cede the Black Hills to the U.S.


The Indian Appropriations Act of 1876, enacted on August 15 of that year, was aimed at acquiring the Black Hills by sale or otherwise starve the people. In 1877, a new treaty was presented by a commission headed by George Manypenny, and some signed the treaty under the threat of starvation, with the Black Hills being taken.


“In any first-year contracts course, we teach that a valid agreement requires mutual assent (an agreement by all parties),” Danielle Finn told Unicorn Riot. Finn is Standing Rock Sioux tribal citizen and professor of Lakota Law at William S. Boyd School of Law at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas.


“What the Manypenny Commission presented to the Sioux in 1876 fails that test categorically,” Finn said, “the Fort Laramie Treaty — a binding instrument under the Supremacy Clause — required the signatures of three-fourths of all adult male Sioux to cede any portion of their reservation. The ‘agreement’ that was actually presented to the Sioux was signed by only 10% of the adult male Sioux population. No legitimate legal system would call that consent. The Supreme Court didn’t either.”


The taking of the Black Hills has been challenged several times in federal court by the tribes ultimately resulting in a Supreme Court decision that ruled in favor of the tribes’ claim.


Justice Harry Blackmun delivered the Supreme Court’s opinion in 1980,

United States v. Sioux Nation of Indians

, and wrote that the tribes were never fairly compensated for the taking of the Black Hills and that they should be. The tribes were entitled to an award of at least $17.5 million, without interest, as damages under the Indian Claims Commission Act of 1946.


“What all people must understand is that the Supreme Court’s holding here was not a gesture of sympathy, it was a constitutional determination,” Finn said. “When the Court confirmed that the 1877 Act constituted a ‘taking’ under the First Amendment, it was applying the same Takings Clause that protects any American property owner from government seizure without just compensation.”

title: Sincan’dan notlar: LGBTİ+ operasyonu tutukluları ve dayanışmanın politikası
content:
Bugün Sincan Cezaevi’ndeydim. “Ailem Güvende” adı verilen operasyon kapsamında tutuklanan sekiz arkadaşımızı ziyaret ettim: Janset, Umut, Metin, Baran, Tuğba, Nedime, Burçin ve Selin.


Bazılarıyla uzun zamandır tanışıyorum. Bazılarını ise sadece isimlerinden, politik mücadelelerinden biliyorum. Eylül’ün 12-13’ündeki baskın ve gözaltı sürecinde elimden geldiğince yanlarında olmaya çalıştım. Ardından bir süre Ankara dışında olduğum için ziyaretlerine gidemedim. Bugün, tutuklanmalarından sonra ilk kez bir araya geldik.


Cezaevi ziyareti muhalefet milletvekillerinin, bilhassa bizim partinin bir rutini. Son zamanlardaki gelişmeler sanırım CHP ve Yeni Parti’nin de çok daha sık cezaevi yollarına düşmesini getirdi. Ben de üç buçuk yıllık milletvekilliğim boyunca Sincan’a özellikle çok sık gittim. Kobani duruşmalarının sürdüğü dönemde bir ayağım neredeyse hep oradaydı. O davadan tutuklanan arkadaşlarımızı, Gezi tutuklularını, farklı siyasi davalardan içeride bulunanları fırsat buldukça ziyaret etmeyi sürdürüyorum. Bakırköy, Silivri, Diyarbakır, Edirne, Erzincan, Kandıra, Sincan… Gidebildiğim cezaevleri.


Her cezaevi başka bir dünya. Gezi tutuklularının deneyimi başka, Kobani davasından tutuklananlarınki başka, LGBTİ+’larınki bambaşka. Bu dünyaları birbirine benzetmek, aralarındaki farkları silmek olur. Ama her birinde insanın özgürlüğüyle, onuruyla, bedeniyle ve hayatını kurma hakkıyla ilgili ortak bir mesele var.


Cezaevleri, dışarıdaki hayatın bir süreliğine paranteze alındığı yerler değil yalnızca. Aynı zamanda dışarıdaki eşitsizliklerin, ayrımcılıkların ve iktidar ilişkilerinin içeride başka biçimlerde yeniden üretildiği mekânlar. Üstelik kapılar kapandığında, içeride yaşananların dışarıda duyulması da giderek zorlaşıyor.


Bu nedenle siyasetçilerin, milletvekillerinin ve hak savunucularının cezaevlerini sessiz bırakmaması gerekiyor. Avukatların ve ailelerin kurduğu dayanışma elbette vazgeçilmez. Fakat dışarıdan kurulan bağların da sürmesi, içeride yaşananların gündeme taşınması, insanların yalnızca dosyalarından ibaret olmadıklarının hatırlanması gerekiyor. Siyasetçilerin bir gözünün ve bir kulağının orada olması gerekiyor. Bir ayağının orada olması gerekiyor.


Bugün sekiz kişiyle görüştüm. Sabahtan akşam mesai bitinceye dek. İçeri girerken bıraktığım Ankara, çıktığımda puslu neredeyse kar havası diyeceğim bir havaya ve yağmura teslim olmuştu. Belki de ne kadar isterlerdi o havada dışarıda olmayı, yağmurda ıslanmayı, hatta üşümeyi... Şehre bir buçuk saatte dönebildik. Sekiz ayrı hayat, sekiz ayrı hikâye. Zaman zaman güldük, zaman zaman ağır şeyler konuştuk. Her birinin kendi koşulları, kendi ruh hâli, kendi direnme biçimi var. Ama ziyaretlerin sonunda aklımda kalan, yalnızca kendilerine yapılanları anlatmaları değildi. Kendi bildik hayatları tümden ellerinden alındığında bile başkalarının hayatlarına bakmaya devam etmeleriydi.


Belki de bugün en çok bunu düşündüm.


Janset’in söylediği bir şey var. Bunları öğrenmemiz için onları ziyarete gitmemiz gerekmiyor.


Haklıydı. Hak ihlallerini, ayrımcılığı, yoksulluğu ve cezaevlerinin koşullarını öğrenmek için bunları yaşayan insanların bunu anlatmasını beklememeliyiz. Birilerinin yaşadıklarını bize anlatmak zorunda kalmadığı bir politik duyarlılık geliştirebilmeliyiz. Ne var ki çoğu zaman, bildiğimizi sandığımız şeylerin gerçek anlamını, karşımızda bir insan oturduğunda, onun hikâyesini dinlediğimizde kavrıyoruz.


İlk Janset’le görüştüm


Janset’i Ankara’daki çeşitli panellerden, toplantılardan tanıyorum. Aramızda bir dayanışma hukuku olduğunu sanıyorum. Bana bir dostum, arkadaşımmış gibi geliyor. Söylediklerinde kişisel bir sitemden çok, son derece açık bir politik itiraz vardı. Siyasetçilerin LGBTİ+’larla dayanışma konusundaki çekingenliğine dikkat çekti. Sözü dolandırmadan söyledi: Siyasetçi linci göze alacak. Cesareti yoksa da "mış gibi", dayanışıyormuş gibi yapmayacak.


Bu sözün üzerinde durmak gerek.


Siyaset, herkesin zaten rahatlıkla söyleyebildiği şeyleri tekrar etmekten ibaret değil. Başkalarının dile getirmekte zorlandığı sözleri de dile getirmek gibi bir sorumluluğunuz var. Bunun bir bedeli olabilir. Hedef gösterilebilirsiniz, linç edilebilirsiniz, hiç hak etmediğiniz saldırılara maruz kalabilirsiniz. Ama siyasetçinin meselesi, kendisini bu ihtimallerden korumak olamaz.


Ben de lincin zaten hep orada tetikte beklediğini söyledim. Kadın voleybolculara destek amacıyla attığım bir tweetin günlerce süren bir linç kampanyasına dönüşebildiğini anlattım. Yıllar …

content:
20 октября, 20:00, Auditoria Booksbar 22–26 S. Janashia St. eng + перевод основных тезисов лекции

Журнал Эгалите приглашает вас на лекцию профессора Аллана Антлиффа, посвященную историческому исследованию того, как анархизм трансформировал эстетические практики в литературе, поэзии, музыке и изобразительном искусстве после Второй мировой войны.

title: Eskişehir’de İklim Adaleti Forumu: “İklim adaleti mücadelesi sınıfsal temelde ele alınmalı”
content:
Eskişehir Ekoloji Derneği tarafından Taşbaşı Kültür Merkezi’nde İklim Adaleti Forumu düzenlendi. İklim krizinin sınıfsal boyutunun, emisyon ticaret sisteminin, madencilik faaliyetlerinin ve uluslararası iklim politikalarının ele alındığı forumda, ekoloji mücadelesinin emek ve yaşam hakkı mücadelesiyle birleştirilmesi gerektiği vurgulandı.

Forumda avukat Mert Yedek ve avukat Onat Öncü’nün yanı sıra Eskişehir-Bilecik Tabip Odası Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Murat Erol, TMMOB Makina Mühendisleri Odası Eskişehir Şubesi adına Mustafa Haydar Tiftikçi, İYİP Odunpazarı İlçe Başkanı Gürol Yer, Çiftçi-Sen Yönetim Kurulu Üyesi Hasan Cengiz Yazar, Emek Partisi Eskişehir İl Örgütü adına Şevval Duran, ziraat yüksek mühendisi Zevaiddin Özcan, Tüm Emeklilerin Sendikası Eskişehir Şubesi Yürütme Kurulu Üyesi Alim Yıldızkan, Eskişehir Gıda Topluluğundan Emin İrfan Akkaya, Türkiye Ormancılar Derneği Eskişehir Temsilcisi Deniz Hakan Durmuş, Eskişehir Barosu Kent ve Çevre Komisyonu Başkanı Ecir Ayaş ve akademisyen Ozan Devrim Yay söz aldı.

Avukat Mert Yedek, iklim krizinin sonuçlarının toplumun bütün kesimlerini aynı biçimde etkilemediğine dikkat çekerek iklim adaleti mücadelesinin sınıfsal bir perspektifle ele alınması gerektiğini söyledi. Aşırı yağışlar, sel ve taşkınlar gibi iklim krizinin sonuçlarından en fazla emekçilerin ve yoksulların etkilendiğini belirten Yedek, sermaye sahiplerinin ise sahip oldukları ekonomik olanaklarla kendilerini bu sonuçlardan kısmen koruyabildiğini ifade etti.

Yedek, “Bir avuç, yüzde 1’e tekabül edecek sermayedarlar bir şekilde buradan kendi birikimleri ve servet birikimleriyle birlikte kendilerine sürdürülebilir bir yaşamı var edebiliyorlar. Ama adalet kısmı burada açığa çıkıyor” sözleriyle iklim krizinin yarattığı eşitsizliğe dikkat çekti. Krizin sorumluluğunun ve sonuçlarının toplumun farklı kesimleri arasında eşit dağılmadığını vurgulayan Yedek, iklim adaleti tartışmasının yalnızca çevresel etkilerle sınırlı tutulamayacağını belirtti.

İklim krizi karşısında bireysel tüketim alışkanlıklarının değiştirilmesinin çözüm olarak sunulmasını da eleştiren Yedek, su tüketimini azaltmak, toplu taşıma kullanmak ve bireysel karbon ayak izini düşürmek gibi önerilerin büyük şirketlerin ve üretim faaliyetlerinin sorumluluğunu geri plana ittiğini söyledi. Bireysel önlemlerin öneminin, üretim ilişkileri ve sermayenin doğa üzerindeki etkisi tartışılmadan ele alınamayacağını belirten Yedek, iklim krizinin yapısal nedenlerine odaklanılması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Yeşil dönüşüm ve net sıfır emisyon hedefleri kapsamında gündeme getirilen emisyon ticaret sistemini de değerlendiren Yedek, karbon salımının alınıp satılabilen ekonomik bir değere dönüştürülmesine karşı çıktı. Karbon salımının piyasa mekanizmaları üzerinden düzenlenmesinin iklim krizini ortadan kaldırmaya yetmeyeceğini belirten Yedek, “Karbon devredilebilir, ücretlendirilebilir, ekonomik bir değer verilebilir ve tahsis edilebilen bir meta hâline getirildi” dedi.

Yedek, emisyonların ticarete konu edilmesinin iklim krizinin çözümünü piyasanın işleyişine bağladığını belirterek, “Bizim tartıştığımız bu makro iklim krizi dediğimiz ve herkesin yakıcı bir şekilde hissettiği durumu önleyebilmesi ne yazık ki mümkün değil” ifadelerini kullandı. İklim politikalarının şirketlerin kârlarını ve piyasa ilişkilerini korumak yerine emisyonların azaltılmasını ve ekolojik yıkımın önlenmesini esas alması gerektiğini vurguladı.

Yedek, yeşil dönüşüm politikalarının yalnızca yenilenebilir enerji yatırımları üzerinden değerlendirilmesine karşı çıkarak bu dönüşüm için gerekli görülen madenlerin hangi amaçlarla kullanıldığının da sorgulanması gerektiğini söyledi. Nadir toprak elementlerinin yalnızca enerji teknolojilerinde değil, savunma sanayisi ve silah teknolojilerinde de kullanıldığına dikkat çeken Yedek, bu kaynaklar üzerindeki rekabetin uluslararası güç mücadeleleriyle bağlantısına işaret etti.

Türkiye’de madencilik faaliyetleri ve acele kamulaştırma kararlarının yerel halkın yaşamı üzerindeki etkilerine değinen Yedek, Eskişehir’de nadir toprak elementlerinin çıkarılmasına yönelik girişimlerin de bölge halkının üretimini ve geleceğini doğrudan ilgilendirdiğini belirtti. Yıllardır işledikleri topraklardan geçimini sağlayan köylülerin, yaşamlarını etkileyecek kararların alınmasında yeterince söz sahibi olmadığını ifade etti.

Üreticilerin yaptıkları harcamalar, ektikleri ürünler ve gelecek dönem için kurdukları ekonomik planların bu süreçlerde belirsizliğe sürüklendiğini belirten …

title: Accordi libertari
content:
Accordi libertari: grande partecipazione alla prima edizione del Canto Anarchico a Massenzatico, 2-3-4 ottobre 2026


Si è conclusa domenica sera la prima edizione del festival del canto anarchico tenutasi alle Cucine del Popolo di Massenzatico (RE). Sono stati tre giorni intensi di conferenze, presentazioni di libri, concerti dal vivo con cantautori, band e cori, allietati dal buon cibo e dall’immancabile lambrusco, che hanno registrato la partecipazione complessiva di oltre 600 persone. Venerdì sera abbiamo aperto ricordando Francesco Guccini, come uomo e come artista, mettendo l’accento sulla Locomotiva, indimenticabile brano con cui è stato anche concluso il concerto finale della Ciurma del Galeone di domenica. Prima di ascoltare i 100 canti anarchici di Alessio Lega, è stata abbozzata da Enri Volta una proposta interpretativa e di studio del canto anarchico oggi. Sabato poi è stata presentata la mostra discografica, con Lp e 7” originali dagli anni ’70 ad oggi sul tema, e Franco Schirone ha presentato il fondamentale libro sul canto anarchico in Italia, giunto ormai alla terza edizione e scritto insieme a Santo Catanuto. Le presentazioni sono poi proseguite con gli approfondimenti di Claudio Piccoli e Tiziana Oppizzi sulla rivista Il Cantastorie di Vezzani e quello di Alessia Masini sul rapporto tra musica e politica nel punk, a cavallo tra gli anni ’70 e ’80. Tra il pomeriggio e la sera si sono esibiti Mars on pluto, Francesco Pelosi e Riccardo Dodi, che ci hanno fatto cantare a pugno chiuso il vasto repertorio che va dagli Arditi del popolo alla Resistenza passando per la Spagna del 1936 e non solo. La serata si è poi chiusa con lo scatenato dj set di Naon Grrrl che ci ha fatto ballare a suon di post punk. La giornata conclusiva di domenica si è aperta con le presentazioni dei libri “Cantare la piazza” sui cantastorie, e “Pino Pinelli un racconto musicale”, che raccoglie i canti per Pino e sulla Strage di Piazza Fontana. Nel pomeriggio Marco Fincardi ha ripercorso le evoluzioni delle serenate alla rovescia raccolte nel suo volume “Derisioni notturne”. La musica dal vivo è poi proseguita con i Cantografi, Donato Landini e Roberto Ruberti, che hanno interpretato rispettivamente l’ampio repertorio libertario sia popolare che d’autore, le canzoni per Giovanni Marini e Franco Serantini e i brani scritti da sua madre Paola Nicolazzi. C’è stata poi un’incursione rap, rigorosamente legato al dialetto reggiano, con La Kattiveria, e la serata si è conclusa con i Quarto Podere e il finalone con tutta la ciurma del Galeone. Ad ogni pasto poi si è esibito un coro. L’amata Rossa, Stazione Rossa, i Malfattori, Oltrecoro e i Violenti Piovaschi hanno intonato canti di lotta e resistenza da tutti i continenti. Un grande ringraziamento va a coloro che hanno reso possibile questo evento tramite il loro lavoro volontario e a tutte le persone che sono venute da ogni dove per partecipare. Un buon primo passo quindi, per continuare con “lo sguardo rivolto all’aurora”, oltre che alla prossima edizione!


Il comitato organizzatore


Reggio Emilia 5/10/2026


DISCORSO INAUGURALE


Subito dopo la “Locomotiva” direi che la miglior citazione di Guccini sugli anarchici si trova in “Canzone di Notte N.2”, quando li definisce come “gente che finisce male: o in galera od ospedale…” – di questi tempi ancora attualissima. Da qui forse si può partire per inaugurare questo festival della canzone anarchica. In questa introduzione proporrò un po’ di ragionamenti: abbozzati, magari provocatori, spero non sterili né deliranti. Beh, innanzitutto parlando di canto anarchico possiamo partire dicendo che esiste ancora. Il fatto che sia esistito non significa che per forza continui ad esistere, per esempio i canti repubblicani esistevano, ma non mi pare che oggi godano di buona salute… Oppure movimenti e realtà politiche non per forza lasciano una produzione canora. Come se guardiamo al movimento anarchico degli anni ’50 del Novecento in Italia, c’è un vuoto: cioè gli anarchici c’erano ma c’è poco o nulla a livello di canti. Anche queste carenze vanno interrogati. Se volessimo categorizzare per forza, – ammesso che sia lecito in ambito anarchico – ma almeno quando è utile credo sia giusto categorizzare, credo che il canto anarchico si possa dividere in: 1) canti DEGLI anarchici (scritti da anarchici, es. quelli di Pietro Gori); 2) canzoni SUGLI anarchici (canzoni che raccontano le loro vite e/o lotte, non per forza – soprattutto in tempi recenti – scritte …

author: Unknown
title: Il terreno sta cedendo? Lo yen, il dollaro e l’autunno caldo in Francia
content:
Pubblichiamo la traduzione di questo interessante articolo di Andrée Dima apparso su

Realité

 il 14 ottobre 2026


in vista della giornata di mobilitazione del 17 ottobre in Francia.


Diciotto mesi fa, dopo la pubblicazione del nostro primo articolo, “

Su un terreno instabile”

, abbiamo ricevuto numerosi commenti da parte di lettori tanto benevoli quanto perplessi: che farsene di queste analisi e, in fin dei conti, a che pro tutto questo arrovellarsi il cervello? Nella prospettiva di un autunno di lotte sociali, vorremmo mostrare, in maniera più concreta, i legami tra congiuntura monetaria e lotta di classe e, soprattutto, che cosa cambi per chi intende intervenire nel movimento reale.


Da una trentina d’anni, i paesi ricchi vivono a ritmo di credito a basso costo, e gli Stati Uniti, la Gran Bretagna e la Francia hanno potuto mascherare, attraverso il debito, lo smantellamento della propria industria nazionale. È questo il contesto che ha plasmato le forme assunte dalle lotte e i «compromessi sociali» che ne sono nati; è questo il contesto nel quale ci siamo formati, abbiamo compiuto la nostra formazione politica e, forse, nel quale abbiamo acquisito delle cattive abitudini. La situazione sta tuttavia cambiando, e il 17 ottobre potrebbe assumere una portata ben diversa rispetto ai movimenti sociali ai quali ci siamo abituati, gilet gialli compresi: la posta in gioco non è più costringere il governo a fare marcia indietro su una legge o un provvedimento, ma mettere la borghesia francese con le spalle al muro, imponendole un’alternativa: la fine della guerra a Est oppure il sacrificio dell’euro. Due prospettive la cui portata supera di gran lunga i confini nazionali e che mettono in gioco gli equilibri mondiali. A condizione, però, che il movimento sia consapevole di ciò che ha tra le mani. 


Per rendere tutto questo più tangibile, occorre ripartire da una sequenza iniziata quest’estate, con un avvenimento apparentemente lontano, quasi esotico: nella torpida calura del mese di agosto, la Banca centrale del Giappone ha annunciato un’operazione congiunta con il Dipartimento del Tesoro statunitense, volta ad arginare la svalutazione della propria valuta, lo yen. Se vale la pena soffermarsi su questa iniziativa, è perché si trattava di un’operazione alquanto borderline. Innanzitutto, per il metodo adottato: in una situazione del genere, la prima reazione di una banca centrale sarebbe, in linea di principio, quella di aumentare i propri tassi di riferimento (che determinano gli altri tassi d’interesse). Poiché in Giappone questi figurano tra i più bassi al mondo, la banca centrale dovrebbe

apparentemente

 disporre di ampi margini di manovra, ma il problema è che un intervento del genere avrebbe avuto conseguenze spiacevoli

anche

 per il mercato del debito pubblico statunitense, e non solo. L’economia giapponese sta emergendo da trent’anni di deflazione, e i tassi d’interesse vi rimangono strutturalmente più bassi che altrove. Siccome il denaro costa poco, gli speculatori si indebitano in yen, per poi convertirli e investirli in titoli più remunerativi, come i buoni del Tesoro statunitensi. È un’operazione nota come

carry


trade

, che contribuisce a indebolire il valore dello yen e, allo stesso tempo, ad alimentare la domanda di debito pubblico americano. Lo yen a buon mercato funziona come una macchina per fare soldi, non soltanto per gli speculatori, ma anche per lo Stato americano: basta però che Tokyo aumenti i propri tassi perché questo meccanismo che alimenta il debito pubblico statunitense rischi di incepparsi.


Per evitare di arrivare a tanto, l’adorabile Scott Bessent, segretario al Tesoro americano, si è dunque offerto generosamente di dare una mano: anziché aumentare i tassi d’interesse, la Banca del Giappone avrebbe potuto riacquistare la propria valuta, riducendone la quantità in circolazione e facendone così risalire il valore. E per evitare che il Giappone finanziasse l’operazione vendendo titoli del Tesoro americano, Washington avrebbe potuto persino farsene carico al suo posto, magari vendendo euro per coprire i costi. Il tutto per qualche centinaio di miliardi di dollari. Questa mossa ha lasciato di stucco gli osservatori. Segnala infatti che il mercato del debito americano, il più profondo e liquido del mondo, non è più in grado di assorbire uno shock dell’ordine di un centinaio di miliardi di dollari senza subire un aumento immediato, doloroso e intollerabile dei tassi d’interesse sul …

author: Radikal Perspektif
title: Yabancılaşma
content:
Yazan: David Graeber


Çeviren: Gorthim


Çevirilen Asıl Metin


PDF Linki


Yabancılaşma kavramı oldukça sıra dışı bir kavramdır; zira bu kavram, bir yandan yaygın bir duyguyu —çok öznel, bir bakıma tanımlanamaz bir duyguyu— açıklamaya yönelik bir girişim, diğer yandan da bu duyguyu düzenli olarak üreten her türlü toplumun doğasına yönelik bir eleştiri niteliğindedir.


Bu her zaman böyle değildi. Kişinin dünyada kendini evinde hissetmemesi, çevresinden, kendinden ve diğer insanlardan yabancılaşma hissi, tarih kadar eski gibi görünmektedir; çoğu dünya dininde (Budizm, Hristiyanlığın çoğu mezhebi ve Taoizm, İslam’daki Sufi akımları) bu duygu, esas olarak insanlık durumunun gerçeğine dair derin bir içgörüyü yansıttığı şeklinde değerlendirilirdi. Keşişler, rahipler ve meditasyon yapanlar, daha yüce bir şeye ulaşmanın bir yolu olarak yabancılaşma duygularını sıklıkla aktif bir şekilde değer vermiş veya beslemişlerdir. Kalvinizm, izolasyon ve boşluk duygularını insanlığın lütuftan düşüşünün bir işareti olarak görerek modern kavrayışa daha çok yaklaşmış olsa da, bu terimin modern anlamı aslında ancak on dokuzuncu yüzyılda ortaya çıkmıştır. Bu kavrayış, geniş, kişiliksiz, endüstriyel bir şehirde yaşama deneyimiyle yakından bağlantılıydı. Yabancılaşma duyguları, özellikle önceki nesillerde melankolinin muhtemel kurbanları olarak görülebilecek kişileri etkilemeye meyilliydi: entelektüeller, sanatçılar ve gençler. Etkileri de hemen hemen aynıydı: depresyon, kaygı, umutsuzluk, intihar.


Modern yabancılaşma literatüründe iki ana akım ayırt edilebilir: Birincisi, deneyimin kendisini modern yaşamın şahsi olmayan, bürokratik doğasının kaçınılmaz (ancak muhtemelen hafifletilebilir) bir sonucu olarak vurgulayan ve bu deneyimi, dünya hakkında daha derin, daha gerçek bir gerçeğe ulaşmak için kullanma yeteneğinin yitirilmesini beraberinde getiren bir akımdır — zira Tanrı’nın ve geleneksel otorite yapılarının ortadan kalkmasıyla birlikte, bu gerçeklerin çoğunun kesin olarak yitirildiği kabul ediliyordu. Diğeri ise, daha eski teolojik geleneklerden yararlanarak, yabancılaşmayı modern (yani kapitalist, endüstriyel) düzenin kendisinin gerçek, gizli doğasının anahtarı olarak görür ve bunun, ancak o düzenin devrilip yerine kökten farklı bir şeyin getirilmesiyle çözülebilecek dayanılmaz bir durum olduğunu ortaya koyar.


İlk gelenek, Alexis de Tocqueville, Émile Durkheim veya Max Weber gibi sosyal düşünürlerde; Fyodor Dostoyevski veya Franz Kafka gibi romancılarda; ve Søren Kierkegaard veya Friedrich Nietzsche gibi filozoflarda görülebilir. Burada yabancılaşma, modernliğin tüm olumlu değerlerinin karanlık yüzüdür; topluluk, hiyerarşi, kutsal gibi önceki tüm anlam kaynaklarından kopmuş olanların deneyimidir. Bu, bireyciliğin yalnızlığa, özgürlüğün köksüzlüğe, eşitlikçiliğin tüm değerlerin yok edilmesine, rasyonalitenin ise demir bir kafese dönüştüğü noktadır.


Muhtemelen bu türdeki en ünlü kavram, Émile Durkheim’ın (1858–1917) anomi kavramıdır. Hem ekonomik yükseliş hem de ekonomik çöküş dönemlerinde intihar oranlarının artma eğiliminde olduğunu gözlemleyen Durkheim, bunun tek nedeninin, hem yükselişlerin hem de çöküşlerin sıradan insanların beklentilerini tamamen altüst etmesi olduğu sonucuna vardı; bu durum, insanların normlardan yoksun bir duruma düşmelerine, hayattan neyi bekleme veya isteme hakkına sahip olduklarını belirleyememelerine ve bunu yapabilecekleri bir zamanı hayal edememelerine yol açıyordu. Bu tür bir analiz, ya modern toplumdaki kamusal yaşamın asla gerçek anlamda yabancılaşmadan başka bir şey olamayacağına dair (sosyal muhafazakarlar tarafından benimsenen) bir varsayım olan boyun eğen bir karamsarlığa ya da yabancılaşmayı bir sapma biçimi ya da uygun entegrasyon eksikliği olarak gören ve politik karar vericilerin ideal olarak bunu hafifletebilmesi, hatta aşabilmesi gerektiğini savunan liberal bir yaklaşıma yol açabilirdi.


Diğer gelenek ise, teolojik kaynaklardan büyük ölçüde yararlanan Georg Wilhelm Friedrich Hegel’e (1770–1831) kadar uzanır. Hegel için “yabancılaşma”, Ruh’un

1

İnsanlık tarihi de aynı öyküyü barındırıyordu: Zihin kendini dünyaya yansıtarak, örneğin Hukuk’u, Sanatı, Bilimi ya da Devleti yaratırdı; daha sonra kendi yarattıklarıyla, kendisine yabancı ve garip gelen bir şey olarak yüzleşirdi; nihayetinde ise bu yabancılaşmış …

author: anonerror
title: Deriva totalitaria y fin de la formalidad democrática
content:
Impulsar estrategias que tengan vocación transformadora es una tarea lenta, y además, en un contexto tan cambiante como el actual es difícil saber con qué escenarios nos vamos a encontrar en los próximos años. Aun así conviene hacer el esfuerzo de mirar más allá de la próxima manifestación o de la última ley aprobada, pues se trataría no tanto de adivinar el futuro como de atisbar los efectos futuros que podrían tener las apuestas que hacemos hoy. Hay algunas tendencias y situaciones cíclicas que nos pueden dar pistas de lo que puede pasar, y también hay experiencias de lucha que podrían aportarnos ideas sobre cómo encararlo. Lo que sigue es un intento de localizar esas tendencias y pretende ser una contribución para tratar de afinar mejor nuestras propuestas.

En sus orígenes, la idea de crisis se refería a un período decisivo en que se producían cambios fundamentales. En los años 70 comenzó una de esas etapas con la crisis de los combustibles fósiles (1973), más tarde, esa misma crisis se ha ido manifestando con otras formas: como la de las puntocom (2000), la financiera (2008), la del Covid (2020), o las regionales como la de la deuda en América Latina (1982), la asiática (1987), la rusa (1998) o la argentina (2001). A pesar de sus distintas formas, éstos periodos son expresiones diversas de una misma crisis de ciclo más largo que puso fin a los llamados Treinta Años Gloriosos, una época de expansión económica sostenida que se dio en muchos países tras la 2ª Guerra Mundial. Este proceso de crecimiento se apoyó en la reconstrucción tras la guerra, la industrialización, el fomento del consumo y las materias primas baratas extraídas por medio del neo-colonialismo, entre otras causas.

En los países de la región noratlántica, la prioridad de los gestores políticos tras la guerra fue mantener la estabilidad y la paz social para no perjudicar a la economía. Con ese propósito los partidos de derechas y los socialdemócratas llegaron a un pacto que algunos han llamado el consenso social liberal (1). Fue un compromiso que definía el espectro de las políticas que se entendían como aceptables. Este marco incluía la adopción de un conjunto de leyes compartidas que diesen imagen de neutralidad al Estado, cierta intervención estatal para dinamizar la economía, algunas ventajas para la población asalariada y excluida en forma de políticas sociales, y el reforzamiento de los canales institucionales para la gestión de la conflictividad social.

Así, vemos como el consenso social liberal ha sido una construcción ideológica propia del período expansivo de la economía. Este marco ideológico ha servido a los gestores estatales para mantener el debate político dentro de unas coordenadas definidas. Sin embargo, la aparición cada vez más frecuente de las crisis hace que este consenso haya llegado a una especie de época otoñal. Cada vez que las élites económicas han percibido que sus beneficios peligraban, las instituciones estatales han mostrado su parcialidad, como pasó en 2008 con los rescates a las empresas y las leyes represivas dirigidas a contener la protesta. A medida que ha ido avanzando la crisis, el Estado se ha ido deshaciendo de sus políticas sociales, al tiempo que los gastos se han ido redirigiendo hacia el control y el militarismo. La forma democrática está dejando paso a la estructura dura del Estado. Al mismo tiempo, y con el objetivo de adaptar a la población a las nuevas necesidades del Capital, se están promoviendo hábitos y formas culturales que mercantilizan todos los aspectos de la vida.

El 15 de marzo de 2020, en plena crisis sanitaria, el gobierno declaró el Estado de Alarma e impuso un confinamiento que duró 100 días. En esos meses se desplegaron fuerzas policiales y militares que ocuparon el territorio, sobre todo en las ciudades. Se promocionó una visión punitiva del mantenimiento de la salud colectiva con el fin de ocultar las miserias de la industria alimentaria y de la institución sanitaria. Como consecuencia aumentaron exponencialmente los casos de detenciones arbitrarias y abusos policiales, especialmente entre los sectores de población que son estigmatizados habitualmente por los medios. La estructura autoritaria del Estado se expresó con la nitidez de una radiografía, asegurándose los beneficios empresariales y manteniendo el orden de forma estricta a costa de aumentar las situaciones de desigualdad.

>Μαγείρεμα της Συν-τροφικής Κουζίνας Αλληλεγγύης / Solidarity Kitchen Cooking


Μετά από τόσα χρόνια κρίσης, οφείλουμε όλοι να αντιληφθούμε ότι

δεν υπάρχουν μαγικές, αυτόματες και μεγάλες λύσεις.

 Σε μια κατάσταση που πολύ μεγάλα κομμάτια του πληθυσμού αντιμετωπίζουν πλέον προβλήματα επιβίωσης, έχουμε δύο ξεκάθαρες επιλογές:

ή θα συνεχίσουμε σε έναν κατήφορο που μόνο σε μεγαλύτερη εκμετάλλευση, εξάρτηση και αλληλοφάγωμα μπορεί να οδηγήσει ή θα παρουμε αποφαση οτι κανένας σωτήρας δεν υπάρχει να μας σώσει: έχουμε μόνο ο ένας τον άλλο και η μία την άλλη.

 Αντιμέτωποι με πολιτικές που έχουν ως σκοπό την διαίρεση, την εκμετάλλευση και την αναζήτηση αποδιομπομαίων τράγων, προτάσσουμε την

αλληλεγγύη και την αλληλοβοήθεια

. Δεν μιλάμε για “φιλανθρωπία” και ελεημοσύνη: μιλάμε για αλληλοϋποστήριξη, για χέρια που απλώνονται για να βοηθήσουν τους άλλους να σηκωθούν χωρίς να ξεχωρίζουν φυλή, φύλο, θρησκεία. Αντιπαλεύουμε την φτώχεια και τον αποκλεισμό με την αλληλεγγύη. Απέναντι σε ένα κράτος και ένα οικονομικό σύστημα που μας θέλει μονους να παλεύουμε κάθε μέρα για την επιβίωση, η κάθε δομή αλληλεγγύης είναι μια σπίθα αντίστασης. Μια τέτοια σπίθα διαλέγουμε να ανάψουμε και εμείς, οργανώνοντας μια ανοιχτή συλλογική κουζίνα στα δυτικά της Θεσσαλονίκης, εκεί που η φτώχεια και η εξαθλίωση είναι κάτι παραπάνω από καθημερινότητα: είναι το μέλλον που μας περιμένει όλους.

Μαγειρεύουμε συλλογικά, τρώμε συλλογικά, αλληλοϋποστηριζόμαστε, δίνουμε το χέρι για να σηκωθούμε όλοι μαζί και οργανώνουμε τις αντιστάσεις μας.


(Το αρχείο μεταφορτώνεται. Παρακαλούμε περιμένετε μέχρι να εμφανιστεί προτού πατήσετε “Αποθήκευση”.)


Κάθε Σάββατο στις 12:00, μαγειρεύουμε συλλογικά στην Λαϊκή Ξηροκρήνης (Πάρκο Λεωφ. Καλλιθέας και Συνταγματάρχου Φρύζη)


Κάθε Δευτέρα συνέλευση στις 20:00 στο Στέκι Μεταναστ(ρι)ών – Βαλαωρίτου 20, 6ος όροφος.


Κανένας/καμία μόνος/η απέναντι στην κρίση.


Το μόνο που έχουμε είναι ο ένας την άλλη, η μία τον άλλο.


Αλληλεγγύη, αυτοοργάνωση, αλληλοβοήθεια, αντίσταση.


Συν-τροφική Κουζίνα Αλληλεγγύης


After so many years of crises,

we all have to realize that there are no magic, instant or grand solutions.

 In this situation, where very large parts of the population are now facing problems with surviving, we have two clear options:

either we will continue in a downward spiral that can only lead to greater exploitation, dependence and strife, or we will have to understand that there is no savior for us : we only have each other.

 In the face of government policies that divide, hurt, exploit and search for scapegoats to blame, we unite for active solidarity and mutual support. Not charity or philanthropy, but hands that pull up one another, not distinguishing between race, gender, religion. We fight poverty and division, by uniting in solidarity. Against a state and an economic system that wants us alone and fighting every day for survival, every solidarity structure is a spark of resistance. Such a spark is the one we are trying to ignite by organizing an open solidarity kitchen at the west part of Thessaloniki, where poverty and misery are more than everyday life: it is the future that awaits us all.

We cook collectively, we eat collectively, we support each other, we give a hand to stand up together and we organize our resistances.


Every Saturday at 12:00, collective cooking at Ksirokrini Open Market (Park at Leoforos Kallitheas and Colonel Frizi)


Every Monday at 20:00, open assembly at Steki Metanast(ri)on, Valaoritou 20 6th Floor.


No one alone in times of crisis


We only have each other


Solidarity, self-organisation, mutual help, resistance

author: Unknown
title: De la révolte à la révolution
content:
Ce qui se passe actuellement en France en terme de révoltes populaires est passionnant et beaucoup de gens dans d'autres pays nous regardent.


Il semblerait qu'il y ait un potentiel révolutionnaire dans cette période.


Comment faire pour que cet élan ne s'essouffle pas, se renforce, se multiplie et s'étende

 

?


Pour que l'État ne puisse pas l'écraser et que les forces contre révolutionnaires, bourgeoises, réformistes ou autoritaires ne puissent pas le récupérer, et confisquer le pouvoir, comme ça a été le cas encore et encore au cours de l'Histoire

 

?


Déjà l'élan de la révolte pousse de plus en plus de gens à manifester, à faire grève, à bloquer, à occuper, à faire des assemblées, à tout faire pour élargir le mouvement et faire converger les forces.


Mais comment faire pour que cet élan tienne dans la durée, se perpétue, et devienne plus offensif et révolutionnaire

 

?


L'idée avancée dans ce texte (et qui n'est pas spécialement originale en vérité) est que pour cela il faudra que les assemblées qui se créent dans le mouvement se saisissent à bras le corps des questions de l'autonomie, de l'auto-organisation, sur notamment ce qui touche à la subsistance quotidienne du peuple révolutionnaire.


Auto-gérer l'auto-défense, par exemple comme les gens qui se sont organisés contre l'

ICE

 aux États Unis


Auto-gérer la nourriture, par exemple en expropriant des supermarchés pour redistribuer la nourriture à celleux qui en ont besoin, en renforçant ou créant des réseaux de récup, en faisant des cantines ou en s'approvisionnant directement auprès de producteurs solidaires de la lutte


Auto-gérer les logements, par l'expropriation, les occupations, la redistribution, le partage, et en repensant comment on se loge, comment on habite, en sortant des carcans individualistes


Auto-gérer les soins, en ouvrant ou intégrant des lieux de soin communautaire, avec des soignants solidaires de la lutte révolutionnaire


Auto-gérer la communication, en faisant nos propres journaux, nos propres radios, nos propres internets (ou en ralliant à notre cause des medias, si tant est qu'ils soient réellement révolutionnaires et qu'ils sachent rester à leur place)


Auto-gérer les enfants et les personnes qui ont besoin de soin spécifiques ou d'assistance, en créant ou en intégrant dans la lutte des lieux dédiés à ça


Et ce ne sont que des pistes pour illustrer le propos, en vérité tout doit se décider entre les gens, en fonction des besoins réels, des capacités, réelles, des situations et des possibilités réelles.


Il faut déserter tout ce qui alimente le Capital et investir tout ce qui alimente le peuple révolutionnaire.


Déserter, ou réorienter les forces vers l'auto-organisation et l'autonomie.


Si on a un travail qui fait sens, qui répond à des besoins réels des gens, pourquoi pas les mettre au service de la révolution, c'est-à-dire au service des gens, et non au service de l'argent et du pouvoir

 

?


On ne peut rien attendre de l'État et du Capital.


On peut tout attendre de l'auto-organisation, de l'entraide, de la solidarité.


On peut tout attendre de la révolution.


Il faut du courage et de l'insoumission (on en a)


Il faut s'organiser, réorganiser la vie, réinventer la manière dont on se lie les uns et les unes aux autres.


Recréer du sens, choisir nos valeurs réelles, se réapproprier nos vies, collectivement, élaborer ensemble de quoi on a réellement besoin et ce qu'on doit faire. Expérimenter, apprendre.


Et ça ne doit pas se faire chacun.e dans son coin.


Si on veut abattre ce système, les forces révolutionnaires doivent s'alimenter (au sens propre comme au figuré) et se relier les un.es aux autres, à l'intérieur de la France, mais aussi à l'international.


On doit décupler nos forces, créer des infrastructures qui permettront au mouvement de tenir, créer des solidarités matérielles et concrètes partout où on peut.


Créer un maillage avec ce qui existe déjà, s'associer là où on peut, dans le but d'avoir une puissance matérielle qui maintient la lutte et la conflictualité.


Coordonner ces puissances matérielles et ces luttes.


C'est en se saisissant de ces enjeux qu'on réussira peut-être à faire ce que tant de gens avant nous n'ont pas réussi à faire, ou pas assez, parce qu'ils se sont fait écraser, trahir, déposséder, par la bourgeoisie, par des élites, par des partis, par des soit disant professionnels de la politique.


On est pas obligé.es de se faire écraser, on est pas obligé.es de se faire …

author: Hassan Alnaser, Mohamed Alagra, Mashair Idris
title: Govt scrambles to solve fuel crisis without clear end in sight, divided on fava bean import ban; Quintet tries to balance competing political initiatives; RSF continues Blue Nile push; Military sets sights on Darfur
content:
Subscribe to our Lens on Sudan newsletter

 here

.


The struggling wartime economy took center stage this week in Sudan with a pair of issues at the heart of daily life.


The first is a fuel crisis that has grown increasingly worse in recent weeks as gas stations have become makeshift campsites and prices have skyrocketed. While the government has projected an outward image of assurance, behind closed doors, the wheels are turning to try to bring fuel to the nine states under military control.


The plan has two axes, sources informed of the discussion told Mada Masr. The first is essentially a triage: tighten fuel allocations and movement to where it is needed. Various government bodies have tried their hand at centralizing authority to better streamline decision-making, but Sudan’s fractured executive apparatus has seen more attempts than results.


The second part of the plan would require solving the issue at its source: bringing in new supplies to offset the non-performing domestic oil sector. For this, Transitional Sovereignty Council chair Abdel Fattah al-Burhan is holding talks with Saudi Arabia. But as an informed TSF source told Mada Masr, the government cannot commit to a timeline to end the crisis until external agreements are finalized and the necessary financial guarantees are in place.


Alongside the fuel crisis, more potential trouble looms on the horizon, and this one is of the government’s own making. At the beginning of October, the Agriculture Ministry announced it would implement a prime ministerial decree banning fava bean imports in order to bolster domestic production and save foreign currency. In the last two weeks, the move has come in for fierce public criticism, which has been mirrored by criticism from the government and traders, sources in both arenas told Mada Masr.


The concern centers on whether a domestic agriculture sector strained by war and the fuel crisis can realistically carry the burden of producing enough supply of the daily food staple. Government sources told Mada Masr that the process in announcing the decision was flawed, and the Cabinet does not have the required data to ensure the ban won’t have disastrous effects. State-level administrative officials and traders chimed in to argue that the timing of the decision hasn’t given farmers enough time to adjust this season’s production plan to bolster supply.


While a source in Prime Minister Kamel Idris’s office projected confidence that the Agriculture Ministry has the necessary data to back up the soundness of the ban, a source in the ministry said that officials are already discussing contingency plans.


The political front this week saw yet another spin on the merry-go-round of political initiatives. The Quintet — which comprises the African Union, the United Nations, the Arab League, the European Union and the Intergovernmental Authority on Development — is trying to carefully engage with all competing political initiatives without endorsing any. This comes amid increasing divides between civilian political groups and the preparatory committee leading the government-sponsored internal dialogue over who gets to set its terms and who gets to participate. Both sides of the divide are trying to influence the AU to gain a leg up.


On the military front, the Rapid Support Forces continued this week to push for greater control of the Blue Nile locality of Wad al-Mahi. The military was able to push the advance back in a counteroffensive on October 9.


On the western front, the military launched airstrikes on RSF positions as it looked to translate its control of North Kordofan into a stronger position in West Kordofan to take the strategic city of Nuhud. Control of Nuhud would open the door to North Darfur, on which they already have their sights set, military sources told Mada Masr.


From within Darfur, the military made strategic gains this week, with the joint forces advancing from their remaining garrisons in the north of the region down into West Darfur, where they seized control of the agriculturally rich area of Bir Keleikil.


***


Burhan takes direct control of oil file amid worsening fuel shortages


Crowded gas station in Khartoum, September 27. Courtesy: Nepta Petroleum CO.LTD via Facebook.


The Sudanese government is scrambling for solutions in the face of a worsening fuel crisis marked by long lines at filling stations and growing concerns over everything from trade to markets to the ongoing planting …

author: Mzi Velapi
title: ‘End hunger, stop climate harm’: protesters take demands to Parliament
content:
About 200 residents and activists marched through the streets of Cape Town on World Food Day, calling for the government to end hunger and stop climate harm. Organised by the Climate Justice Charter Movement (CJCM) and the South African Food Sovereignty Campaign and allied partners, the protesters handed the memorandum to parliament where they called for the adoption of the People’s Sovereignty Act No 1 of 2024, a People’s Sovereignty Policy and an immediate ban on pesticides.


At least 14 to 15 million people in South Africa live below the food poverty line and experience regular food insecurity, while 11,000 children die due to malnutrition every year, and 10-million tonnes of food go to waste every year, according to Unite Against Hunger.


A recent report by the International Panel of Experts on Sustainable Food Systems (IPES-Food) found that nearly 1.4-billion people in the world work in the agrifood sector, including farmworkers. Despite their number and the vital role they play, they are among the most exploited workers in the world.


Speaking to

Elitsha

, Kara Mackay from Women on Farms Project said that women farmworkers bear the brunt of lack of access to food because of the unequal power relations that govern their relationship with farm owners. “The issue of poor wages and the high prices of food is linked to unequal power relations where the farmer is seen as the producer and the farmworkers as merely consumers,” she said.


Retired farmworker, Magrieta Prins from De Doorns said that farmers deny workers the opportunity to grow their own food by controlling their access to water. “Farmworkers do not have land to grow their own food but even in instances where they are allowed to do so, the farmer controls their use of water and in most times just deny them access to water,” Prins said.


A seasonal farmer from Ceres, Charmaine Lynx said that not having access to water impacts on their ability to produce their own food. “The social grants play a crucial role during off season. I have to look after my daughter and family during off season as I share my AllPay grant with them. Some have to resort to recycling as a means to put food on the table for their families,” said Prins.


One of the demands of the protesters is the implementation of the climate emergency social contract, that requires the government and the corporations which promote and profit from fossil fuels, pay the price.


Communities on the coastal areas of the Western Cape are experiencing severe weather that has impacted on their ability to feed their families. Fisher woman from Buffels Baai in the Southern Cape, Sarah Niemand said that the weather patterns have resulted in cold waters and fish migrating away. “For the past two months we struggled to get fish because they are scarce because of the bad weather,” she said.


Addressing the protesters outside of parliament, activist and academic, Vishwas Satgar said that southern Africa is heating at twice the global average rate, pushing the region toward an estimated 3°C of warming as global mitigation targets face severe shortfalls. “We are here to tell this government that we are not going to pay the price for their failure of leadership to prepare this country. Climate signs are telling us that El Niño is coming and the last El Niño resulted in collapsed food systems and pushed the food prices up as a result,” Satgar said.


Responding to the memorandum, Mfuneko Toyana said that the government will announce additional funding to respond to El Niño, when the minister of finance tables the Medium-Term Budget Policy Statement next week.


Satgar responded to this news: “It does not add up, this is the government that is squeezing the working class and the poor in this country. They are driving austerity meaures, and this is just a modest gesture given that the problem is big and El Niño is coming.”
