author: Ali Harb
title: “Democrats for Mike Rogers” PAC Is Funded by Republicans, Records Show
content:
The group has spent more than $4 million in an attempt to defeat Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

Democrats for Mike Rogers, a group that has spent millions of dollars to defeat Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, has received funds from Republican-aligned organizations, campaign finance records show.

Federal Election Commission (FEC) filings, made public on October 16, revealed that TFM, a super PAC that has been running commercials against El-Sayed under the “Democrats for Mike Rogers” name, was funded by two other PACs that back Republican candidates.

GLCF, a pro-Rogers group, gave TFM $50,000, while American Unity PAC, whose stated mission is to promote “Republicans who support LGBT freedom,” transferred $25,000 to the Michigan group.

Other donors include three individuals in Tennessee and one Michigan resident.

The name and place of residence of the Michigan donor — Michael Sandler, of West Bloomfield — matches those of a doctor who was appointed to the Central Michigan University board of trustees in 2017 by then-Gov. Rick Snyder, a Republican.

Friday’s quarterly filings cover up to September 30, offering only a partial picture of TFM’s finances. The group has spent more than $4 million to help defeat El-Sayed, suggesting that most of its donations came after the September 30 deadline and will not be made public until after the election on November 3.

Nonetheless, the records appear to back suspicions from El-Sayed’s supporters against the group that it may be a Republican-led operation trying to manufacture Democratic support for Rogers and paint the progressive Democrat as an extremist.

An X account associated with the group was created after the bruising Democratic primary ended in August, which pitted El-Sayed against pro-Israel Congresswoman Haley Stevens. It quickly amassed thousands of followers.

The Democrats for Mike Rogers account frequently shares and amplifies attacks against El-Sayed, including regularly questioning his medical credentials and painting him as untruthful.

Last week, the group released a TFM-funded ad, featuring several people who are supposedly Black voters in Michigan questioning El-Sayed’s commitment to Michigan and arguing that he cares more about Palestine.

“I think Abdul cares more about the West Bank than west Detroit,” one person says in the commercial — a message that is echoed by two other people.

“I’m a lifelong Democrat, and this year I’m voting for Mike Rogers,” another says.

El-Sayed is supportive of Palestinian rights and says U.S. taxpayer dollars should be spent improving the lives of Americans, not sent overseas to commit war crimes.

Rogers, a former member of Congress, is a staunch supporter of Israel and has pledged to “unconditionally support” what he calls “Israel’s right to defend itself.”

Israel — which leading human rights groups and United Nations investigators say is committing genocide in Gaza — receives at least $3.8 billion in U.S. military support annually.

U.S. support for Israel has become a key point of contention in the Senate race in Michigan.

TFM was established initially as Democrats for Mike Rogers on August 27 but later changed its name at the FEC’s behest because independent expenditure PACs cannot include a candidate’s name without authorization.

State Representative Karen Whitsett, who was elected as a Democrat but has aligned with Republicans for years, is the sole person listed on the TFM’s filings, serving as the group’s treasurer and custodian of records.

In 2020, Democrats in the Michigan House of Representatives censured Whitsett after she met with President Donald Trump and thanked him for promoting hydroxychloroquine, an unproven drug that she said helped with her recovery from COVID-19. Earlier this year, Whitsett announced she would not run for office again due to her faith. “For me, it is impossible to be a faithful follower of Jesus Christ while remaining a member of the Democratic Party as it exists today,” Whitsett said at the time. “I cannot reconcile that platform with Scripture.”

Prior reporting from Drop Site News has also found that several other people publicly associated with Democrats for Mike Rogers, are, in fact, not Democrats.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Washington Post Journalist Hospitalized After Israeli Settler Attack
content:
Netanyahu cast doubt on the journalists’ account of the attack just hours after it happened.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Israeli settlers conducting an assault on Palestinians in the occupied West Bank amid their autumn olive harvest also attacked a U.S. journalist on Friday, sending her to the hospital as she and other journalists were documenting the coordinated violent raid.

Heidi Levine, a veteran photojournalist for The Washington Post, was donning a “press” vest when settlers chased her and a group of other journalists away from the site of the raid on Palestinian families. They knocked her to the ground, stole her phone and cameras, and beat her.

“They just kept kicking me and kicking me, like probably 50 times,” Levine said. Video of the attack shows Levine on the ground being beaten by masked assailants.

Fellow U.S. journalist Jasper Nathaniel said that Levine was being prepared for surgery on Friday morning Eastern Time. Her “injuries are significantly worse than initially thought,” Nathaniel said, adding that she has a cracked rib and may have been stabbed. He also posted a picture of her bloodied hand, which showed that she had multiple stitches in at least one finger.

Nathaniel said that Israeli settlers and soldiers had opened fire with machine guns on Palestinian families attempting to conduct their olive harvest and that at least one Palestinian was shot. Multiple witnesses said Israeli forces arrived on the scene to help protect and enable the settler raid. Journalist Andrey Khrzhanovskiy, who also witnessed the attack, said that the presence of the Israeli soldiers actually emboldened the settlers.

As Nathaniel and Khrzhanovskiy came to Levine’s aid and they ran from the settlers toward the Palestinian medics, video taken by Nathaniel shows a battered Levine saying: “I can’t. Let me die. Let me die.”

The Post’s executive editor, Matt Murray, called for an investigation in response to the attack.

“This morning, a Washington Post photographer, Heidi Levine, was attacked by Israeli settlers while reporting in the West Bank. She was wearing visible markings clearly identifying her as a journalist. While we are relieved that Heidi has received medical care and is safe, we are outraged by this unwarranted attack on a journalist doing her job and urge a thorough investigation and follow-through from authorities.”

Israel is notorious for opening supposed investigations into incidents of settler or soldier violence, and either never finishing the probe or clearing themselves of responsibility.

Indeed, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office already cast doubt on the journalists’ and witnesses’ accounts of the attack.

“The facts surrounding the confrontation near Abu Falah, during which Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine was allegedly assaulted, remain unclear and are under investigation,” Netanyahu’s office said in a statement. “We will not allow disputed incidents to be exploited to demonize the hundreds of thousands of law-abiding Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria.”

Just a day before Levine was attacked, Nathaniel reported that another American, Haytham Taysir, was beaten by settlers in Ramallah.

The attacks come after a report last week found that the U.S. embassy in Israel has purposefully suppressed findings on nine Palestinian Americans who have been killed by Israeli forces and settlers in the West Bank in recent years.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Daron Letts
title: Blasting begins for new Ampere facility in Iqaluit
content:
Iqaluit’s Road to Nowhere is making space for a makerspace.


Manager Cole Tucker, left, and technician Bryce So work on a computer upstairs at Ampere as part of the Computers for Success Nunavut initiative on Thursday. The pair say they look forward to more space in a new facility being designed for the organization. (Photo by Daron Letts)


Tower Arctic Ltd. is preparing to blast rock starting this weekend for Ampere’s proposed Makerspace Economic Development Hub, which would allow the non-profit organization to allow more people to participate in its science and technology focused educational programming. Currently every program has a waitlist.


“We are looking forward to seeing this building come to fruition,” said Kevin Kelly, Ampere’s director of Nunavut operations, in an interview on Thursday.


Ampere provides people of all ages opportunities take part in media and online literacy activities and entrepreneurial skills training.


Programming runs throughout the week, including after school and on evenings and weekends.


Ampere staff also refurbish old laptops for free redistribution across the territory, as part of the organization’s Computers for Success Nunavut initiative.


Ampere has outgrown its current space, said Cole Tucker, the tech program’s manager.


“We’re pretty cramped up here,” Tucker said. “In the new building we’re going to have a lot more space.”


Tucker supervises six staff who fix computers on the second floor. He said he can’t schedule the full team at one time due to the lack of space.


As for what the new structure would look like, that’s in part up to Iqalummiut.


Ampere secured a little over $1 million from the Canadian Northern Economic Development Agency in April to cover design and pre-construction work for a two-storey, 7,200-square-foot building. That’s more than double the size of the organization’s current location at 1412 Sikituuq Crt.


The nonprofit educational organization purchased the plot at 4120 Road to Nowhere from the city back in 2024. The site is located on the southwest corner of the intersection with Imiqtarviminiq Street.


Ampere plans to host one of several community consultations as early as November to ask residents what they’d like to see in the space.


In the meantime, Ampere staff are informally seeking input from individual educators, students, small business owners, policy makers, families and anyone else they cross paths with, to solicit ideas for the new space, said Kent Driscoll, Ampere’s director of advocacy and strategic initiatives.


“We’re going to have the perspective of all members of the community on what they would like to see,” Driscoll said Thursday in an interview.


There is no timeline for the final design and construction of the new building, said Driscoll, adding the organization is still looking for funding.


Once Ampere’s new home is built, the organization will double its staff of 12 mostly full-time positions, Kelly said.


The city issued a public service announcement earlier in the week that advised construction crews will remove a bedrock outcrop at the site from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. starting Friday. The work was scheduled to run until Oct. 26.


The city is asking residents to use caution in the area.

author: Unknown
title: Jineolojî Academy: Jineolojî should be at the heart of social organization
content:
In a message sent to the European Jineolojî Conference, the Jineolojî Academy Board reflected on 11 years of accumulated experience in Jineolojî activities and highlighted the tasks and responsibilities of the new period.


Stating that Jineolojî is rooted in the historical experience of struggle of the Kurdish Women’s Freedom Movement, the board emphasized that its activities should be developed on the basis of building a democratic society and advancing women’s freedom.


Stating that Jineolojî should not be confined to a single committee, the board emphasized that all institutions within the women’s movement should incorporate this perspective into their activities.


“Every individual, institution, organization, and structure working towards social transformation and revolution can achieve their political objectives only through a sound sociological approach,” the message stated.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261016113503_2026-10-16-haelen-avrupa-jineoloji-konferansi-pajk-mesaji_1.mp4


‘Jineolojî should be organized under the umbrella of the Jineolojî Academy’


The message stressed the need for a new organizational model at the current stage of Jineolojî activities, highlighting the importance of transitioning from a committee structure to an academy model. It called for research, education, written studies, and academic activities to be organized under a common umbrella, urging the establishment of “a functional academy model worthy of its role as the science of the women’s revolution.”


The board emphasized the need to distinguish between integrating the Jineolojî perspective into all areas of work and the specific responsibilities of institutions specializing in Jineolojî. Highlighting the importance of coordination and joint planning among institutions, the message stressed the need to prevent confusion over duties and roles.


‘We must reach our own social base’


The message highlighted the significant international impact of Jineolojî activities in Europe, while identifying the failure to sufficiently strengthen ties with women from Kurdistan and the Middle East as one of the main shortcomings. “We must engage in self-criticism regarding our failure to reach and establish a meaningful presence within the social fabric of Kurdistan and the Middle East,” the board stated.


Drawing attention to the changing sociological realities of the Kurdish community living in Europe, the message emphasized that activities should move beyond an approach focused solely on supporting the struggle in Kurdistan. It highlighted the importance of organizing Jineolojî within its own social base and developing solutions to the problems faced by women and society.


‘Defending society must be a priority’


Addressing violence against women, the targeting of young people by prostitution and drug gangs, and the problems arising from nationalist and religious influences on society, the message stressed that Jineolojî activities must develop responses to these challenges.


The board pointed out that educational, research, and camp activities carried out within the framework of Jineolojî should strengthen social organization. “When determining the perspective, model, and planning of Jineolojî activities, the most important task must be to defend and organize society as a collective,” it said.


The message also warned against distorting the concept of Jineolojî by severing it from its historical roots. Emphasizing that Jineolojî is grounded in the experience of the struggle of the Kurdish Women’s Freedom Movement, the board called for the accumulated knowledge and experience to be brought together and further developed through a strategic perspective.

author: Unknown
title: I giovani lo sanno.
content:
Oltre 40 città si sono mobilitate nella giornata di sciopero studentesco di venerdì 16 ottobre. Il tema è chiaro: contro la guerra e contro chi vuole mandarci in guerra. Una guerra che si traduce in crisi sociale e impoverimento a tutti i livelli, la scuola è uno di questi.


Torino, Padova, Bologna, Roma, Cosenza, Campobasso sono solo alcune delle città che hanno visto decine di migliaia di studenti e studentesse manifestare insieme. La Polizia ha risposto con cariche a Bologna e con idranti e lacrimogeni a Torino nel tentativo di reprimere le proteste. Nei giorni scorsi si è scatenata un’ offensiva poliziesca contro le scuole in occupazione senza precedenti, con arresti e fermi all’interno degli istituti scolastici.


La chiarezza riguarda anche gli intenti: non ci potrà essere qualcun altro a decidere al posto dei giovani. Chi oggi è sceso in piazza, uscendo dalla propria scuola occupata, dai licei ai tecnici, ha vissuto passaggi epocali in questa fase storica. Prima una pandemia globale, poi la guerra sempre più vicina. Chiusura di prospettive e assenza di futuro, non solo dal punto di vista della valorizzazione delle proprie capacità ma di un futuro

sostenibile

, nel più profondo senso del termine. Se va così è perché l’assenza di senso complessivo è totale, a partire dalle proprie aule scolastiche. A partire da ben prima dell’istruzione media superiore la perdita completa di un obiettivo comune, del perché si è lì ogni giorno su banchi sporchi e tra quattro mura scrostate, del motivo per il quale bisognerebbe stare a sentire qualcuno che a sua volta – molto spesso e non in tutti i casi – non sa perché si trovi lì, è un processo devastante. Non c’è nessun bisogno che qualcun altro, tendenzialmente adulto e incline a contribuire al fallimento generale, dica come è meglio fare. O come bisogna stare.


Un mondo mediatizzato e ipercollegato permette di vedere che in Francia i ragazzi e le ragazze si sentono esattamente nello stesso modo. Permette un collegamento profondo tra chi si riconosce su delle istanze che hanno un significato politico intrinseco. Distruggere perché non c’è niente di riformabile. Ma anche riconquistare uno spazio in cui esserci, sentirsi collettività, imporsi, nella gioia e nella rabbia.


Il ruolo del mediatico è evidentemente ambivalente e la narrazione dei giornali ha immediatamente assunto un piano banale e becero ossia la caccia “all’incappucciato” che non sarebbe studente (eppure giovane lo è) e che si infiltra nelle scuole o nei cortei per essere “violento”. Fioccano gli inviti di dirigenti (perché la scuola è un’azienda) a isolare i violenti, a tenere fuori gli esterni e a gestire gli infiltrati, il tutto con il supporto delle forze dell’ordine. Eppure, al di là dei titoli e di qualche video sensazionalistico, quel che si è visto oggi nelle piazze in tutta Italia è una gioventù che insieme ha partecipato a cortei con numeri e determinazione significativi. Si è visto la presenza di docenti e personale scolastico solidale. Si è visto che il rifiuto della divisione razzista portata dall’alto non passa tramite il buonismo moralista di sinistra ma dall’essere insieme con un sentire comune.


Sarebbe inutile lanciarsi in immagini evocative che vogliono romanticizzare una realtà che invece porta con sé le sue contraddizioni. Ma la realtà è fatta di dati: una mobilitazione a macchia d’olio si sta diffondendo, scuole che mai avevano occupato prima d’ora oppure che lo avevano fatto per la prima volta con il Blocchiamo Tutto dell’autunno scorso lo hanno rifatto, l’insofferenza si traduce in moto collettivo. Non è poco in un tempo di frammentarietà e individualismo. Non è poco quando il governo italiano si trova a dover affrontare una crisi probabilmente recessiva nell’arco di pochi mesi, non è poco quando anche altri settori sociali decidono di mobilitarsi, come gli autotrasportatori e gli agricoltori.


La coperta è corta e per capire che con i rapporti di forza è possibile anche vincere il passo è breve.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Chuck Schumer Hasn’t Said a Word About Trump’s Attempt to Deport Ilhan Omar
content:
Ethics lawyers say the raid violated the Hatch Act. The Democratic Senate minority leader has been silent.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Days after the Trump administration’s unprecedented raid of Rep. Ilhan Omar’s (D-Minnesota) house just weeks before the midterm elections, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-New York) has not once publicly defended the progressive Democrat against the naked political prosecution.

The Democratic leader — one of the most powerful in the country — has not issued statements to the press or through his social media channels about the Homeland Security Investigations raid on Monday, nor has he done any media appearances to comment on the issue, which critics have described as a five alarm fire for the state of democracy in the U.S.

This is despite the fact that the Trump administration is waging an inter-agency effort to denaturalize and deport Omar, as reports have uncovered this week. The timing of the raid is also unprecedented, coming just 22 days before the midterm elections in which Omar is on the ballot; these elections should be of grave import to Schumer, since they’ll determine whether or not Democrats will have the power to follow through on their pledges to hold Donald Trump accountable for his escalating fascist authoritarianism.

Other top Democrats have spoken out in defense of Omar — but even those statements have been muted in relation to the magnitude of the attacks.

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-New York) and other House Democratic leaders issued a short statement following the raid that called it “deeply disturbing” and said that it “raises serious questions” about the Trump administration’s “weaponization of the federal government.”

The only mention of consequences in the statement, however, is a promise that the Democrats “will deliver full accountability for the rogue abuse of power from the Department of Homeland Security and Department of Justice.” There is no mention of what that “accountability” would entail.

Jeffries also addressed the issue in an interview on MS NOW about the elections. Throughout the 11-minute interview, Jeffries doesn’t bring up the attacks on Omar once — until he’s asked about them at the very end. In that answer, he simply says that the Department of Justice (DOJ) “is going to be held accountable” and rattles off a list of other people that Trump has tried to prosecute, including Republican Federal Reserve Governor Jerome Powell.

The Democratic Party has also been relatively mum. Chair Ken Martin’s statement about the raid was short, simply calling it a “new low for the Trump administration.”

By contrast, it was shorter than the post about the raid by far right former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene, who said that she and Omar are “far apart” on beliefs but called the raid a distraction from real issues like gas and health insurance prices: “People are so sick and tired of the bullshit,” Greene said.

This is despite the fact that Democrats have many avenues to defend Omar. The Washington Post reported on Thursday that Trump administration officials had already tried to search Omar’s immigration records for evidence to take away her citizenship in 2019, but found insufficient evidence to mount a full investigation.

None of the top Democrats’ statements named Trump’s attacks on Omar as openly racist and Islamophobic, despite Trump having called Omar and other Somalis “garbage” for years. Meanwhile, a group of prominent ethics lawyers have said that they believe the actions of the DOJ and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) were actually illegal. The lawyers, including former counsels to the White House, said that the raid was a violation of the Hatch Act because of its timing in relation to the election.

“DOJ and DHS’s decision to instigate this raid at this very moment and for these alleged reasons is unexplainable — except for as a politically motivated use of power to influence the Minnesota congressional election in violation of the Hatch Act,” the lawyers wrote.

Critics say that Schumer’s silence may be explained by the simple fact that he does not ally himself with Omar, despite sharing a party with her. title: Women discuss Jineolojî experiences and the needs of the new period
content:
The European Jineolojî Conference, held in Haelen, the Netherlands, under the slogan “Bi Jineolojî ber bi avakirina jiyana komunal û azad” (With Jineolojî towards building a communal and free life), continued with its first session, titled “Jineolojî: The Science of Building Women’s Identity on the Basis of Freedom.” The session addressed the experiences, achievements, shortcomings, and perspectives for the new period of Jineolojî activities carried out across Europe.


Jineolojî experience in Europe evaluated


The session began with an extensive visual presentation featuring testimonies from women, photographs, short videos, and audio recordings documenting conferences, camps, educational programs, research initiatives, and committee activities organized or attended by European Jineolojî committees over the years.


The presentation, which traced the development of Jineolojî activities in Europe over the past 15 years, highlighted the considerable knowledge and experience accumulated through conferences, educational programs, research, and camps. It emphasized the need to transform these activities into lasting organizational structures, strengthen ties with local women, and make the knowledge produced accessible throughout society.


The visual presentation examined the development of Jineolojî activities in Europe, their achievements, and the challenges encountered. It highlighted how thousands of women living in different countries had come together through conferences, educational programs, research, and camps centered on Jineolojî, creating a shared experience and collective memory.


The presentation noted that the concept of Jineolojî was first introduced in 2008 through Abdullah Öcalan’s book

Sociology of Freedom

. Jineolojî activities subsequently took shape as a committee in the guerrilla-held Medya Defense Zones in 2011 and began developing more systematically from 2013 onwards.


The first Jineolojî Conference, held in Kurdistan in 2015, was described as a significant turning point that helped clarify the direction of the activities. The second conference, held in 2018, was also highlighted as an important milestone in evaluating the accumulated knowledge and experience and identifying the needs of the new period.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261016155657_2026-10-16-haelen-jineoloji-konferasi-kadinlar-jineoloji-deneyimini-tartisti-1.mp4


Activities expanded across Europe


The presentation highlighted the important role played by the first European Jineolojî Conference, held in Cologne in 2014, in the development of Jineolojî activities across Europe. It noted that subsequent conferences in Paris and Stockholm created common platforms for discussion among women living in different countries.


The assessment stated that the conferences were followed by educational programs, seminars, reading groups, and local initiatives. Camps also developed into spaces where women experienced living, producing, making decisions, and learning together. These activities were described as strengthening the connection between knowledge and everyday life and contributing to experiences of communal living.


The visual presentation noted that Jineolojî committees and research groups began emerging in various European countries from 2019 onwards. Activities carried out in Switzerland, Germany, France, England, Italy, Sweden, Norway, Catalonia, the Basque Country, Ireland, and Scotland were said to have generated new experiences and marked significant progress in education, research, and organization.


The main areas of research included women’s history, witch hunts, the history of colonialism, migration experiences, women’s resistance movements, women’s archaeology, mythology, the relationship between women and nature, and local women’s collective memories. These studies aimed to bring renewed visibility to women’s experiences and traditions of resistance that had been rendered invisible throughout history.


Shortcomings and the needs of the new period


Jineolojî Committee members Sarah Marcha and Necîbe Qeredaxî used storytelling to describe the committees’ organizational structures and working methods, their shortcomings, and the needs of the new period.


Necîbe Qeredaxî greeted the delegates and the women who have contributed to Jineolojî activities in every sphere of life, recalling that the work began under difficult circumstances and gradually developed its own cadres.

title: Bayındır: It is time to open the door wide to freedom, peace, and equality
content:
The Democratic Regions Party (DBP) met with civil society organizations and residents in the Tatvan district of Bitlis under the slogan “We are building dialogue for peace with the people.” DBP Co-Chair Keskin Bayındır attended the gatherings.


Speaking during a meeting with representatives of civil society organizations on Friday, Bayındır recalled previous peace processes that had failed to produce results and highlighted the importance of the current Peace and Democratic Society Process.


Stating that the cessation of conflict for the past two years was significant, Bayındır emphasized that resolving the Kurdish question was not simply a matter of laying down arms. He said the Kurdish people’s demands for constitutional recognition and status must also be addressed.


Bayındır described the commission established in parliament as part of the process and efforts to draft a framework law as important but insufficient. He called for the release of political prisoners and legal arrangements that would enable guerrilla fighters and members of the Kurdish diaspora living in Europe to return.


Emphasizing that the process could not advance through statements of goodwill alone, Bayındır said, “The rights and demands of the Kurdish people must be recognized. It is time to open the door wide to freedom, peace, and equality in these lands.”


Bayındır also addressed the economic crisis and social problems, calling for a united struggle for peace, freedom, and equality.


Speaking at a public gathering in the village of Avêtax in Tatvan, Bayındır argued that years of struggle had created the conditions for negotiations and a political resolution. “We are now a force for a resolution,” he said.


Residents who spoke at the gatherings expressed their trust in Kurdish leader Abdullah Öcalan who initiated the current process and called on the government to take the necessary steps for further progress. The DBP’s public gatherings are expected to continue in the villages of Şîrînşas and Siwar.

title: TUHAY-DER in Mardin calls for the release of political prisoners in Turkey
content:
The Association for Solidarity and Cooperation with Families of Prisoners and Convicts (TUHAY-DER) staged a sit-in outside the courthouse in Mardin, calling for the release of political prisoners and concrete steps in the Peace and Democratic Society Process. Under the slogan “Freedom for Prisoners, Hope for Peace,” relatives of political prisoners, representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, and numerous other people gathered for the protest. A banner read: “No Extensions of Imprisonment – Freedom for Political Prisoners.”


Ayşe Bozan, co-chair of TUHAY-DER’s Mardin branch, particularly criticized the practice of keeping political prisoners behind bars even after they have served their sentences. She said that repeatedly denying their release prevented them from returning to a life of freedom. Many relatives, especially mothers, have long been waiting for the prison gates to finally open, she added.


Bozan pointed to the contradiction between the stated efforts to achieve a democratic and peaceful solution to the Kurdish question and the continued repression within the prison system. “While talks focus on strengthening democratic politics and establishing lasting social peace, practices that prevent equal participation in political and social life remain in place,” she noted.


Bozan emphasized that political prisoners must be given the opportunity to participate in the peace process under conditions of freedom. She called for the release of all political prisoners and an end to arbitrary extensions of imprisonment.


“The practices that cast a shadow over the process must be brought to an end, and concrete steps must be taken immediately to pave the way for peace,” Bozan stated.


The demonstration concluded with a sit-in and chants of “Bijî Berxwedana Zindana” (Long live the resistance in the prisons).

author: Unknown
title: Muğla Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ahmet Aras, CHP'den istifa etti
content:
Fotoğraf: Muğla Büyükşehir Belediyesi

Muğla Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ahmet Aras, CHP üyeliğinden ayrılarak görevini bağımsız sürdürme kararı aldığını açıkladı. Aras, “Bir süredir şahsım üzerinden yürütülen siyasi tartışmaların, kentimiz için yaptığımız çalışmaların önüne geçtiğini görüyorum. Bu tartışmaların Muğla’ya ve hemşehrilerimize bir katkı sağlamadığına inanıyorum” dedi.

Bir süredir AKP'ye geçeceğine dair iddialar gündeme gelen Muğla Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ahmet Aras en son bir hafta önce ODA TV'ye yaptığı açıklamada “Kesinlikle hayır. Ne AKP ne de başka bir parti. Bunu defalarca dile getirdim. Yolumuza CHP çatısı altında devam edeceğiz” demişti.

Ahmet Aras'ın açıklamasının tamamı şöyle:

“Sevgili hemşehrilerim, Muğla Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanlığı görevini Cumhuriyet Halk Partisi çatısı altında, sizlerin güveni ve desteğiyle üstlendim. Bu yolda benimle omuz omuza yürüyen, emek veren bütün yol arkadaşlarımın katkısını; birlikte verdiğimiz mücadelenin, kurduğumuz dostlukların ve ortak emeğimizin kıymetini her zaman saygıyla taşıyacağım. Bugün Muğla’mızın gündeminde çözüm bekleyen önemli meseleler, hayata geçirilmeyi bekleyen hizmetler ve geleceğimize yön verecek büyük sorumluluklar bulunuyor. Buna karşın bir süredir şahsım üzerinden yürütülen siyasi tartışmaların, kentimiz için yaptığımız çalışmaların önüne geçtiğini görüyorum. Bu tartışmaların Muğla’ya ve hemşehrilerimize bir katkı sağlamadığına inanıyorum. Bugün itibarıyla Cumhuriyet Halk Partisi üyeliğimden ayrılarak Muğla Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanlığı görevimi bağımsız olarak sürdürme kararı aldım. Kararımın temelinde, Muğla’ya karşı taşıdığım sorumluluğu halkımızın iradesi ve kentimizin ihtiyaçları doğrultusunda sürdürme anlayışı bulunmaktadır. Belediye başkanlığı, ayrım yapmadan herkesin belediye başkanı olmayı gerektirir. Bugüne kadar olduğu gibi bundan sonra da siyasi görüşü, yaşam biçimi veya yaşadığı yer ne olursa olsun her hemşehrimize aynı samimiyetle yaklaşmaya; Muğla’mızın bütün ilçelerine ve mahallelerine adaletle hizmet götürmeye devam edeceğim. Hizmet anlayışımızın ölçüsü değişmeyecek: Güçlü bir altyapı, güvenli ulaşım, korunan doğa, desteklenen üretici, dayanışmayla güçlenen bir toplum ve çocuklarımıza bırakacağımız yaşanabilir bir Muğla için çalışacağız. Merkezi yönetimle, kamu kurumlarıyla, siyasi partilerle, ilçe belediyelerimizle, meslek odalarıyla ve sivil toplum kuruluşlarıyla Muğla’nın yararına olan her konuda iş birliği içinde olacağız. Kentimizin menfaatine yönelik her samimi adıma açık olacak, çözüm üretmek isteyen herkesle ortak bir zeminde buluşacağız. Bu karar, geçmişimizi yok saymak değildir. Birlikte verilen emeğe, kurulan dostluklara ve paylaşılan mücadeleye duyduğum saygı daima devam edecektir. Aynı zamanda bu karar, Muğla’nın bugünü ve geleceği için taşıdığım sorumluluğun bir gereğidir. Bugün aldığım kararda olduğu gibi, yarın üstleneceğim sorumluluklarda da halkımızın güvenini ve rızasını esas alacağım. Muğlalı hemşehrilerimin takdiri ve kentimizin öncelikleri, yoluma yön verecektir. Benim tarafım Muğla’dır. Önceliğim hemşehrilerimizin huzuru, refahı ve kentimizin geleceğidir. Muğla için çalışmaya, halkımızla birlikte yürümeye aynı inanç ve kararlılıkla devam edeceğim. Sevgi ve saygılarımla.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: New Nunavik rehabilitation service to begin with 46 patients
content:
A new service that will give Nunavimmiut access to specialized services that are typically difficult to access in the North is set to begin later this month with 46 patients.


It’s the product of a

partnership

 between the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services, the Constance-Lethbridge Rehabilitation Centre and the Quebec Health Centre-West-of-Montreal University.


“Work on the initiative began in 2022 and involved several years of consultation, co-ordination and planning,” said Maude Parenteau, planning, programming and research officer at the health board, Thursday in an email.


The service, administered by a technologist, will provide help with orthotics, prosthetics and positioning equipment, such as braces, artificial limbs and specialized wheelchairs.


Patients who need this care currently must travel to Montreal.


The technologist plans to visit two communities on the Hudson Bay coast during the week of Oct. 25. Two c

ommunities on the Ungava Bay coast are set to get their initial visit the week of Dec. 7.


Parenteau declined to identify the villages that will receive the service first. She also did not say if the technologist would visit every village.


First visits will focus on assessment, taking measurements and making moulds. Later visits will allow staff to deliver and fit the equipment and make any needed adjustments.


Several sources are funding the service, including Quebec’s health insurance board and the federal Non-Insured Health Benefits Program. Health centres and the regional health board will also cover costs.


Who pays for equipment and services will depend on the type of equipment needed and the patient’s eligibility for coverage.


Some patients with more complex needs may still have to travel to southern Quebec for assessments or procedures that cannot be done locally, Parenteau said.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Indigenous youth stuck in ‘revolving door’ of justice system: StatsCan
content:
A new report from Statistics Canada says Indigenous youth are stuck in a “revolving door” when it comes to repeat offences, which is perpetrated by factors ranging from unrealistic bail restrictions to over-policing.


The paper, published Thursday, also said that the overrepresentation of Indigenous Peoples in the Justice system extends to those younger than 18 and that there were measurable differences when it came to sentencing outcomes in cases involving Indigenous youth versus their white counterparts.


Data was collected between 2016/2017 and 2022/2023. Within that seven-year gap, First Nations, Métis, and Inuit defendants made up approximately 27 per cent of the youth court population, despite only forming eight per cent of minors in Canada overall.


On the other hand, the report found white youth were underrepresented, accounting for only 52 per cent of defendants despite making up 60 per cent of the youth population.


The imbalance was the most prominent in British Columbia and the northern territories, where Indigenous youth accounted for 43 per cent of the youth court population, nearly four times higher than what they make up of the total youth population in that entire region, which is 12 per cent.


They were also overrepresented in the prairie provinces (56 per cent of the youth court population, versus 17 per cent of the total population) and Ontario (13 per cent versus 4 per cent).


First Nations youth are affected the most prominently. Three quarters, or 76 per cent, of youth in the courts were First Nations, while Métis and Inuit were 19 and three per cent, respectively.


There was also an imbalance when it comes to gender, according to the report.


While two-thirds of Indigenous youth accused were boys, girls accounted for the remaining 34 per cent. However, only 22 per cent of white youth were female.


There’s no set answer as to why there’s a dramatic difference in representation, according to the report. However, authors referenced other criminal justice research which has cited factors such as “over-policing, differential charging practices and varying access to diversionary programs and measures,” as being common.


Researchers also found that factors including “differential access to and use of extrajudicial measures [non-court responses to youth crime], variations in police diversion and judicial discretion [

community-based justice and counselling

], and the unequal availability of culturally appropriate, community-based alternatives,” also played into how these cases are then handled before a judge.


Sentencing


According to the report, Indigenous youth were slightly more likely to receive a guilty decision in court, by six per cent.


Additionally, they were also 18 per cent more likely to have their trial stayed. This means the trial would either temporarily or permanently be put on hold.


Indigenous youth were 16 per cent less likely to get a withdrawal, dismissal or discharge compared to white youth.


After receiving a guilty decision, including those which were the result of a guilty plea, Indigenous youth were 100 per cent more likely to receive a custody sentence.


“This disparity persisted even when broken down by all the accused person and case characteristics,” the report noted, such as the seriousness of the charge or the person’s background and previous offences, if they existed.


“Between 2016/2017 and 2022/2023, Indigenous youth with no prior convictions and with at least one prior conviction were more likely to receive a custody sentence than their white counterparts,” the report continued. “The disparity was largest among those with five or more prior convictions (+119 per cent).


“These findings indicate that sentencing outcomes are not fully explained by variations in criminal history alone, suggesting that judicial decision-making involves factors beyond prior record.”


It stated the results also “suggest a compounding effect,” or an accumulation, as “Indigenous youth become more entrenched in the criminal justice system.”


Probation, referred to as “a less restrictive sentencing option than custody” in the report, was a less common result, as Indigenous youth were then 10 per cent less likely to receive it.


Among that group, Inuit youth were the most likely to receive probation, at 72 per cent.

author: Joshua Carroll
title: Israel Badly Burns Young Girl and Kills Her Mother in Airstrike on Gaza Home
content:
A small child has been found sitting alone on a bed engulfed by smoke and flames moments after Israel destroyed her home in Gaza City, leaving her badly burned and killing her mother.


Dramatic footage captured by

Palestinian journalist Ali al-Jaafrawi

 showed him racing to rescue the girl, later identified as Maryam Ahmed Ghanem, from the burning building. Her mother was 33-year-old Reem Asaad Awad.


“I went back to rescue others and to document what happened, but I suffocated and lost consciousness because of the thick smoke. I saw a woman on fire inside the apartment,” he told Al Jazeera Arabic.


Hospital photos of Maryam with extensive burns on her face have led to widespread condemnation of the attacks.


Children’s educator and YouTube star Ms Rachel, a vocal critic of Israel’s genocide in Gaza, questioned why Maryam’s story had not received greater media coverage. 


“The mainstream news is complicit in this genocide as well as everyone who witnesses it and stays silent,” she wrote on social media. 


The strikes killed four people and injured several others,

the Anadolu Agency

 reported, citing a source from Al-Shifa Hospital. It is unclear if the girl had other relatives who were killed or injured. Her father was killed in a seperate attack at the start of the genocide, the New Arab reported. 


Israel says it was targeting a Hamas member but has not provided evidence to substantiate the claim.


The Council on American-Islamic Relations (Cair), a civil rights group, called on US lawmakers to condemn Israel for “burning a Palestinian mother alive while her daughter watched in Gaza.” 


Media reports about the attack have not confirmed the exact cause of the mother’s death. But throughout the genocide in Gaza, Israeli airstrikes have set thousands of buildings and tents alight, burning their inhabitants to death.


In June, an

entire sleeping family of five

 burned to death in their Gaza City home. Last December, Israeli strikes killed five people inside their tents, including two children, in the al-Mawasi displacement camp, a “safe zone” west of Khan Younis. Medical sources at the nearby Kuwaiti Hospital said the bodies of the victims

arrived badly charred

. 


Israel Defense Forces (IDF) soldiers say the military routinely bombs homes knowing

multiple civilians are inside

, while a UN report in June found that Israel

deliberately

kills and tortures Palestinian children. 


The IDF has repeatedly violated a so-called ceasefire agreement signed with Hamas in October 2025, killing at least 1,498 Palestinians and injuring more than 5,000, Gaza health ministry figures show.

author: Unknown
title: AKOM'dan turuncu alarm: “Mecbur kalmadıkça dışarıya çıkmayın”
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi (İBB) Başkanvekili Nuri Aslan, Afet Koordinasyon Merkezi’nde (AKOM) gelişmeler hakkında aldığı bilgileri paylaştığı bir açıklama yaptı.

Salı gününden itibaren teyakkuzda olduklarını ifade eden Aslan, “Dün bakanlarımızla toplantılar yaptık. Bugün de Çevre ve Şehircilik Bakanımız ve İçişleri Bakanımız ile beraber sabahın erken saatlerinden itibaren Ayazağa'daydık. Devletin bütün kurumları eş güdüm içinde çalışıyor. İstanbul Valiliğiyle ve AFAD ile koordineli çalışıyoruz. Bugün meteorolojik verilere göre maalesef yurt genelinde sarı ve turuncu kodlu alarm seviyeleri var. Kocaeli, Adapazarı, Yalova, Bursa civarlarında turuncu kod seviyesine geçildi. Yurdun bazı yerlerinde de sarı kodla önlemler alınmaya çalışılıyor. İstanbul'da cuma günü beklenen hafif sağanak yağışlar, akşam 18.00'den sonra yağışın birazcık daha şiddetlenmesini bekliyoruz. Ancak cumartesi öğlene doğru kuvvetlenme ihtimali çok yüksek. Dolayısıyla İstanbul'da da turuncu alarm seviyesindeyiz” dedi.

“Mecbur kalmadıkça dışarıya çıkmayın” uyarısı yapan Aslan, “Bu akşamdan itibaren, mecbur kalınmadıkça dışarıya çıkılmaması, mecbursanız da kendi aracınızla değil, toplu taşıma araçlarıyla trafiğe çıkmanızı öneriyoruz. İnşallah yaşadığımız bu büyük felaketi bir daha yaşamayız. Tek amacımız var: İstanbul'daki hemşerilerimizin herhangi bir felakette olumsuz etkilenmesini engellemek. Başka bir düşüncemiz yok. Bu tür afetlerde İstanbulluların göstermiş olduğu gayrete, yardımlaşmaya, dayanışmaya teşekkür ediyorum” ifadelerini kullandı.

author: Shireen Akram-Boshar
title: Man Shot by ICE in NYC Last Week Yet to Receive Surgery for Bullet in His Neck
content:
Lawyers for Oscar Belgal have called for his immediate release, citing inadequate care.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

Oscar Belgal, the 28-year-old Dominican man shot by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) in New York City last Thursday, has not received surgery to remove a bullet lodged in his neck for over a week.

Lawyers for Oscar Belgal have called for his immediate release, citing inadequate care.

On Wednesday, the Legal Aid Society, which is representing Belgal, filed a habeas corpus petition decrying ICE’s “flagrant abuses of authority and categorically lawless conduct.”

ICE agents attacked Belgal in Manhattan on October 8 around 4 PM, soon after he picked up his 5-year-old son from school. The Legal Aid Society’s petition describes ICE’s sudden attack, noting that “an anonymous, masked man stormed Oscar’s driverside window with his firearm drawn, followed closely behind by several other masked men also wielding firearms. The men did not identify themselves, show any documents or otherwise communicate with Oscar in any substantive way.” They were all wearing civilian clothing, the report added.

The petition goes on to describe the attack against Belgal, as an ICE agent shot into his car “while his son cowered in the back seat.” ICE agents then “pinned him to the ground” and left him semi-conscious, without aid. Only later, when he woke up in a hospital, did the agents identify themselves as ICE officers.

Days later, the petition explains, the bullet remains lodged in his neck, and Belgal has “experienced a loss of sensation in half of his face, as well as hearing loss in his left ear, and has not received surgery to remove the bullet from his neck.”

Lawyers from the Legal Aid Society said Thursday that ICE has held Belgal in solitary confinement, under 24-hour lockdown. Initially detained in New Jersey, he was moved on October 9 to the Metropolitan Detention Center in Brooklyn – the same jail where former Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro is being held.

Legal Aid Society lawyers said Wednesday that this is “a facility notorious for medical neglect.”

“With a bullet still lodged in his neck and his serious medical needs unmet, every additional day in custody puts him at further risk. The Court must intervene and order his immediate release,” they added.

Belgal’s shooting last week spurred a renewal of protests against ICE in New York City. Protestors demanded an end to ICE’s presence in the city and called for the abolition of the agency. In addition, demonstrators have called for an end to ICE’s use of local parking lots – and for city police commissioner Jessica Tisch to resign. Activists who attended a Manhattan protest that erupted the night of the shooting reported seeing NYPD “helping the ICE vehicles whisk away our neighbors and come in and out of the hospital.”

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

title: Разрушение государства посредством марксизма-аньолизма
content:

Йоахим Брун (Б.): Ленин как-то ответил на вопрос, чем должны заниматься революционеры в нереволюционные времена, мол, им необходимо упражняться в «терпении и теории». Ты же, напротив, сказал, что необходимы терпение и ирония. Не является ли это методом, пусть и в определённых рамках, приспособиться? Как получается, что ты, с одной стороны, омытый всеми водами диалектики враг государства, а, с другой стороны, тебя обхаживают все — от фонда им. Ханнса Зайделя Христианско-Социального Союза вплоть до Вальтера Момпера, настолько, что журнал «Штерн» выставил тебя на обложке выпуска, посвящённого двадцатилетию 68-го года, придворным шутом революции? Ирония возобладала над теорией? Вот так ты устроился?

Йоханнес Аньоли (А.): Почему бы и нет? То, что революционер всегда и повсюду должен ходить с угрюмой мордой, это — застарелая центарльноевропейская традиция, совершенно неподходящая к тому образу, которому должен соответствовать аутентичный революционер. Не обязательно быть иезуитом, якобинцем или большевиком просто потому, что ты собираешься разрушить государство. Настоящий революционер должен всегда сохранять какой-то остаток иронии и самоиронии. Коммунизм важен, но и оссобуко не помешает. То, что я знаком с широким спектром людей, от фонда им. Ганса Зайделя до Момпера, мне не мешает. Контакт с фондом произошёл после приглашения — и это был первый и последний раз, когда мне там были рады; а Вальтер Момпер посещал мои семинары и затем, что вполне относится к человеческой свободе, сделал из моих рассуждений неверные выводы.

Б.: Левым сейчас нужно выступить против нацоналистической склонности немцев к морализаторству и запрета курения. В конце концов, коммунизм — это не о воплощении прекрасного, истинного, хорошего принципа, а об оссобуко для всех. Но меня интересует ирония. Нея является ли она юморным вариантом скепсиса? Я помню, Эккехард Крипендорф (немецкий либертарный политолог, 1934-2018 гг. – liberadio) как-то поздравил тебя в газете «taz» словами: «Аньолисту стукнуло 60». Что ты будешь делать, если встанет вопрос об организации? Ты организуем?

А.: Нет, я не организуем. А в «taz», в общем-то, должно было ещё стоять — и если не стояло, то я это сейчас восполню, что в тот момент, когда марксизм-аньолизм, который я представляю, станет программой какой-либо группы, я тут же, так сказать, выйду из своей собственной теории. Что касается организации, то я, странным образом, всё-таки кое-что создал или помог создать: «Ноябрьское общество» и «Республиканский клуб» (организации, входившие в конце 1960-х в т.н. «Внепарламентскую оппозицию» – liberadio) в Берлине. Все остальные организации, в которых я состоял, всегда выгоняли меня через два-три года.

Б.: Ты даже в СДПГ был самоироничным членом?

А.: Да, и через три или четыре года меня снова исключили. Вступил я в 1957-м году, а в 1961-м я снова был свободен.

Б.: Как ты вообще додумался до того, чтобы стать социал-демократом?

А.: Это было нетрудно. На выборах в Бундестаг в 1957-м Аденауэр получил абсолютное большинство. А мы сидели в Тюбингене и считали, что нужно что-то предпринять против превосходящих сил ХДСГ. Так, в 1957-м я вступил с СДПГ, в 1958-м начались дискуссии о Годесбергской программе, а затем я стал членом рабочей группы в Тюбингене, целью которой была разработка антипрограммы. Тогда мы работали вместе с ССНС, существовал альянс СДПГ-ССНС. В этой группе состояла и ассистентка Эрнста Блоха, переехавшая вместе с ним из Лейпцига в Тюбинген. Мы подали наш проект программы на Годесбергском съезде партии — вместе со всеми другими проектами, включая проект программы Вольфганга Абендрота из г. Марбурга. Я, кстати, был делегатом на съезде в Годесберге. (…)

author: Unknown
title: Calabria: un mese di mobilitazione diffusa per il lavoro e contro il carovita
content:
Ripubblichiamo l’analisi di

Addunati – Lamezia


Scriviamo questo contributo mentre la Calabria è ancora teatro di importanti lotte e momenti di mobilitazione popolare, con lo scopo di comprendere e attraversare, senza alcun pregiudizio, ogni frattura che si apre in questa terra.

Si tratta di una ricostruzione incompleta a causa della durata e della diffusione capillare delle proteste in tutta la regione che ha reso difficile seguire e approfondire tutte le iniziativa di lotta.


Prima ancora delle mobilitazioni degli agricoltori sono stati i tirocinanti di inclusione sociale ad accendere le strade di questo autunno calabrese.

Dopo anni di mobilitazione intensa e costante, di assemblee, presìdi e blocchi stradali, che hanno portato a concorsi e stabilizzazioni, sostenuti dall’USB, il 15 settembre in centinaia sono tornati sotto la Cittadella Regionale per rivendicare risposte concrete sulla loro stabilizzazione e interventi di sostegno al reddito.

Per anni i TIS hanno prestato la propria attività all’interno di Comuni, enti locali, scuole, parchi e altri servizi pubblici, contribuendo concretamente al funzionamento della macchina amministrativa.

Ma oggi centinaia di lavoratrici e lavoratori si trovano senza alcuna prospettiva occupazionale.

Il 22 settembre si sono ritrovati a Lamezia Terme per un corteo che si è fermato davanti all’ingresso della Stazione Centrale dove si sono registrati momenti di tensione con la polizia in assetto antisommossa che ha impedito l’ingresso in stazione.

Il 29 settembre invece sono stati i precari ATA e della cultura a scendere in strada con USB davanti alla Cittadella Regionale, mentre l’1 ottobre un nuovo presidio dei TIS sotto la Prefettura di Catanzaro si è concluso con il blocco del ponte Morandi.

Intanto, con presìdi simultanei agli svincoli autostradali di Pizzo, Rosarno e Firmo e a Crotone e Spezzano Albanese, lunedì 28 settembre prende il via la mobilitazione generale degli agricoltori calabresi.

La protesta degli agricoltori nasce come risposta all’aumento del costo del carburante e al prezzo sottocosto dei prodotti agricoli e ha visto, almeno in un primo momento, un’unità di intenti di tutte le organizzazioni autonome ed indipendenti dei produttori agricoli come Movimento Territorio e Agricoltura, gruppo Agricoltori del Crotonese, Movimento Popolare Nazionale, Associazione Tutela Agricoltori, in netta contrapposizione con le associazioni di categoria, accusate di aver addirittura boicottato le iniziative di lotta.

Dopo poche ore si aggiunge anche il presidio di Davoli Marina caratterizzato da un’importante sostegno popolare.

Nello specifico si protesta per l’aumento del prezzo del gasolio agricolo, arrivato a 1,63 euro al litro al quale viene contrapposto un prezzo sottocosto dei prodotti agricoli come ad esempio il latte – versato per terra in diversi presidi – pagato a 38 centesimi al litro o il grano pagato a 20 centesimi al kg, mentre il prezzo finale del pane arriva addirittura a 3 euro al kg.

Speculazioni che portano dunque ad aumenti sproporzionati lungo la filiera che alla fine vanno a ricadere sul produttore e sul consumatore.

Venerdì 3 ottobre La Base e USB si mobilitano a Cosenza con un partecipato corteo cittadino che segna una prima saldatura tra i movimenti sociali e i movimenti degli agricoltori.

I presìdi restano attivi per diversi giorni mentre per lunedì 5 ottobre viene organizzata una manifestazione alla Cittadella Regionale insieme alle associazioni rappresentative degli autotrasportatori.

Sempre lunedì 5 ottobre, all’alba, gli agricoltori del Movimento Territorio e Agricoltura bloccano gli accessi ai depositi petroliferi di Vibo Valentia, avviando una crisi nel sistema di rifornimento di carburante in Calabria ed innalzando, così, il livello della mobilitazione.

Arrivano così le prime timide reazioni della politica: proprio lunedì 5 ottobre il presidente della Regione Calabria Roberto Occhiuto annuncia lo stanziamento di 15 milioni di euro di contributi alle aziende calabresi, ma questo, così come lo sconto concordato dalle principali aziende petrolifere, non basta a placare gli animi di chi protesta.

Decine di Tir infatti si mettono in marcia a 50 km orari sulla Salerno – Reggio Calabria creando importanti disagi alla circolazione regionale e annunciando uno sciopero a partire dal 16 ottobre.

La scintilla è partita e non bastano annunci dell’ultimo minuto a fermare la rabbia di centinaia di calabresi scesi in strada.

author: Marcelo Oliveira
title: Meta bloqueia conteúdos políticos pró-Lula e contra Flávio acusando terrorismo e nudez
content:
Investigamos o que importa para os brasileiros além do que passa na campanha eleitoral. Leia mais reportagens como essa clicando

aqui

.


Imagine de uma noite para a outra você ficar sem o seu WhatsApp, Instagram e sem seu número de telefone? Foi o que aconteceu com a arquiteta e urbanista Carolina Martins, 43 anos, moradora de Brasília. Ela coordena uma comunidade no WhatsApp de mobilização para “virar voto” em prol da candidatura de Lula.

 A comunidade tem um grupo de bate-papo e ambos foram suspensos pela Meta (dona do WhatsApp, Instagram e Facebook) sob a alegação de “atividade relacionada a organizações terroristas”. 


A suspensão ocorreu no último dia 8 de outubro e o grupo ficou paralisado por pelo menos três dias.

Martins adoeceu. Teve uma crise de fibromialgia e ficou acamada boa parte do tempo. Até agora ela conta que está sem seu número, que foi bloqueado, e só está conseguindo voltar aos aplicativos e à gestão do grupo pois adquiriu outro chip de telefone. 


“Eu tenho fibromialgia, então assim, fiquei tão estressada, sem andar. Para além das outras coisas, dos atentados à soberania, nossa liberdade de reunião e de expressão, teve toda essa parte da minha saúde emocional”, contou a arquiteta à

Agência Pùblica

.

 


Comunidade e grupo de bate-papo pró-Lula foram suspensos por atividade relacionada a organizações terroristas


Martins já está com o Instagram ativo novamente e com a comunidade, que tem agora 895 participantes. Antes do bloqueio, a comunidade tinha atingido o limite de mil membros. Por intermédio de uma amiga ela conseguiu contato com a Meta e apurou que o bloqueio teria se dado por uma suposta “falha de tradução” de um monitoramento da comunidade que apontou “disruptive behaviour” (comportamento perturbador), o que teria sido interpretado como terrorismo. 


Meta bloqueia vídeo crítico a Flávio por “nudez infantil” 


Já o professor e artesão Karl Hadzic Júnior, 47 anos, morador de São Paulo, republicou em sua timeline o vídeo viral “como mãe de menina, meu voto jamais será dessa família”, postado originalmente pela professora paraense Vanessa Silva, no dia 7 de outubro, e que teve quase 45 mil compartilhamentos e 115 mil curtidas.

O vídeo foi bloqueado pela Meta também no dia 8 de outubro, sob a acusação de ter ferido padrões de comunidade sobre nudez infantil. 


O vídeo começa com uma foto de Silva abraçada com a filha, sem expor nenhuma região sensível da garota. A publicação utiliza um vídeo de Flávio Bolsonaro que ficou conhecido em 2023 no qual ele aparece sem camisa, supostamente imitando o irmão Jair Renan, dizendo: “sou filho do presidente, quer me dar?”. 


View this post on Instagram


Vídeo que viralizou no Instagram e foi marcado pela Meta como conteúdo sensível


O vídeo de Silva segue no ar, mas foi sinalizado com um filtro do Instagram que aparece antes da reprodução, informando sobre “conteúdo sensível”.

 A professora contou à

Pública

 que várias pessoas que publicaram o vídeo nos stories disseram a ela que a publicação foi suspensa ou até mesmo tiveram as contas bloqueadas. 


A

Pública

 procurou a Meta para ouvir a companhia sobre casos relatados nessa reportagem, mas não houve resposta.


Professor compartilhou vídeo crítico a Flávio Bolsonaro, mas foi bloqueado pela Meta por nudez infantil


MPF pede esclarecimentos à Meta após levantamento indicar parcialidade nos bloqueios


Tanto o caso de Marins, quanto de Júnior foram compilados pela organização social brasileira Ctrl+Z, voltada ao enfrentamento dos abusos e do modelo de operação das grandes empresas de tecnologia, que reuniu mais de mil denúncias de usuários de produtos da Meta e do X que relatam casos de bloqueio ou suspensão de contas e postagens relacionados às eleições.


A

Pública


mostrou

 como esse levantamento indica que a Meta tem barrado mais conteúdos pró-Lula e progressistas que pró-Flávio.

Reportagem

 da Folha mostrou que funcionários da Meta admitiram em mensagens internas que a “conta de Lula estava ‘limitada’ em comparação à de Flávio, e que isso seria negativo pela “alta chance” de haver ação jurídica”.


O levantamento da Ctrl+Z ganhou apoio das organizações de direitos humanos Conectas, Artigo 19 e Sleeping Giants Brasil e transformou-se em uma representação à

Procuradoria Federal dos Direitos do Cidadão do Ministério Público Federal (MPF) que abriu uma investigação no último dia 13 e pediu, no dia seguinte, uma série de esclarecimentos à Meta.

title: Burdur’da barakada çıkan yangında 85 yaşındaki Dudu Şimşek hayatını kaybetti
content:
Burdur’un merkeze bağlı Çallıca köyünde, 85 yaşındaki Dudu Şimşek’in yaşadığı barakada henüz belirlenemeyen nedenle yangın çıktı. Alevleri fark eden vatandaşların ihbarı üzerine olay yerine itfaiye, sağlık ve jandarma ekipleri sevk edildi.

İtfaiye ekiplerinin müdahalesiyle kontrol altına alınarak söndürülen yangının ardından yapılan incelemede, Şimşek’in hayatını kaybettiği belirlendi.

Olay yerindeki incelemelerin ardından Şimşek’in cenazesi, otopsi yapılmak üzere Burdur Devlet Hastanesi’ne kaldırıldı.

Yangının çıkış nedeninin belirlenmesi amacıyla inceleme başlatıldı.

Anche in Italia sabato 17 ottobre sembra essere diventata una data di mobilitazione contro il carovita e contro il carocarburante a partire da chiamate spontanee soprattutto tramite social e gruppi telegram. L’appuntamento si inserisce in settimane di inizio autunno che hanno visto cortei di massa per la Palestina il 10 ottobre, occupazioni nelle scuole con la mobilitazione studentesca di oggi 16 ottobre, blocchi degli autotrasportatori al Sud e, in prospettiva, vedranno altri cortei sui temi della guerra e del riarmo oltre allo sciopero del 30 ottobre.


Di seguito alcuni contributi in vista delle piazze.


Agricoltori piemontesi contro caro carburante e carovita


In continuità con le interviste fatte in questi giorni agli agricoltori in mobilitazione in tutta Italia, ci siamo collegate con Gabriele Ponzano, presidente del nodo di Agricoltori Autonomi Italiani di Alessandria, e membro di COAPI (Coordinamento Agricoltori Pescatori Italiani). Ponzano ci aggiorna sull’ultima, partecipata assemblea dell’associazione, la scorsa settimana. 


Da questo incontro è emersa chiaramente l’intenzione di muoversi insieme agli agricoltori del sud Italia, ma anche ad altri cittadini e cittadine per opporsi all’aumento dei costi di produzione, al caro energia e al carovita. Proprio in questa prospettiva, sono diversi gli agricoltori e le agricoltrici che sabato 17 ottobre parteciperanno alla piazza chiamata a Torino ore 15 in piazza Castello.

CONTRO IL CAROVITA: MANIFESTAZIONE A BRESCIA SABATO 17 OTTOBRE


Sabato 17 ottobre anche a Brescia è organizzata la manifestazione “Italia in Piazza” con numerose rivendicazioni: contro il carovita, per il lavoro sicuro, contro gli stipendi da fame, per aumentare i finanziamenti alla sanità pubblica, alle scuole e all’università.


Il “nodo” bresciano di questa manifestazione si dà appuntamento in Largo Formentone a partire dalle ore 14. Una manifestazione che viene organizzata prevalentemente attraverso whatsapp e i social network (qui il link al profilo 

Instagram

)


Noi abbiamo intervistato due delle organizzatrici, Sara Marini e Giulia Benedetti


MANIFESTO

 


In questo documento sono racchiuse le motivazioni e i fini della manifestazione  “Italia in Piazza”.  


“Italia in piazza” è una manifestazione apartitica. Essa vuole essere una riunione  pacifica di cittadini, diritto sancito dall’articolo 17 della Costituzione Italiana, con lo  scopo di mettere il focus sulle problematiche che affrontiamo ogni giorno. Il  sistema in cui viviamo, che spesso ci sembra inalterabile, è in realtà  estremamente fragile: solo lasciandoci dietro divisioni e pregiudizi possiamo  veramente essere uniti per pretendere di vivere, e non solo di sopravvivere. 

Non  importa chi siamo, in cosa ci identifichiamo, quale sia il nostro orientamento  sessuale o quali divinità preghiamo

: a unirci è il fatto che non lasceremo che ci  rubino ciò che ci spetta di diritto. 


“Italia in piazza” nasce per unire i cittadini per la stessa causa, i cui punti principali  sono: 


Lavoro sicuro, futuro sicuro: basta morti sul lavoro e giovani in  fuga. 


I lavoratori italiani sono costretti ad accettare condizioni lavorative inadeguate o a  fuggire all’estero: quello che resta è un mercato del lavoro caratterizzato da nero  dilagante, abuso di forme contrattuali precarie (tirocini, contratti a termine),  retribuzioni da barzelletta e condizioni di sicurezza che mietono morti ogni  giorno1. 


Basta stipendi da fame incapaci di coprire il costante aumento  del costo della vita. 


Carburanti, energia e beni alimentari di prima necessità costano sempre di più a  causa delle scelte egoistiche di potenti di cui il nostro Paese è succube: i nostri  soldi vengono spesi in armi e soldati mentre le famiglie ne hanno sempre meno  per vivere. I partiti che di volta in volta governano si affannano a farci credere che  vada tutto bene, ma la realtà è sempre più uno sfacelo: guerra dopo guerra, una  crisi dopo l’altra, il costo di qualunque cosa è in continuo aumento mentre gli  stipendi italiani sono gli stessi da 30 anni. 


La sanità non può continuare a diventare sempre più un lusso. 


Per la sanità pubblica si spende sempre meno e una porzione sempre maggiore  di quella spesa è fatta di acquisti di prestazioni e materiali da aziende private che,  ciliegina sulla torta, beneficiano anche di sgravi fiscali sempre più corposi. La  realtà del Sistema Sanitario Nazionale è totalmente inadeguata rispetto …
