title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Will 1793 Take Place?
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Will 1793 Take Place?

Subtitle

: Destituent Remarks on the Chilean Uprising and the Yellow Vests

Date

: October 6

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by the authors and Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/1793


 


 First published in French in August 2026, the present article argues that the 2018–19 Yellow Vests movement in France and the 2019 Chilean uprising form two instances of a single pattern. In each case, an insurrection begins with modest demands, such as a metro fare or a fuel tax only to then explode outward, outstripping its own stated goals, before ultimately being contained by constituent processes, referendums, and left-wing electoral projects. The authors treat the Constitution of 1793, with its famous article on the “duty of insurrection,” as the archetypal “act of capture” for such sequences: on the one hand, it was an attempt by ruling powers to absorb revolutionary energy into itself; at the same time, it served to embed a permanent insurrectionary principle into the political-legal system, one which the state has never been able to fully extirpate. Against the left’s push for new constitutional initiatives, the authors argue for a “revolution without power” grounded in the refusal of institutions and representation, crediting the Yellow Vests with developing new forms of assembly and fleeting affiliation in the absence of a distinct language or subject of its own. The key question, they suggest, is ultimately not whether 1793 will take place, but who will finish the job.


 


 Then annihilate forever what may one day destroy your work. Consider that the fruit of your labors being reserved for your grandchildren only, duty and probity command that you bequeath them none of those seeds of disaster which could mean for your descendants a renewal of the chaos whence we have with so much trouble just emerged. At the present moment our prejudices are weakening; the people have already abjured the Catholic absurdities; they have already suppressed the temples, sent the relics flying, and agreed that marriage is a mere civil undertaking; the smashed confessionals serve as public meeting places; the former faithful, deserting the apostolic banquet, leave the gods of flour dough to the mice. […] One more effort; since you labor to destroy all the old foundations, do not permit one of them to survive, for let but one endure, ‘tis enough, the rest will be restored. And how much more certain of their revival must we not be if the one you tolerate is positively the source and cradle of all the others! —Marquis de Sade,

Philosophy in the Bedroom

, 1795


In Santiago as in Paris


 Chile, October 25

th

, 2020.

[1]

 After months of insurrectionary demonstrations, the government agrees to hold a referendum to elect a constituent assembly. The vote takes place on the 15

th

 and 16

th

 of May, 2021, and on July 4

th

 the assembly begins its work, which is to last for a period of one year. With the initiation of the constituent process, another quite distinct process draws to a close: the revolutionary process. The latter began on October 7, 2019 when groups of young people, dissatisfied with the rise in metro fares, decided to refuse to pay and to jump the ticket barriers en masse. Collective ingenuity, the joy of rebellion, the determination of the

primera línea

 (frontline), the feeling of being on the verge of storming heaven, all gradually give way to self-serious protocols and democratic formalism. On two separate occasions, the newly drafted constitution is rejected in referendums and abandoned. The rest is history: the left wins the elections of November–December 2021 with an abstention rate of roughly 50 percent, taking power in March 2022. Yet the aftermath proves disappointing and, in December 2025, a far-right candidate, the son of a Nazi, is elected as the country’s leader against a backdrop of a spectacular rise in voter turnout (up thirty-eight percent in the first round, and twenty-nine in the second). Once again, hopes for a Chilean path towards a freer and more egalitarian society are dashed. Once again, counterrevolution succeeds in stifling the revolutionary process, by imposing upon it the timeframe and institutional forms of democratic power: the mirage of a referendum, a moment of national electoral unity, a left-wing government, and a breakthrough by the far right.

title: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan - Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt
content:
Author

: Groupe Révolutionnaire Charlatan

Title

: Remarks on the Ongoing Student Revolt

Date

: October 9

th

, 2026

Notes

: Translated by Ill Will

Source

: https://illwill.com/remarks-on-the-ongoing-student-revolt


 The following remarks, forged in the heat of battle during a wave of student unrest that is now spreading to Belgium and Italy, were posted to

x.com

 on October 6, 2026. For a longer position piece by the same authors, see their recent article, “

Will 1793 Take Place?

”


1.


 The student revolt is the spearhead of the movement announced for October 17.


2.


 The “gangs” [bandes] of students from working-class neighborhoods constitute the actual driving force both within and against the current youth movement. In a sense, this force is less a part of the student movement than it is a continuation of the Nahel revolt. It has neither demands nor representatives; it does not conform to the codes of the Left and rejects bourgeois politeness. It wants revenge.


3.


 The universities have followed the high schools and joined the dynamic of the blockades. They, in turn, could bring about a qualitative leap by, for example, launching an occupation that could be taken up and spread by other sectors of society—whether students or not. This hypothesis, however, is oppposed by the overwhelming dominance of student union organizations, which leave little room for group spontaneity, collective ingenuity, and self-subversive practices.


4.


 When one speaks of “blockades” at high schools, one is already engaging in a form of reduction and simplification of the practices of the student revolt. There are acts of sabotage (doors set on fire, gates knocked down, “e-blockades” against distance learning) and acts of revenge (against the school hierarchy and the police outside), urban guerrilla tactics (barricades) and wildcat strikes (work stoppages during breaks and staggered blockades), and finally something akin to a game aimed at ridiculing authority (slogans about Macron and his teacher, superhero costumes in contrast to the oppressors’ uniforms).


5.


 The unions cannot come to terms with the idea of October 17, as it reminds them too much of the Yellow Vests. They must pretend to join the movement in order to gain better control over it—both through their monopoly on negotiations and by dictating the timeline. If the inter-union coalition called for action on October 6 alongside the students, it was only to better defuse the call for October 17, which they wish to reduce to an interim date ahead of their mobilization on November 5.


6.


 In high schools, the left differs from other political forces in form, but not in substance. In form, the left pushes students into the role of victims, thereby allowing itself to present as the “responsible adults.” Consider the human chains of parents and teachers, or elected officials denouncing the police’s use of LBD weapons. It is striking, however, that batons, shields, helmets, and other standard components of the arsenal of democracy are far less frequently called into question.


7.


 In terms of substance, the left aligns itself with the other political forces in their efforts to restore peace. This is precisely what happens when it puts forward demands that are consistent with its platform, thereby helping to separate the “good” students (those with demands deemed legitimate) from the “bad” students (these “rioters” without ideas or genuine political motives).


8.


 Unlike the left, we have neither flags to wave, nor a tempo to set, nor lessons to teach.


9.


 How should we deal with the enthusiasm for “October 17” and the way certain segments of the youth present it as an echo of the Yellow Vests movement? Even if a new generation seems to invoke its symbolic power full of hope, it is by no means certain that reusing the object will help us rediscover its spirit. Nevertheless, perhaps that is precisely what is expected of us: to don it and see if it—even if only temporarily—embodies a sense of belonging with which others can identify and to which they can align themselves, without appropriating it in the process. At the risk of appearing ridiculous and anachronistic, and discarding it again swiftly.


10.


 The spectacular actions of the student revolt are the work of bands or gangs [bandes] that organize themselves and make their identity known in this way. Wearing Under Armour outfits fools no one: only to the extent that we reconnect …

title: Peso dives to new record low
content:
The Philippine Peso dove to a new record low on Thursday, breaching past the P63 threshold per US dollar for the first time in history. The Peso-Dollar exchange rate closed at P63.15 per US greenback. The previous record was P62.925 per US dollar set exactly a month ago on September 15.


The Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) cited a stronger US dollar, shifting expectations around US Federal Reserve rate cuts, and regional market pressures brought about by the prolonged war in the Middle East as the reasons for the dive.


The Philippine currency had lost P5.21 to the US dollar since the US-Israel led war against Iran started in February 28.


The new record low happened as the BSP played conservative in defending the peso against the volatile foreign exchange market, choosing to preserve its reserves and intervening only when movements become sharp and disorderly.


The BSP primarily uses the country’s Gross International Reserves to stabilize the Philippine peso against foreign exchange volatility and to service foreign debt obligations.


The Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA), meanwhile, said electronic products and petroleum products, such as crude oil and refined fuel are two top importations that drain the country’s foreign exchange and import outlays.


Much of the country’s reserves come from remittances from its millions of workers abroad, such as 2.4 million overseas laborers in the Middle East. There are about a million Filipinos in the UAE alone, contributing approximately P380 billion or $6.06 billion every year.


Local economic think-tank Ibon Foundation said that a record-low Philippine peso paired with high global oil and import prices creates a “double whammy” that aggressively drives up domestic inflation and worsens economic strain for Filipino households.


The PSA recently reported that the inflation rate in the Philippines was at a whopping 7.2 per cent last September, a sharp increase from 6.1 per cent last August.


Philippine oil industry sources have already announced a gasoline price increase of up to P4.30 per liter next week. #

(Raymund B. Villanueva)

content:
Yeni Parti İzmir Milletvekili Ümit Özlale, fon vurgunu soruşturmasına ilişkin yaptığı açıklamada Türkiye Sigorta Genel Müdürü Taha Çakmak’ın istifasının daha geniş bir ilişki ağının araştırılması gerektiğini gösterdiğini söyledi.

Çakmak'la birlikte fon soruşturması kapsamında tutuklanan eski TCMB Başkan Yardımcısı Erkan Kilimci ve soruşturmada adı geçen eski bakan yardımcısı Bülent Aksu'nun Berat Albayrak'ın Hazine ve Maliye Bakanlığı dönemiyle bağlantılarının açıklığa kavuşturulması gerektiğini söyleyen Özlale, Borsa İstanbul Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı ve Türkiye Varlık Fonu Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili Erişah Arıcan'ı da "yolların kesiştiği isim" olarak tanımlıyor. Özlale, Berat Albayrak'ın tezini Arıcan'la birlikte yazdığını hatırlatıyor.

Özlale, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı açıklamada şu ifadeleri kullandı: "Bir istifa, onlarca bağlantı, milyarlarca liralık soru… Taha Çakmak kim? Erişah Arıcan’dan Türkiye Sigorta’ya, kredi derecelendirmesinden yatırım fonlarına uzanan ilişkiler bize ne anlatıyor? İsim isim, kurum kurum anlattım. Bir halka koptu diye zincirin geri kalanını unutturamazsınız. Taha Çakmak’ın istifası ve bir ilişki ağının anatomisi. Bir istifa çok sayıda bağlantı. İstifası bugün kamuoyuna yansıyan ve haberlerde malvarlığına tedbir konulduğu belirtilen Taha Çakmak sıradan biri değil. Kendisi, Şahap Kavcıoğlu’nun TCMB Başkanı olduğu dönemde başkan yardımcılığı yaptı. Daha önce, 2016–2018 yıllarında TCMB Başkan Yardımcılığı yapan ve sonrasında TERA yönetiminde yer alan Erkan Kilimci de fon soruşturması kapsamında tutuklandı. Kilimci ile Çakmak aynı dönemde başkan yardımcılığı yapmadı; ancak farklı dönemlerde kamu finans yönetiminde görev alan bu isimlerin daha sonra hangi kurumlarda buluştuğunun araştırılması gerekiyor. Fon soruşturmasında adı geçen eski bakan yardımcısı Bülent Aksu’nun da bulunduğu bu çevrenin Berat Albayrak dönemiyle bağlantıları açıklığa kavuşturulmalıdır. Yolların kesiştiği isim: Erişah Arıcan. Sayın Berat Albayrak tezini Erişah Arıcan ile yazmış. Erişah Hanım o kadar kıymetli biri ki kendisi hem Borsa İstanbul Yönetim Kurulu Başkanı hem de Türkiye Varlık Fonu Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili. Lisans derecesini nereden aldığına dair çok bilgi yok ama sonrasında hep Marmara Üniversitesi’nde olmuş. Zaten kendisi aynı üniversitede öğretim üyesi olan Aydın Ayaydın’ın yeğeni. Erişah Hanım’ın çok başarılı tez öğrencileri var. Biri de yukarıda bahsettiğimiz Şahap Kavcıoğlu. Kendisinin başkanlık döneminde TCMB’de insan kaynakları genel müdürü olarak görev yapan Doğan Başar da Taha Çakmak’ın genel müdür olduğu Türkiye Sigorta’da genel müdür yardımcısı olarak görev yapıyor. Türkiye Sigorta’nın bir de teknik genel müdür yardımcısı var. Adı Çağrı Akpınar. Kendisi Marmara Finansal Bilimler Fakültesi Dekan Yardımcısı Özgür Akpınar’ın kardeşi ve Erişah Arıcan’ın da doktora öğrencisi. Türkiye Sigorta’nın parası nereye gitti? Peki, daha önce hakkında tedbir kararı alındığı ve bu kararın saatler sonra kaldırıldığı ileri sürülen Türkiye Sigorta A.Ş. neden önemli? Fon vurgununu konuşurken neden bu kurumun yatırım kararlarını sorguluyoruz? Çünkü topladığı primlerle, tasfiyesine karar verilen fonlara ve soruşturmaya konu hisse senetlerine yüksek tutarlı yatırım yaptığına ilişkin iddialar var. Türkiye Sigorta’nın ana hissedarı, sermayesinin yüzde 76,1’ini elinde bulunduran TVF Finansal Yatırımlar AŞ. Kalan yüzde 23,9’luk pay Borsa İstanbul’da işlem görüyor. Dolayısıyla Borsa İstanbul’un hissedar olmasıyla şirket paylarının borsada işlem görmesi birbirine karıştırılmamalı. Buradaki temel soru, bu ölçekte kurumsal kaynağın hangi yatırım kararlarıyla, hangi riskler üstlenilerek kullanıldığıdır. İşin bir de özel sektör tahvili tarafı var ki önlem alınmazsa ciddi bir piyasa riski doğurabilir. Sistemi, Adil Varlık Yönetim AŞ hakkında ileri sürülen iddialar üzerinden ele alalım. Şirketin ortaklık yapısı, Mustafa Yazıcı ve Ali Emre Ballı’yla bağlantıları, gerçekleşen tahvil ihraçları ve ihraç gelirlerinin kullanım yerleri birlikte ortaya konmalıdır. İncelenmesi gereken ihtimal şu: Bir şirket tahvil ihraç ederek topladığı parayı faaliyet veya yatırım yerine sorunlu fonlara yönlendirirse ne olur? Bu şirketin borçlanmaya erişiminde güçlü bir kredi notunun etkisi bulunabilir. İşte bu noktada devreye kredi derecelendirme kuruluşları giriyor. Bu alanda önemli bir yeri bulunan kredi derecelendirme kuruluşu JCR Eurasia’ya bakalım. Yönetim Kurulu Başkan Vekili ve Genel Müdür Prof. Dr. Feyzullah Yetgin bilin bakalım kiminle …

title: Vahap Seçer'den TBB Başkan Vekili seçilen Ayşe Ünlüce'ye tebrik: Bu görevi başarıyla sürdüreceğine inanıyorum
content:
Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği, TBB Başkanı Vahap Seçer’in tutuklanarak görevden uzaklaştırılması nedeniyle başkan vekili seçimi yaptı. Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce, TBB Başkan Vekilliğine seçildi.

Tutuklu Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği ve Mersin Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Vahap Seçer, TBB Başkan Vekilliğine seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik etti.

Belediyelerin gücünü temsil ettikleri kentlerin yurttaşlarından aldığını söyleyen Seçer, demokrasi ve milli iradeyi savunmaya devam edeceklerini ifade etti.

Seçer, seçimin ardından yaptığı açıklamada şu ifadeleri kullandı:

“Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği Başkanvekilliği görevine seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik ediyorum. Benim de gururla üstlendiğim bu görevi başarıyla sürdüreceğine inanıyorum. Demokrasinin ve milli iradenin en doğrudan tecelli ettiği belediyeler, gücünü temsil ettikleri kentin yurttaşlarından alır. Ülke nüfusunun büyük bölümünü sosyal belediyecilik anlayışıyla kucaklayarak kurduğumuz gönül bağının gücüne inancım tam. Bu inançla, her nerede ve hangi koşulda olursak olalım, demokrasi ve milli iradeyi savunmaya devam edeceğiz.”

author: Isabela Dias
title: Eduardo Bolsonaro vive noite de celebridade na festa da extrema direita nos EUA
content:
Na noite de quarta-feira (14), empresários conservadores, influenciadores digitais e autoridades do governo dos Estados Unidos se reuniram no Andrew W. Mellon Auditorium, na capital Washington, D.C., para a festa de gala da Hispanic Heritage, organizado pela plataforma financeira Latino Wall Street.


O homenageado do evento foi Javier Milei, presidente da Argentina. Seu principal aliado no Brasil, Eduardo Bolsonaro, foi um dos convidados de honra.  


Na entrada, convidados trajados com roupas brilhantes e smokings cercaram Eduardo para tirar selfies e apertos de mão. Muitos perguntavam sobre o pai, Jair Bolsonaro, que cumpre em casa a pena de 27 anos de prisão por tentativa de golpe de Estado. Outros demonstravam entusiasmo com a liderança do irmão Flávio Bolsonaro no primeiro turno da

disputa presidencial

 contra o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. 


Eduardo conversou com veículos de comunicação identificados com o movimento MAGA (“Make America Great Again”, um dos slogans de Donald Trump), como a ex-boxeadora Cara Castronuova, uma das

correspondentes da Casa Branca

 alinhadas ao governo. Ele também

posou

 ao lado de Javier Negre, comunicador espanhol apelidado de “Rei Midas da viralidade”. Negre é sócio de Fernando Cerimedo, marqueteiro argentino de extrema direita,

detido

 em agosto na Bolívia, acusado de envolvimento em ataque a tiros contra a ex-companheira.    


Em determinado momento, na entrada do evento, uma mulher que parecia ser uma das convidadas segurou o braço de Eduardo e ambos olharam para baixo, compenetrados. Eles rezavam pelo Brasil. Quem também tietava Eduardo Bolsonaro era a autointitulada diplomata espiritual, consultora de direitos humanos e empresária gaúcha

Luciana Pananos

, que mora nos EUA. 


Do lado de dentro, iniciada a cerimônia, os oradores no palco falavam sobre acabar com a criminalidade e derrotar o socialismo na América Latina. Na plateia, os convidados, que pagaram entre US$ 3 mil e US$ 10 mil para participar do evento, saboreavam almôndegas de wagyu (carne bovina de origem japonesa), pato defumado com amoras, abacate recheado grelhado e filé-mignon bovino defumado. 


“Vamos expulsar o ditador comunista do Brasil”, bradou o homenageado da noite, Javier Milei, após

abraçar

 calorosamente Eduardo, que deu chutes no ar como se estivesse expulsando Lula do posto. O presidente da Argentina disse ainda que os conservadores “não podem ceder um centímetro em nossa reconquista do hemisfério”. 


“Um discurso inspirador”


Após a fala de Milei, Eduardo discursou. Ele ponderou que o resultado da eleição ainda não estava definido. Mas o tom era abertamente comemorativo. “Quando confirmarmos a vitória do meu irmão, o senador Flávio Bolsonaro, como presidente do Brasil, vamos entrar em uma nova era, que eu chamo de Era de Ouro da América Latina!”


O deputado cassado adotava um dos slogans de Donald Trump, que costuma dizer que o país vive uma nova “era de ouro” sob sua batuta. “Temos tudo para ser iguais aos Estados Unidos”, completou Eduardo.


Durante o discurso, ele também louvou outros presidentes de extrema direita na América Latina, como Nayib Bukele, de El Salvador, e o colombiano Abelardo de la Espriella.


“Amamos todos aqueles que dificultam a vida dos criminosos”, declarou, acrescentando que “pela primeira vez veremos todos os países [da América Latina] combatendo o narcoterrorismo”. O público aprovou e aplaudiu entusiasmado. Um empresário do setor imobiliário que atua em Honduras disse à reportagem que considerou o discurso “inspirador” e que o Brasil deveria adotar o “modelo Bukele”. 


Flávio e Eduardo já

visitaram

 o CECOT, o megacomplexo penitenciário para onde o governo Trump enviou imigrantes que, segundo

relatos

, foram torturados. Se a vitória de Flávio Bolsonaro se concretizar, o Brasil pode integrar a coalizão

Escudo das Américas

, formada por 19 países da região e liderada pelos EUA.  


“O melhor ainda está por vir”, declarou Eduardo Bolsonaro, prometendo libertar o Brasil, começando por seu pai.


Mais que entusiasta da candidatura do irmão à Presidência, Eduardo é um dos nomes mais

cotados

 para se tornar o próximo ministro das Relações Exteriores do Brasil em um eventual governo de Flávio. Desde que se mudou para os EUA, no início de 2025, o filho 03 de Bolsonaro perdeu o mandato de deputado federal por faltar a mais de 80% das sessões e também foi despojado do

emprego

 como investigador da Polícia Federal por abandono de posto.

author: Equality Now
title: Consent does not depend on one’s level of intoxication: The Cornell University Case in review
content:
15th October 2026


Consent does not depend on one’s level of intoxication: The Cornell University Case in review


14 min read


News and Insights


End sexual violence


United States


Image credit: Matthew Poveromo / Shutterstock.com


The allegations presented in the

sexual violence case involving a Cornell University student

 describe egregious acts of sexual violence and profound violations of the human rights of the alleged survivor. The case returned to public attention two years after the alleged assault, when the accuser, known publicly as Jane Doe, filed a civil lawsuit in 2026, bringing renewed scrutiny to the handling of her allegations and the evidence surrounding them while simultaneously raising serious concerns about whether criminal justice systems are fit to conduct thorough investigations, prosecutions, and adjudications of sexual violence cases. 


In November 2024,

a Cornell University student reported being sexually assaulted the month before by multiple men at a fraternity house

. According to her account and evidence subsequently reviewed by the University, she had consumed alcohol and drugs, including the dissociative drug ketamine, which left her severely incapacitated and unable to consent to sexual activity. She reported that multiple men entered the room at different points during the evening, and that several attempted to grope, kiss, or have sex with her despite her incapacitation. She also described gaps in her memory. During the alleged assault, one member of the fraternity shared messages on a group chat of more than 50 members, indicating that a woman was upstairs and available for sex, inviting others to join. Other members reportedly responded to and discussed the invitation in lieu of reporting the abuse. 


Cornell subsequently conducted a

Title IX investigation

, resulting in disciplinary sanctions against several students. The local District Attorney’s Office declined to investigate, and so no criminal charges were pursued at the time. The criminal investigation has now been reopened, with New York Attorney General Letitia James appointed as special prosecutor.


All criminal investigations must be assessed on the evidence, and anyone accused of a crime is entitled to due process. Yet, too often, criminal justice systems approach sexual violence cases through assumptions about force, resistance, credibility, or a survivor’s conduct and behaviour, rather than applying the same scrutiny to whether a person was able to freely consent to sexual activity.


A person who is unconscious or otherwise incapable of freely consenting cannot consent to sex. At the centre of this case, regardless of its eventual outcome, is a fundamental question: whether the one’s capacity to consent to sex was properly examined at all.  


Gaps in sexual violence law can harm survivors


Reporting sexual violence can require a survivor to recount deeply personal experiences to officials, investigators, police, prosecutors and lawyers, often while facing intense scrutiny of their choices, conduct, and credibility. In this case, the student has spent nearly two years navigating university, criminal and civil proceedings in pursuit of justice.


The reopening of a criminal case, particularly when the adequacy of a prior investigation of sexual violence allegations is under question,

has the potential to retraumatize survivors who will be forced to recount their experiences

 yet again. However, this case presents an important opportunity to examine how New York’s judicial system and the laws that govern it can become capable of delivering justice when survivors report sexual violence.  


In 19 US states, including New York, sexual assault laws distinguish between voluntary and involuntary intoxication

 in ways that can make prosecution for rape more difficult when a survivor voluntarily consumed alcohol or drugs. In these states,

 the law fails to recognise that a person who has become incapable of consenting is incapable of consenting, regardless of how they reached that state.


Under New York’s Penal Law,

most sexual offences are defined by lack of consent based on either forcible compulsion or incapacity

, although certain offences, including rape in the third degree, also recognise when a person clearly expresses that they do not want s to engage in sexual activity, even in the absence of force or incapacity, as lack of consent. Circumstances including statutory rape where someone over …

title: TELE1 çalışanları hakkını alamadı, Halk TV'de belirsizlik sürüyor: Kayyım baskısı gazetecilerin çalışma alanını da daraltıyor
content:
Son iki yılda aralarında Flash Haber, EkoTürk, Habertürk TV, Show TV, Bloomberg HT, HT Spor, Show Türk, Show Max, TELE1 ve Halk TV’nin bulunduğu 10 televizyon kanalına kayyım atandı. Farklı gerekçelerle yürütülen süreçlerde televizyonların yönetimleri Tasarruf Mevduatı Sigorta Fonu’na (TMSF) devredilirken, TELE1 ve Halk TV’ye yönelik müdahaleler, iktidar çizgisi dışında yayın yapan az sayıdaki televizyon kanalının yönetimlerinin değiştirilmesi açısından diğer kayyım süreçlerinden ayrıldı. Bu kanallarda çalışanların ve işten çıkarılanların yaşadıkları ise basın özgürlüğü ile çalışma hakkının aynı süreçte nasıl kesiştiğini ortaya koydu.

TELE1’e 24 Ekim 2025’te kayyım atanmasının ardından kanalın başına getirilen İbrahim Paşalı, 14 Ekim 2026’da Halk TV’ye de kayyım olarak atandı. Yeni Şafak’ta köşe yazarlığı yapan Paşalı, daha önce Flash Haber, Habertürk, Show TV ve Bloomberg HT’nin de aralarında bulunduğu medya kuruluşlarında kayyım olarak görev almıştı.

TELE1’de kayyım atandıktan sonra istifa eden bir gazeteci kayyım atamasının ardından yaşanan süreci anlattı. Kanalın kayyım yönetimine geçtiğinde 140 kişilik bir çalışan kadrosuna sahip olduğunu belirten gazeteci, önce Ankara bürosunun kapatıldığını, kanalın İstanbul’dan yürütüleceğinin söylendiğini, ardından İstanbul bürosunda da işten çıkarmaların devam ettiğini söyledi.

“140 kişilik ekibimizden 130 kişiyi işten attılar” diyen gazeteci, işten çıkarılan bazı arkadaşlarının Koza TV, İlke TV ve son olarak Halk TV’ye geçtiğini anlattı.

Ancak medya sektöründeki kayyım ve baskı süreçleri nedeniyle gazetecilerin çalışabileceği alanların zaten daraldığını belirten gazeteci, Halk TV’ye de kayyım atanmasının ardından bu alanın daha da küçüldüğünü söyledi. TELE1’de kayyım tarafından işten çıkarılanların önemli bölümünün halen işsiz olduğunu belirten gazeteci, bazı çalışanların ücret ve kıdem tazminatlarını da alamadığını söyledi. “Bu insanlar aylardır işsiz, hakları olan ücretleri alamadı, “bu sadece halkın haber alma hürriyetine kayyım atanması değil, bu gazetecilerin çalışamaması sonucu basının da işlevsiz bırakılmasıdır” dedi.

TELE1’de kayyım sonrasında işten çıkarılan başka bir gazeteci ise tazminat ve diğer alacakların ödenmediğini belirterek, işsizliğin sektördeki daralmayla birlikte ağırlaştığını söyledi.

“24 Ekim 2025’te TELE1’e kayyım atanmasının ardından aslında yıllardır süregelen kayyım uygulamasının mağdurları arasına eklendik” diyen gazeteci, bazı çalışanların ayrılmayı, bazılarının ise ekonomik zorluklara rağmen bir süre çalışmayı tercih ettiğini anlattı.

“Sonuç olarak hepimiz işten çıkarıldık. Aradan geçen zamana rağmen ödenmesi gereken, bilgi mesajıyla iletilen tazminatlarımız hala ödenmedi” dedi.

İşini kaybetmenin yarattığı ekonomik sıkıntıya hak edilen alacakların ödenmemesinin de eklendiğini belirten gazeteci, “Bir günde işten çıkarıldık, hala iş bulamayan basın emekçileri var” diye konuştu.

Gazeteci, bugün işini kaybetmenin yalnızca yeni bir iş aramak anlamına gelmediğini belirterek, “Giderek daralan çalışma alanlarında yeniden iş bulmaya çalışmak, geçinebilmek, kira ve faturaları ödemek, geleceğe dair belirsizlikle mücadele etmek anlamına geliyor” dedi.

TELE1’de işten çıkarılan çalışanların bir bölümünün daha sonra Halk TV’ye geçtiğini anlatan TELE1 çalışanının sözleri, Halk TV’de kayyım sonrası oluşan belirsizlikle de kesişiyor.

Halk TV reji ekibinden bir işçi, kayyım atanmasının ardından çalışanlar ve yöneticiler açısından ciddi bir belirsizlik oluştuğunu söyledi. Kayyım yönetimiyle yapılan görüşme sonrasında Halk TV yöneticileri, “Biz onlara yardımcı olmayacağız. Onlar burayı devam ettirmek istiyorlarmış. Kimseye ‘şunu yapın’ demiyoruz, karar sizin” denildiğini aktardı.

Kayyım yönetiminin kanalı sürdürmek istediğini söylediğini belirten işçi, “Buranın mali durumu iyi. Biz burayı döndürmek, devam ettirmek istiyoruz” ifadelerinin kullanıldığını söyledi.

Çalışanların öncelikle ne sunulacağını görmesi gerektiğini belirten işçi, teknik ekipteki çalışma arkadaşlarına da ani karar vermemeleri çağrısı yaptığını anlattı:

“Burada insanlar ev geçindiriyor, çoluğu çocuğu olan, faturası olan var. Hiç fevri bir karar vermektense önce bir dinleyelim, bize ne sunacaklar bir görelim. Ardından sendikayla da görüşelim, hep beraber bir karar alalım.”

title: Ünlüce'yi tebrik eden CHP Sözcüsü Sarı'dan "muhalefetin ortak iradesi" vurgusu
content:
CHP Sözcüsü Müslim Sarı, Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği (TBB) Başkan Vekilliğine seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik etti. Sarı, sonucun muhalefetin ortak iradesiyle elde edildiği vurgusunu yaptı.

Sarı, sosyal medya hesabından yaptığı paylaşımda, "Türkiye Belediyeler Birliği Başkanvekilliğine, partimizin desteğiyle seçilen Eskişehir Büyükşehir Belediye Başkanı Sayın Ayşe Ünlüce’yi tebrik ediyorum. Muhalefetin ortak iradesiyle elde edilen bu sonuç, yerel yönetimler açısından önemli bir kazanımdır" ifadesini kullandı.

TBB Başkan Vekilliği seçiminde Yeni Parti, Ayşe Ünlüce'yi aday olarak göstermiş, CHP de aday çıkarmayarak Ünlüce'yi destekleyeceğini duyurmuştu.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: Sally Ncube
title: Child marriage laws in Africa need more funding to protect girls
content:
15th October 2026


Child marriage laws in Africa need more funding to protect girls


12 min read


News and Insights


End child marriage


Africa


With global funding to end child marriage falling yearly since 2019, African governments must take action to strengthen budgeting and implementation of child marriage laws.  


By

Sally Ncube,

 Equality Now, and

Fatou Gueye Ndir,

 Senior Regional Engagement and Advocacy Officer, Girls Not Brides


Although numerous African governments have strengthened laws against child marriage, legal protections remain widely underfunded and ineffectively enforced. Many countries have no clearly outlined, dedicated national budget line for ending child marriage. Instead, allocated money is incorporated into broader gender or social protection budgets, where funds are often difficult or impossible for auditors to trace or civil society to access. 


Funding to end child marriage is falling 


The joint report, ‘

International Funding to End Child Marriage: Reviewing a Decade of Investment

,’ by

Girls Not Brides

 and

Girls First Fund

, with input from

Publish What You Fund

, found that funding to end child marriage accounts for only a tiny fraction of Official Development Assistance (ODA), while local frontline organisations working directly with girls and communities receive only a sliver of available budgets.  


Between 2015 and 2023, just 0.025 per cent of all ODA globally was directed to projects whose primary objective was to end child marriage. A further 0.081 per cent went to broader projects in which addressing child marriage was one of several objectives, rather than the primary purpose, and it was not possible to determine how much of this secondary funding was specifically spent on child marriage interventions. 


Investment to end child marriage peaked in 2019. Since then, it has fallen every year, dropping from US$76 million to US$51 million by 2023, and this deterioration accelerated with

2025’s historic decline in global aid

. With several major donors scaling back investment in gender equality, ODA faces mounting pressure.


Over the next five years, more than 70 million girls worldwide are expected to be at risk of child marriage. Yet current levels of international funding dedicated to ending this form of violence against children amount to less than US$1 per girl at risk each year globally. At a time when conflict, climate change, anti-rights movements and shrinking civic space are all exacerbating the dangers girls face, declining investment threatens to further undermine child protection in Africa.


Ending child marriage is also an economic imperative:

girls who marry later stay in school longer, earn more, and raise healthier families

, with gains that impact entire communities. 


Legal loopholes and poor enforcement of laws leave girls vulnerable to child marriage 


Passing laws is only the first step. Governments must back them with dedicated funding, strengthening relevant institutions and duty bearers, for effective enforcement, oversight, and clear accountability. A dedicated budget line is not a bureaucratic technicality; it is the difference between turning legal promises and human rights obligations and commitments to end child marriage on paper into meaningful real-world protection for girls.


Most African Union Member States have ratified the

African Charter on the Rights and Welfare of the Child

, which requires countries to prohibit child marriage. The Charter has established a strong regional legal framework and contributed to many countries enacting laws to prevent child marriage. What is now needed is a concerted effort to improve implementation of existing laws and remove remaining gaps in legal protections. 


According to the African Union’s 2026 report,

Ending Child Marriage in Africa

, 18 countries in Africa have a minimum marriage age of 18 or above, with no exceptions. The continent’s remaining 37 countries do not meet this standard. Some set a minimum age below 18 for one or both sexes, while others have raised the age of marriage to 18 but permit exemptions, such as allowing judicial, parental or other legal authorisation for a child to marry.


The African Committee of Experts on the Rights and Welfare of the Child (ACERWC), in its 2026

Thematic Report on Harmful Practices Affecting Children in Africa

, stated that despite decades of advocacy and progress in strengthening legal frameworks, child marriage …

author: labor4pal
title: GEO Files Unfair Labor Practice Charge Against the University of Michigan (GEO 3550)
content:
A post shared by Graduate Employees’ Organization 3550 (University of Michigan) (@geo_3550)

ANN ARBOR, MI — On Wednesday October 14th, the Graduate Employees’ Organization (GEO) filed an Unfair Labor Practice (ULP) charge against the University of Michigan for issuing two politically motivated felony charges against GEO president, Hiab Teshome. Hiab was charged with embezzlement and false pretenses charges concerning purchases made by a student group she was a co-signer of. This pretextual and unprecedented legal assault was the University’s latest attempt to interfere with protected Union activities and the collective bargaining process.

In June 2026, so-called “progressive” Washtenaw County Prosecutor and Michigan Attorney General candidate Eli Savit took up the University of Michigan Police Department’s (UMPD) request for felony charges against Hiab. The UMPD have historically violently repressed labor and the Palestine solidarity movement. The arrest warrant and charges were brought forth through a collaboration between Savit, UMPD’s Sergeant Ryan Cavanaugh, and the Center for Campus Involvement (CCI), particularly CCI director Nick Smith. Cavanaugh and UMPD have directly harassed and attempted to intimidate Hiab, including an attempt to visit her prior address. On August 6th, all charges were dismissed by Judge Cedric Simpson.

In addition, UMPD unilaterally usurped the prosecutor’s office and filed to the magistrate judge requests for additional bond conditions against Hiab including attempting to ban her from campus and successfully banning her from the Ruthven Building due to it being the location of the Regent’s offices. The Regents set major University policy and have targeted individuals in the labor and pro-Palestine movement.

The University’s decision to involve law enforcement over alleged misconduct in a student organization is unprecedented and directly contradicts the University’s student organization accountability processes, which explicitly deem criminalization inappropriate. The Central Student Government (CGS), which typically oversees student organizations, released a statement affirming the inappropriate use of the legal system against individuals in their capacity as members of a student organization. The University never engaged in their own internal process and never contacted Hiab until she was being investigated by Cavanaugh and still have not contacted her.

The University of Michigan initiated legal processes against its own policies in an attempt to interfere, restrain, and coerce the elected president of GEO from her rights as a public employee and to deprive the Union of the right to select its own bargaining agents. As such, GEO maintains that the University has violated the Public Employment Relations Act and we are demanding accountability.

It is abundantly clear that, if not for Hiab’s protected union activity, the University of Michigan would never have sought the issuance of such meritless charges. These charges were an attempt to limit Hiab from appearing as a bargaining representative and to restrict her rights as a public employee.

The University used the threat of criminal proceedings to try to silence and intimidate not just a Union member, but our entire Union. GEO will not stand for any attempts by the University of Michigan and its collaborators in the legal system to repress Palestine solidarity or labor organizing. We affirm our commitment to workers at the University of Michigan and will continue to fight for just labor conditions for all workers.

Representatives are available for interviews with the press to talk about the Unfair Labor Practice and GEO’s ongoing contract negotiations with U-M.

author: Lisa Femia
title: Our Lawsuit Against the Trump Administration’s Social Media Surveillance Moves Forward. Here’s What the Court Said.
content:
No one should have to choose between speaking freely and protecting their immigration status. Yet that’s precisely the choice the Trump administration’s mass surveillance of online speech forces on noncitizens living in the U.S. 

  


Last fall, we

sued

 on behalf of three major labor unions to stop this surveillance program. And just this month, we won our first major ruling: A federal district court

denied

 the government’s motion to dismiss our lawsuit. This means the case can move forward—a win for free speech and a critical step in protecting our First Amendment rights online. We’ve already explained why this is a

big deal

 for our clients, so let's take a closer look at the court’s reasoning.

  


Our Lawsuit

 


 Since taking power, the Trump administration has used AI and other automated tools to

broadly surveil

 the social media and online speech of visa and green card holders, with the goal of identifying and punishing people who express views it opposes. The government is targeting a broad range of views, including

criticism of the


Trump administration

;

support for Palestine

 or

criticism of Israel

;

“rationalizing or making light of”

 Charlie Kirk’s murder; and anything nebulously

“hostile”

 to American culture,

founding principles

,

“traditional American views,”

 or

“our way of life.”

 

 


It has paired that surveillance with a public intimidation campaign. High-ranking officials have explicitly

threatened

 to punish noncitizens for their online speech, then followed through with a series of terrifying viewpoint-driven enforcement actions.

This has led to a significant chilling effect on speech, not just for noncitizens, but also for their families, coworkers, and friends.

 


In response, three major labor unions—the United Auto Workers (UAW), the Communications Workers of America (CWA), and the American Federation of Teachers (AFT)—

sued

 the Departments of State and Homeland Security alleging that this viewpoint-based surveillance program violates the First Amendment and the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).  

The unions are represented by EFF, Muslim Advocates (MA), and the Media Freedom & Information Access Clinic (MFIA).

 


The government moved to dismiss our lawsuit, arguing first that federal immigration law prevents federal district courts from hearing the case, and second, that the unions don’t have “standing” to sue. Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein of the Southern District of New York rejected both arguments and allowed the case to proceed. At this stage in the litigation, the court accepted all of the facts in our complaint as true and analyzed the law based on those facts. We will now prove these facts as the case proceeds.

 


Federal Immigration Law Doesn’t Block Our Lawsuit

 


 The government first argued that the court had no power to hear our case at all. It pointed to three provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) that restrict when federal courts can review immigration matters. The district court disagreed and rejected each provision in turn.

 


The first provision,

8 U.S.C. § 1252(b)(9)

, is often called the “zipper clause.” It bars federal courts from hearing challenges that arise from efforts to deport someone, except through review of an individual’s final removal order. The government

claimed

 the zipper clause applies here because our lawsuit is really an effort to stop it from initiating adverse immigration actions.

 


 The district court wholly rejected this argument. Relying on the Second Circuit’s decision in

Ozturk v. Hyde

, it held that the zipper clause bars only challenges to a particular individual’s removal proceedings, not a lawsuit like ours that challenges the constitutionality of the surveillance program itself. That the surveillance program might affect someone’s immigration proceeding down the line doesn’t turn our lawsuit into a removal challenge.

 


 The court similarly rejected the government’s argument that

§ 1252(g)

 and

§ 1252(f)(1)

 prevent federal courts from hearing this case. Our suit, the court explained, “challenges the constitutionality of a government policy that is collateral to any active removal proceedings,” so § 1252(g) doesn’t apply. And § 1252(f)(1) only limits what kind of relief a court can give. So while the court may not be able to stop a particular person’s removal proceedings, it can still block “an unlawful surveillance program that suppresses free speech.”

author: Ed Wanderley
title: A misoginia de diálogos de Vorcaro e CEO que expôs atrizes: “Mulher não pode fazer isso”
content:
Com a boca vermelha e a pele totalmente pintada de verde, Deborah Secco adentrou o Baile da Vogue de 2024, no Copacabana Palace, alternando entre sorrisos fartos e carão carregado nos olhares sensuais, um combo recorrente que já virou tradição no evento, no qual é convidada de destaque. A atriz encarnava um ser extraterrestre de roupas curtas, brancas, com direito a um bebê alien a tiracolo, no estilo carnavalesco típico da celebração, uma das grandes apostas publicitárias da Vogue Brasil e da Editora Globo nas semanas que antecedem o Carnaval.


Mas enquanto posava para os fotógrafos de dezenas de publicações e curtia a festa com sua tradicional animação, Deborah, que dividia o espaço com a nata executiva do Grupo Globo, estava desavisada do julgamento de alguns dos presentes mais relevantes do evento.

“Eu só olhava pra bunda dela rs”. As palavras são do então diretor-geral de mídias impressas e rádios da Editora Globo, Frederick Kachar, para o dono do Banco Master, Daniel Vorcaro, horas depois. “Mas tava muito feia kkk”, rebateu o banqueiro. “Concordo que a fantasia era broxante”, completou Kachar.

 “Tá doido, mulher não pode fazer isso”, disparou Vorcaro.


Os diálogos fazem parte de um conjunto de mensagens interceptadas pela Polícia Federal (PF), entre outubro de 2023 e julho de 2025, cujo vazamento ganhou força nesta semana e levou à demissão do executivo de mídia nesta quinta-feira (15). Em nota, o Grupo Globo não menciona o conteúdo misógino das mensagens como um dos motivos da demissão, mas sim a preservação da independência editorial da Editora Globo.


Nota na íntegra


Grupo Globo comunica desligamento de Frederic Kachar e reforça independência editorial de seus veículos.


O Grupo Globo comunicou hoje o desligamento do diretor-geral de Mídia Impressa e Rádio, Frederic Kachar. O conteúdo das conversas privadas mantidas com Daniel Vorcaro entre outubro de 2023 e julho de 2025, às quais a empresa teve acesso ontem, revela uma relação inadequada do executivo com um anunciante.


A Editora Globo reforça seu compromisso com a ética e a transparência e reafirma a absoluta independência editorial do jornalismo de seus veículos, premissa essencial de sua atuação. O protagonismo da cobertura crítica, isenta e independente que tem feito do caso Master é a demonstração concreta do compromisso inegociável de seus veículos com os Princípios Editoriais do Grupo Globo.


A empresa reconhece os 29 anos de dedicação de Kachar ao desenvolvimento de seus negócios de mídia e informa que o nome de seu substituto à frente da Editora Globo e do Sistema Globo de Rádio será divulgado em breve.


Comunicação Globo

Rio de Janeiro, 15 de outubro de 2026

Mais informações:

https://imprensa.globo.com/


Além de comentários objetificando atrizes ligadas ao próprio Grupo Globo, o conteúdo revela comentários machistas e convites mútuos para festas com mulheres, discrição “sem celular” e encontros descritos como idas à “Ucrânia”.


Um baile de machismo


“Muita mulher pro crime e só gay. Elas tavam dando em cima mesmo acompanhado”, foi assim que Fred Kachar descreveu o ambiente do evento da revista até então sob sua responsabilidade. E completou: “Me fodi. Minha ex foi e marcou em cima”. A ex em questão é a atriz Monique Alfradique, que também chegou a se envolver com Daniel Vorcaro meses depois. “No final não teve jeito. Marcação cerrada”, escreveu ainda. Alfradique não quis se pronunciar sobre os conteúdos das mensagens até a publicação desta reportagem.


“Deborah secco tava pra jogo”, escreveu Kachar. O executivo da Globo ainda relata que a atriz seria madrinha do camarote do Grupo no Carnaval do Rio de Janeiro e teria dito querer “curtir solteira” nos festejos. “Relação aberta. Preciso de uma dessas”

, escreveu Kachar. “Todos nós”, respondeu Vorcaro.


A assessoria de Déborah Secco repudiou a associação indevida do nome da atriz a comentários de teor machista, desrespeitoso e irresponsável, disse que a atriz não conhece Daniel Vorcaro e que sua relação com Fred Kachar sempre foi estritamente profissional. “Tiveram encontros em trabalhos, onde foram fotografados, sem qualquer vínculo entre eles”. A equipe da atriz também destacou que os comentários que se tornaram públicos diz respeito a um evento “onde ambas estavam trabalhando”.


“É inadmissível expor a imagem e a reputação de uma mulher com base em uma narrativa que não corresponde à sua realidade. Também é lamentável a forma como mulheres foram mencionadas, em comentários …

author: Christopher Cartwright
title: As Resistance to Flock Cameras Grows, Another Surveillance Network Is Spreading
content:
Fusus software is being used in at least 324 US communities, with nearly 624,000 cameras connected to a Fusus network.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

More than 28,000 cameras in Atlanta are integrated into a “real-time crime center,” allowing police live access to many of their video streams. In Hawthorne, California, the city surveillance network includes more than 3,700 cameras. And in Seat Pleasant, Maryland — a town of 4,500 — police have access to one integrated camera for every three residents.

These communities are among hundreds in the U.S. that have adopted Fusus, a surveillance platform that allows police to watch live camera networks in their jurisdictions. While local resistance to Flock Safety automated license plate readers has swept the nation — including vandalism of cameras, cities canceling contracts, and a recent national week of action organized by the group DeFlock — the Fusus software has continued to spread.

Owned by Axon, the company behind Tasers and body-worn cameras, Fusus enables police to link security cameras, automated license plate readers, doorbell cameras, police dash cameras, drones, and body-worn cameras to a central hub that can use AI, according to the company’s website. The software’s distinction is its ability to integrate privately owned cameras from individuals, organizations, and businesses, whose participation the company encourages through its voluntary Community Connect program.

A Prism analysis of public information obtained from Axon’s website and the Fusus application programming interfaces (APIs) shows that the software is being used in at least 324 U.S. communities, with nearly 624,000 cameras connected to a Fusus network. These range from rural areas — such as Plaquemines Parish in Louisiana and Artesia, New Mexico — to major cities, including Dallas, Seattle, Miami, and New York City.

Privacy advocates and community organizers say this integrated system rapidly expands the reach of police power. Ed Vogel, a co-founder of Southerners Against Surveillance Systems and Infrastructure, argued that the Fusus business model inherently encourages additional surveillance.

“Anyone who is concerned about Flock safety and license plate readers should be equally concerned with Axon and Fusus,” he said. “Fusus is a tool that invites the police to build out a surveillance apparatus in order to optimize the technology. Because it’s a software that integrates a variety of surveillance tools into it, in order to make the most of it, the police want to and will try to acquire more technology so that they can integrate more tools.”

Data obtained from the APIs include the number of registered, integrated, owned, shared, and subscribed cameras. Registered cameras are those submitted to a police-maintained database. This doesn’t give law enforcement live access to each camera feed, but allows them to create a network map for future investigations. Integrated cameras are those that give police live access, and Axon’s Fusus manual says police can share these video streams with other law enforcement agencies.

Axon did not respond to multiple requests for comment or clarification on the definitions of owned, shared, and subscribed cameras. On its website’s FAQ page, the company says Fusus “promotes ethical policing by improving the accuracy of suspect identification, helping reduce reliance on potentially biased eyewitness accounts.”

In May 2023, the Electronic Frontier Foundation reported that nearly 150 jurisdictions used Fusus. That number has more than doubled since, according to Prism’s analysis of Fusus API data.

Georgia leads the nation in integrated cameras, with more than 275,000. An Axon-run website urging people to register and integrate cameras into the Atlanta police system, called Connect Atlanta, shows that the city has 29,855 integrated cameras, the most of any Fusus network, as of Oct. 15. Sandy Springs, Georgia, has the second-most at 16,415.

The Illinois State Police, the only state agency publicly reporting that it uses Fusus, has integrated more than 4,100 cameras. Three public universities — the University of Illinois, the University of Missouri and the University of Arizona — also use the technology.

author: Unknown
title: İstanbul: Selde can kaybı 4'e yükseldi, 5 kişi de kayıp
content:
İstanbul Valisi Davut Gül, 15 Ekim akşamüstü yaptığı açıklamada 3 kişinin yaşamını yitirdiğini, 5 kişi için kayıp başvurusu yapıldığını bildirdi. Gül'ün açıklamasının ardından Beykoz'da işçi Faik Şentürk'ün ölüm haberi geldi. 


Vali Gül, kurtarma ve sağlık çalışmalarına ilişkin şu bilgileri paylaştı: 


“7 hemşehrimiz tedavisi bittikten sonra taburcu oldu, 5 kişiyle ilgili kayıp başvurusu yapıldı. Arama çalışmaları devam ediyor.”


Gül, kentin normalleşmeye başladığını, hasar tespit çalışmalarının sürdüğünü ve zarar gören yurttaşlara ödemelerin en geç pazartesi günü başlatılacağını söyledi. 


84 yılın yağış rekoru kırıldı, 3 bin 50 kişi kurtarıldı


İçişleri Bakanı Mustafa Çiftçi, İstanbul'da yağışın bazı bölgelerde metrekareye

272 kilograma

 ulaştığını açıkladı. İstanbul Valisi Davut Gül ise kentin 1942'den bu yana kaydedilen en yoğun yağışla karşı karşıya kaldığını söyledi.


Vali Gül'ün akşam saatlerinde verdiği bilgiye göre selde mahsur kalan 3 bin 50 kişi kurtarıldı. Kurtarılmayı bekleyen kimse kalmadığını belirten Gül, kayıp başvurusu yapılan 5 kişinin aranmasına devam edildiğini bildirdi. 


İstanbul'da 16 Ekim Cuma günü de okullarda eğitime ara verilecek. Erdoğan, sağanağın devam edeceğine ilişkin tahminler nedeniyle yurttaşlardan resmi uyarıları izlemelerini istedi. 


838 sigortalı hasar ihbarı


Türkiye Sigorta Birliği (TSB), 15 Ekim itibarıyla İstanbul'da sel ve su baskınları nedeniyle sigorta şirketlerine 838 hasar ihbarı yapıldığını açıkladı. Bunların 776'sı yangın sigortası, 62'si kasko kapsamında kaydedildi.


TSB Başkanı Ahmet Yaşar, Bursa, Kocaeli ve Yalova'daki başvurularla birlikte toplam ihbar sayısının 897'ye ulaştığını belirterek şöyle dedi:


“Bunlar, henüz ilk bildirimler. Önümüzdeki günlerde yeni ihbarların gelmesi ve ekspertiz çalışmalarının ilerlemesiyle hasarın gerçek boyutu daha net ortaya çıkacaktır.”


İstanbul Valisi Davut Gül de hasar tespit çalışmalarının sürdüğünü, selden zarar gören yurttaşlara yapılacak ödemelerin mümkünse cuma öğleden sonra, en geç 19 Ekim Pazartesi başlayacağını bildirdi.


Barajlarda bir günde 7,16 puan doluluk artışı


İstanbul Su ve Kanalizasyon İdaresi'nin (İSKİ) 15 Ekim saat 09.14'te yayımladığı verilere göre, bir gün önce yüzde 38,06 olarak ölçülen kente su sağlayan barajlardaki ortalama doluluk oranı  yüzde 45,22'ye çıktı.


Elmalı Barajı yüzde 100 doluluğa ulaşırken, doluluk Istrancalar 'da yüzde 84,2, Alibey'de yüzde 68,13, Darlık'ta yüzde 67,74 ve Ömerli'de yüzde 62,17 seviyesine yükseldi.


Diğer barajlardaki doluluk oranları Terkos'ta yüzde 34,64, Büyükçekmece'de yüzde 29,02, Sazlıdere'de yüzde 27,47, Kazandere'de yüzde 8,28 ve Pabuçdere'de yüzde 3,41 olarak kaydedildi.


Yağış öncesinde Elmalı Barajı'nın doluluğu yüzde 77,79 olarak  ölçülmüştü.


Elmalı Barajı tamamen doldu: Taşkın tehlikesi var mı?


Elmalı Barajı'nın yüzde 100 dolması, barajın yıkılma veya denetimsiz taşma tehlikesi altında olduğu anlamına gelmez. Barajların olağan su tahliye sistemleri bulunuyor. Ancak güvenliğin değerlendirilmesi için doluluk oranının yanında baraja gelen su miktarı, dolusavak kapasitesi ve aşağı havzadaki akış koşullarının da bilinmesi gerekiyor.


(AEK)

author: Amy Goodman
title: Regulation Should Target AI’s Current Harms, Not Superintelligence Possibilities
content:
A mix of science fiction and delusion distracts from the real harms that we’re seeing, says tech journalist Paris Marx.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

We speak with tech journalist Paris Marx about his new book, Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires. In the book, Marx exposes the deceptive ways tech companies are taking resources from vulnerable communities in order to build massive AI data centers. “We have seen the tech companies that, back in 2019, 2020, wanted us to see them as climate leaders … completely throw their targets out the window in order to pursue generative AI and this data center buildout,” says Marx. He notes that after failing to connect to electrical grids in the locations where they were building data centers, some AI companies have pivoted to building “on-site gas plants,” further increasing dependency on fossil fuels.

Tech companies “want us to believe” that AI models are “starting to become so powerful that within 10 years they could decide that they want to wipe out humanity or a significant chunk of humanity,” says Marx. “That is a mix of science fiction and delusion … and it is also a very effective way to distract from the real harms that we’re seeing from these generative AI products.”

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

AMY GOODMAN: This is Democracy Now! I’m Amy Goodman, with Nermeen Shaikh.

NERMEEN SHAIKH: With the midterms less than three weeks away, we continue to look at how AI data centers have emerged as a political flashpoint.

AMY GOODMAN: We’re joined now by the Canadian journalist Paris Marx, host of the award-winning Tech Won’t Save Us podcast, writes the Disconnect newsletter, author of the new book Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires. He’s joining us from St. John’s, Newfoundland.

And we just talked to Justin Pearson, taking on Elon Musk’s xAI data centers in Memphis. In fact, though, the largest concentration of data centers is in northern Virginia, as you write about. And Nermeen and I are speaking to you from New York, which has the only state moratorium on the building of data centers. Can you give us — can you put that battle in Memphis in the global picture? Why northern Virginia, for example, is there this massive concentration of data centers? It’s not one of the poorest areas in the country.

PARIS MARX: No, certainly not. It’s much more for historical reasons, right? Because a lot of that early work on the internet was happening in northern Virginia, you know, obviously, a lot of military spending that went into that. And, of course, for that reason, a lot of infrastructure, a lot of, you know, fiber infrastructure, connectivity infrastructure, data centers, certainly, over time, were built out in that area. And that, you know, kind of — that legacy continues to this day.

And so, you know, the people who live there in northern Virginia have really felt the effects of all of these data centers having been built out. And especially, you know, they have had data centers for a long time — right? — but one of the things I try to get to in the book is really the shift from data centers as they used to be, you know, in industrial areas, maybe not so much larger than other tenants that would be in those, you know, kind of industrial parks and things like that, to the hyperscale data centers that are just on a whole other scale. You know, the resource demands are just immense, as, of course, you know, Representative Justin Pearson was just talking about in Memphis, where they have really been feeling this firsthand. And I think, you know, because Elon Musk was involved, this really brought it to the attention of a lot more people, seeing the effects that come with one of these major data centers. But, obviously, in northern Virginia, people are feeling a lot of that.

But as we have seen this significant escalation in the construction of these hyperscale data centers, particularly in the past four to five years, and certainly since the generative AI boom really started to take off in 2023, we have seen not just many more communities in the United States seeing data centers planned or being constructed next to them, and feeling, you know, what comes with that, whether that is the increases in their electricity prices, the pressures on their water system, or just, you know …

author: Daron Letts
title: Taloyoak’s new Pangniq High School unveiled with public ceremony
content:
Metalshop students at Taloyoak’s new $90-million Pangniq High School crafted the qulliq that will be lit at an unveiling ceremony set for Friday.


The school overlooks the community from atop a raised plot of ground next to the airport.


Its stature in the landscape is mirrored by its name —  pangniq, an Inuktitut term for the most prominent bull in a caribou herd. Students helped choose that name as part of a contest last year.


“The school is outstanding — state of the art,” said first-year principal Rodney Drover Wednesday in a phone interview.


The school’s 16 staff members and 200 students from grades 7 to 12 began their fall semester in the 3,300-square-metre facility for the first time since

construction

, which was completed on schedule, began in 2023.


It’s the fifth school completed by Iqaluit-based general contractor Pilitak Enterprises Ltd., Winnipeg-based Accutech Engineering Inc., and Parkin Architects, which has offices in Ontario and B.C.


The building blends traditional learning with technology that includes smartboards, microphone systems, and screens in every classroom, Drover said.


“There’s not much that we don’t have,” he said, adding that the

 science lab is “what you would expect to find in a university.”


There’s also a culinary training facility and processing room, in which elders can lead students through lessons in skinning and breaking down country food.


Early in the semester, students used the brand-new stoves to cook muskox recipes. On Wednesday, they prepared seal dishes to serve at Friday’s public event.


The shop, overseen by instructor Bill Akerly, is equipped for carpentry, electrical, welding and other trades.


The building is designed to accommodate more than 400 students.


Friday’s ceremony includes two bands, accordian jigs, throatsinging and drumdancing.


The gymnasium at Taloyoak’s new Pangniq High School is set up in anticipation of Friday’s public unveiling, which Premier John Main is expected to attend. (Photo courtesy of Rodney Drover)


Those on Friday’s guest list, which will include Nunavut Premier John Main and other MLAs, will be greeted by the natural light that floods into the foyer through large banks of north- and east-facing windows.


Guests will be led on a private tour before doors open to the public at 2 p.m. A community feast is scheduled to follow at 3:30 p.m.


“[The school is] a wonderful gift to the community and, more importantly, the students,” Drover said.

title: Cómplices: quiénes son los diputados peronistas y de otros bloques que salvaron a Milei y al DNU 70/23
content:
Este jueves finalmente no hubo quórum para tratar en Diputados el DNU 70/23, así como tampoco emergencia en dispacidad y endeudamiento. Conocé uno por uno quiénes fueron los diputados que resultaron claves para impedir esta sesión.

 Por La Izquierda Diario.


Cuando el reloj marcó las 14:30 hs, quedó claro que este jueves no habría quórum para tratar el DNU 70/23, emergencia en discapacidad y endeudamiento familiar. El decreto, en particular, fue una herramienta fundacional de La Libertad Avanza que avanzó con desregulaciones a favor del mercado en múltiples áreas y favorece desde hace casi 3 años al lloby inmobiliario, de las prepagas, farmaceúticas y otros, afectando gravemente la vida de las mayorías populares.


En ese horario se llegó apenas a 121 presentes. Faltaron apenas 8 para el quórum. Los faltazos que ayudaron al gobierno de Milei y al poder económico fueron transversales y comprometieron a varios gobernadores del PJ, de los ex Juntos por el Cambio y hasta integrantes de Unión por la Patria.


Uno por uno, los responsables claves de no haber dado quórum fueron los 3 tucumanos del PJ de Osvaldo Jaldo (Medina, Noguera y Fernández), 1 de Salta de Gustavo Sáenz (Vega), 1 de Córdoba de Llaryora (Torres) , 2 jujeños de la UCR de Sadir (Rizzotti y Zigarán), 1 misionero de Passalaqcua (Vancsik), 2 santafesinos que respoden a Pullaro (Scaglia y Núñez). Además hubo 2 ausencias de Unión por la Patria: Neder de Santiago del Estero y Tita de Tierra del Fuego. En el caso de Santiago del Estero, hay más sospechas porque su gobernador Zamora ha dado colaboración a Milei en otras oportunidades. También jugaron a favor del gobierno de Milei los diputados del gobernador de Chubut Torres del PRO (Avila) y la de Neuquén de Rolando Figueroa (Maureira).


Diputados. Hubo 121 sentados. Faltaron 8 para el quórum de gobernadores de Tucumán (3), Salta (1), Jujuy (2), Misiones (1), Córdoba (1), Santa Fe (2), Chubut (1), Neuquén (1). Y 2 de Unión por la Patria (de Santiago Del Estero y Tierra del Fuego) https://t.co/uetPVGD3vs

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Tells MAGA Audience Leakers Should “Be Shot”
content:
Trump has a long history of deriding leakers and the press, accusing those who publish leaked stories of “treason.”

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump said Wednesday that anyone leaking information out of his own White House should face execution, in an escalation of violent rhetoric against leakers and journalists.

“Somebody leaked, some sleazebag. They ought to go to jail or be shot,” Trump told the audience.

Speaking at a campaign rally in Arizona on Wednesday, Trump framed his remarks in terms of the start of the war with Iran, “when they leak what time you’re going to attack a country,” the president said. However, no such “leak” has been confirmed to have occurred at that point in time.

After the war began, a White House leak revealed assessments from U.S. Defense intelligence that contradicted the president’s public claims about the impacts of initial strikes on Iran.

“The leakers should be dealt with very, very strongly. … To me, they’re the scum of the Earth,” the president added at the rally.

Trump: "In my opinion, leakers should be shot. In the old days we used to shoot leakers."

Trump also directed his ire against the free press, expressing disdain for journalists over their reporting on leaks from the White House.

“They’re almost as bad as a leaker,” Trump said.

Trump has previously attacked leakers within his own administration, bemoaning the publication of previously hidden information that casts him or others in his orbit in a negative light. In April, he threatened reporters with jail for reporting on details of a rescue mission near the start of the war.

“We have to find that leaker, because that’s a sick person. … The person that did the story will go to jail if he doesn’t say,” Trump said at the time.

In August, Trump threatened “leakers” with treason charges, stating in a Truth Social post that “Long term jail sentences will be sought!”

Treason is a charge punishable by death.

Reporting on leaks is critical for holding government officials accountable. The Pentagon Papers case in the 1970s, for example, divulged how “lies were the foundation of U.S. policy” in the lead-up to and during the Vietnam War, according to an explainer from Freedom of the Press Foundation.

The Pentagon Papers leak established an important Supreme Court precedent on press freedom, ensuring that government entities had to overcome a “very heavy burden” to deny publications of their right to print leaks for the public to see, including in instances involving national security or wartime secrets. Trump’s suggestion that leakers (and the press) should be jailed or even shot for their actions infringes on the right guaranteed by that decades-old precedent.

Truthout is one of only a few platforms for justice-oriented, grassroots journalism. Today, we face an existential threat.

Due to Google’s launch of AI search, we’ve seen a drastic plunge in our site traffic and, as a result, our revenue. We lost 15 percent of our readership overnight. This was a readership we painstakingly built over decades, and it vanished because Google chose corporate greed over a healthy democracy.

We are fundraising right now to meet our basic operating expenses. If you can support Truthout with a one-time or monthly donation, you will make a significant impact on our work. Anything you can do makes a difference — we appreciate your support.

author: Dyepeson Martins
title: Chefe da campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro esteve no Senado mas não votou na 6×1
content:
Enquanto governistas discursavam a favor do projeto que estabelecia o fim da escala de trabalho 6×1, parlamentares da oposição se reuniam para debater estratégias e discursos da campanha do senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) à Presidência da República. A reunião durou mais de três horas e aconteceu no gabinete do líder do PL no Senado Federal e chefe da campanha de Flávio, Rogério Marinho (RN), que não compareceu ao plenário nem participou da votação da proposta —

aprovada na noite de quarta-feira (14), como mostrou a

Agência Pública

.

 Procurado pela reportagem, Marinho não retornou até a publicação. 


Discussão e votação, em primeiro turno, da proposta de emenda à Constituição que acaba com a escala 6×1


Outros dois aliados de Flávio também não votaram: os senadores Sérgio Moro (PL-PR) e Marcio Bittar (PL-AC). O presidente do Congresso Nacional, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), que presidiu a sessão, não votou. Pelas regras do regimento interno do Senado, o presidente não vota. Entretanto, a norma permite que o parlamentar entregue o comando da Casa a outro senador para que este participe da votação. O texto foi aprovado em dois turnos por 75 votos a favor e um voto contrário: o do ex-vice-presidente da República, Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS). 


O senador Hamilton Mourão (Republicanos-RS) foi o único parlamentar a votar contra a PEC que acaba com a escala de trabalho 6×1 no Senado


Rogério Marinho é autor da Proposta de Emenda à Constituição (PEC), apresentada em maio deste ano, que prevê uma jornada por regime de horas trabalhadas — alternativa da oposição à PEC que estabeleceu o fim da escala 6×1. Flávio Bolsonaro e seus aliados sempre se posicionaram contra a redução da jornada de trabalho sem impacto nos salários, por considerarem que isso representaria prejuízos econômicos à indústria. No entanto, diante da campanha governista e da mobilização popular em favor da proposta, Flávio recuou e afirmou que votaria a favor da aprovação do texto. A mudança foi anunciada na terça-feira (13), após ele visitar o pai, o ex-presidente Jair Bolsonaro, que cumpre prisão domiciliar por tentativa de golpe de Estado. 


Flávio Bolsonaro trocou a votação sobre o fim da escala 6×1 no Senado por um ato de campanha em Porto Alegre


O novo discurso foi reforçado durante a reunião no gabinete de Rogério Marinho. Além dele, três correligionários do PL estavam no encontro: os senadores Magno Malta (ES), Carlos Portinho (RJ) e o eleito José Medeiros (MT). Também estavam presentes três congressistas do PP: a senadora e ex-ministra da Agricultura de Jair Bolsonaro, Tereza Cristina (MS); o senador eleito e ex-presidente da Câmara dos Deputados, Arthur Lira (AL); e o deputado federal Ricardo Barros (PR), ministro da Saúde na gestão de Michel Temer. 


“A gente não pode deixar a narrativa nas mãos do adversário”, declarou à

Pública

, sob reserva, um dos membros da reunião a respeito da mudança no discurso da campanha a menos de duas semanas para o segundo turno das eleições. “Foi uma decisão do presidente [Flávio] e o Lira também concordou”, completou o parlamentar. 


Questionado pela

Pública

 após sair da reunião, Lira afirmou que não foi ao gabinete para tratar da PEC em votação.


Flávio Bolsonaro votou à distância enquanto participava de um ato político em Porto Alegre, no Rio Grande do Sul. Ele subiu ao palanque ao lado dos governadores eleitos Luciano Zucco (PL-RS) e Sérgio Moro (PL-PR); e dos governadores reeleitos Jorginho Mello (PL-SC) e Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos-SP). Na ocasião, afirmou aos apoiadores que o governo terá que “pagar a conta” do novo modelo de trabalho para compensar empresários que, segundo ele, estariam “quebrados”.


Senado conservador: “não teremos medo de realizar todas as mudanças necessárias”


Aliados de Flávio confirmaram à

Pública

 que a campanha se reuniu, ao longo do último mês, com empresários para discutir as possíveis consequências da implantação da nova jornada de trabalho. A transição de 44 para 40 horas semanais será gradual e começará a valer dois meses após a promulgação da PEC —  função do presidente do Congresso. Durante o primeiro ano da nova regra, a jornada terá um limite de 42 horas. Após esse período, o limite passará a ser oficialmente de 40 horas. 


Diante disso, Flávio sinalizou ao setor empresarial que, caso eleito, pretende aplicar medidas “compensatórias”; entre elas, propostas legislativas que revertam os efeitos do fim da escala 6×1. As ações seriam possíveis …

title: Kurdish Conference: The Kurdish question must be placed at the center of EU relations
content:
A session titled “The European Union, Turkey and the Kurds: Between Strategic Partnership and Democratic Expectations” was held as part of a Kurdish conference at the European Parliament.


The session was moderated by Hişyar Özsoy, a former member of parliament for the HDP (Peoples’ Democratic Party).


Speakers at the session included Li Andersson, a Finnish Member of the European Parliament and member of The Left group; Pernando Barrena, a Spanish MEP from The Left group; Vladimir Prebilič, a Slovenian representative from the Greens/European Free Alliance; Raziye Öztürk of the Asrın Law Office; and Eleonora Scala, a member of the International Bar Association’s Human Rights Institute from the United Kingdom.


The full conference can be watched here 


https://left.eu/events/20th-international-conference-the-european-union-turkey-the-middle-east-and-the-kurds/

left.eu


Li Andersson, in her remarks, drew particular attention to the European Union’s silence and inaction in the face of authoritarian regimes, stressing that resolving the Kurdish issue must be placed at the center of EU–Turkey relations.


Eleonora Scala shared several observations on behalf of the Independent Legal Mission for the Peace Process in Turkey, of which she is a member.


The mission was established under the auspices of the European Association of Lawyers for Democracy and World Human Rights (ELDH) and the Association for Democracy and International Law (MAD).


Raziye Öztürk of the Asrın Law Office said, “We are going through a process of historic importance,” adding: “We are at a stage where we are discussing whether it is possible to bring an end to a conflict that has continued for many years and to resolve the Kurdish question through democratic and political means. Yet, despite this major change, unfortunately, we still have to talk about the right to hope and, in connection with it, Europe’s policy towards Turkey and the Kurds.


This is because, as I will explain shortly with concrete examples, it is almost impossible to say that Europe has made any changes to its approach towards the Kurds.”
