author: Jim McIlroy
title: ‘Wall of Tears’ memorialises Gaza’s lost children
content:
The Wall of Tears exhibition, memorialising the 18,500 children officially recorded as killed by Israeli forces over two years in Gaza from October 7, 2023, opened at the Pitt Street Uniting Church, in Sydney, on October 9.

The exhibition is supported by Amnesty International Australia (AIA) and Palestinian Christians in Australia. The 15-metre-long artwork is on loan from Perth Doctors Medical Aid for Palestine and is open to the public until October 28.

The Wall of Tears lists the names of children killed in Gaza between October 7, 2023, and July 19, 2025, alongside photographs and stories.

Barbara Gorman, convenor of AIA's Pennant Hills Action Group, told Green Left that the exhibition “confronts us with the human reality behind the devastating number of children killed in Gaza. Every name on this Wall represents a child, a life, a family and a future.

“We hope that by bringing the Wall to Sydney, people will take the time to see those names, reflect on the scale of this loss and remember the children behind the numbers.”

Created by United States artist Phil Buehler, the Wall was first displayed in Brooklyn, New York, in January. A replica was later brought to Australia and has been displayed in Western Australia and on the lawns of Parliament House in Canberra.

“If you approach from a distance, it looks almost like an abstract painting and that draws people in to see, what is that?” Buehler explained. “Then you’ll see they are names of the children killed in Gaza since October 7 and there are thousands of them...

“You see these faces full of joy and hope, snapshots from graduations and birthday parties and family gatherings and knowing that these kids’ lives were just cut short.

“I hope that might lead people to think about how they might help, even if it’s just, tak[ing] a photo of the mural and pass[ing] it along on their social media or to their friends.”

Guest speakers at the moving Sydney launch included international human rights lawyer Chris Sidoti; Dr Saira Hussain, four-time volunteer doctor in Gaza; and Suzan Wahhab, president of Palestinian Christians in Australia. Other speakers included representatives of Muslim, Christian, Jewish and Hindu faiths.

Sidoti told the audience, which numbered more than 100: "The Wall of Tears is about hope, not just tears. In singling out a list of individual children who were killed in Gaza, the Wall shows the true identity of these children, not just names."

Importantly, said Sidoti, the Wall lists children who have died directly from Israeli military attacks, not those who died of starvation and disease, or whose bodies have not been recovered so far.

Dr Hussain said: "Many more Palestinians in Gaza will die unless the Israeli attacks are stopped. This exhibition is part of the essential movement to end the Israeli genocide in Palestine.”

[Visit the Amnesty Internation Pennant Hills Action Group's website for opening hours.]

author: Sonali Kolhatkar
title: New Mexico’s Challenges Hold Lessons for the Struggle for Universal Child Care
content:
New Mexico is finding out that successfully providing universal child care requires giving teachers a living wage.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The state of New Mexico in 2025 made headlines for being the first in the nation to enact free universal child care. A 12-year-long grassroots push by advocacy groups and activists to address the dismal state of child well-being resulted in Gov. Michele Lujan Grisham signing a bill to expand eligibility for no-cost, government-provided child care to all the state’s residents, regardless of income.

It was a historic bill, one that paved the way for New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani to enact a similar program.

According to the Santa Fe New Mexican, enrollment in New Mexico’s government-provided child care centers jumped over the past year, with 15,000 new enrollees recorded since the program was launched. But waitlists are also growing as demand rapidly outpaces supply. And dire stories are emerging, such as Vox Media’s June 2026 story headlined “How to Screw Up Universal Childcare.”

Expanding free child care to meet growing need isn’t as simple as opening new facilities and enrolling families. Early childhood education requires well-trained staff who are paid generously enough to remain on the job. And that appears to be the biggest obstacle to fully realizing New Mexico’s pioneering program and ensuring that all those who need child care get it.

A June 2026 report by the child advocacy group New Mexico Voices for Children (NM Voices), examined every aspect of child well-being in the state including “early childhood education” — which is the term preferred by advocates to describe child care. The report concluded that, in spite of great strides, New Mexico was falling short in serving the families who need most help, and urged policy makers to “build on recent progress by strengthening the early childhood workforce, expanding access to high-quality programs and ensuring students receive the academic and social supports they need to succeed.”

Enrollment in New Mexico’s government-provided child care centers jumped over the past year, with 15,000 new enrollees recorded.

Matthew Henderson, executive director of OLÉ Education Fund, which helps organize child care workers, underscored how “the universal child care system is definitely something to celebrate, and we do celebrate it because it has given thousands of parents free child care, saving them tens of thousands of dollars.” And Gov. Lujan Grisham, who leaves office at the end of the year, has pinned her legacy to New Mexico’s early childhood education program and hopes it offers a model for the rest of the nation. She told the Associated Press, “My hope is, as we watch elections take hold around the country, that our congressional candidates are talking about these investments, our gubernatorial candidates are talking about these investments” in child care.

And yet, according to Henderson, “there are still parents who can’t access [the program] because the administration has not been smart about how to grow the state’s capacity.”

Child care workers, who are disproportionately low-income women of color, and who are charged with caring for the most vulnerable members of society, are also egregiously underpaid. Although New Mexico’s early educators are now compensated as much as $16-$19 an hour — which is higher than the state’s $12-an-hour minimum wage — it’s not nearly enough to prevent constant turnover and worker shortages.

The New Mexico Early Childhood Education and Care Department (ECECD), which is the government agency overseeing the state’s child care centers, announced a “wage and career lattice” for employees “to support long-term recruitment and retention.” Henderson lauded the approach as “really excellent,” but accused the administration of “slow-walking any attempts to implement professional compensation for the workforce.”

Teresa Madrid, executive director of a New Mexico-based advocacy organization called Partnership for Community Action agreed, telling the Santa Fe New Mexican that the “wage and career lattice is something that has been part of ECECD’s strategic plan for the last several years, and we are now in 2026 with no implementation, no action and no dollars committed to that wage and career lattice.”

title: Resistance against geothermal project in Varto: Court schedules site inspection for November
content:
Resistance against a planned geothermal power plant in the village of Xwarik in the Varto district of Muş province continues. For 165 days, local residents have maintained a protest vigil against the project proposed by the US-based company IGNIS H2 Energy. As the protests continue, the Administrative Court in Bingöl has set a new date for a court-ordered expert inspection of the project site.


Local residents filed a lawsuit against the power plant project on April 9, requesting a suspension of its implementation. On July 21, the court ordered an on-site inspection and the preparation of an expert report. After objections were raised to the inspection initially scheduled for October 8 over the need for a suitably qualified geophysicist, the inspection was postponed to November 2. The project site in the neighboring district of Karlıova is also scheduled to be examined on the same day.


DBP joins protest vigil


The protest vigil, initiated by the Youth Council of the Varto Ecology Platform, is being supported by different groups on a rotating basis. On the 164th day of protests, the local branch of the Democratic Regions Party (DBP) took over the vigil. A banner displayed by the protesters reads: “The people of Varto do not want a geothermal power plant. Hands off our water and our land.”


Aziz Oral, co-chair of the DBP district branch in Varto, welcomed the upcoming court inspection and reaffirmed his party’s support for the resistance. He said the ongoing destruction of nature was the result of policies pursued for years at the expense of ecological livelihoods.


“For us, ecology is not an issue that can be postponed. It concerns not only the future but also the present. When nature is damaged, it affects every aspect of our lives,” Oral stated.


“The struggle against the power plant project is therefore not merely a local issue. It also concerns people who have moved from Varto to major cities. We do not see the ecological struggle as separate from the struggle for life,” Oral said, announcing that the DBP would continue to actively participate in the protests. Meanwhile, the protest vigil in Xwarik continues, with supporters visiting in solidarity.

title: Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî sentenced to more than five years in prison
content:
Kurdish politician and former co-chair of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî (Lahur Sheikh Jangi Talabani), has been sentenced to five years and three months in prison by a court in Sulaymaniyah. His lawyer confirmed the verdict to the news outlet The New Region on Thursday. Talabanî’s brother Polad was also sentenced to three years and six months in prison. The court handed down a two-year prison sentence to their close associate Rebwar Hamid Haci Gali.


Power struggle within the PUK


The case stems from a long-running power struggle within the PUK, one of the two dominant governing parties in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI). Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî led the party alongside Bafel Talabanî until he was removed from power in 2021. The two are cousins, and Bafel Talabanî remains the leader of the PUK. Another cousin, Qubad Talabanî, serves as deputy prime minister of the Kurdistan Region.


Following his removal from the party leadership, Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî founded the opposition People’s Front (Bereyî Gel). In August 2025, PUK-affiliated security forces deployed tanks and drones to arrest the politician at his residence in the Lalezar Hotel in Sulaymaniyah. The operation triggered hours of heavy fighting in a residential area of the city. According to official figures, two members of Talabanî’s staff and three members of the PUK security forces were killed. Other reports indicate a higher death toll.


Defense calls for an independent trial


Following the clashes, Lahur Şêx Cengî Talabanî, his brother Polad, and numerous others were arrested. A total of 27 people detained in connection with the fighting remain in prison. The trial had been repeatedly postponed since then.


Talabanî’s defense team had requested that the proceedings be transferred to Hewlêr (Erbil), where they believed a more transparent and fair trial could be held. His lawyers also criticized alleged human rights violations against detained members of his security team.

title: Kurdish Conference: Conditions for Abdullah Öcalan to work freely must be established
content:
The final session was held under the title “Turkey Between the Peace Process and the Crisis of Democratization: Dialogue, the Rule of Law, and the Future of Political Participation.” Dilek Odabaşı moderated the session.


Speakers included DEM Party MP and Imrali Delegation member Pervin Buldan, DEVA Party MP Mehmet Emin Ekmen, Yeni Party MP Okan Konuralp, and Republican People's Party (CHP) MP Oğuz Kaan Salıcı.


The full conference can be watched here


https://left.eu/events/20th-international-conference-the-european-union-turkey-the-middle-east-and-the-kurds/

left.eu


Pervin Buldan: The EU must play its part


Opening the session, Pervin Buldan assessed the current stage of the peace process. “Achieving lasting peace in Turkey would have a positive impact not only on the Middle East but also on Europe,” she said.


Buldan added: “As a result of the human rights violations, torture, and policies of repression that Kurds have endured for half a century, European countries have become closely acquainted with the Kurdish issue and the Kurdish people. Over the years, the Kurdish issue has become a regional and even global concern, closely connected with Europe as well.”


Noting that Kurds make up a significant portion of the diaspora in Europe today, Buldan said: “For this reason, our fundamental expectation is that the European Union, which once actively defended democratic values, should make a positive contribution to the peace process underway in Turkey, support it, and assume the role expected of it.”


“The project of the century”


Buldan said the peace process had reached a historic turning point and emphasized that it was a “project of the century.”


She said: “Particularly in the face of the enormous risks and threats created by the crises and conflicts in the Middle East, the peace process initiated by Mr. Öcalan's February 27 Call for Peace and a Democratic Society, and opened up through the political will demonstrated by Mr. Devlet Bahçeli and Mr. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, has reached a historic turning point. This process has opened the door to a new era for peoples, democracy, universal law, and democratic politics. It would therefore not be wrong to describe the Peace and Democratic Society Process as the project of the century.”


Buldan continued: “A democratic solution to the Kurdish issue is the strongest guarantee of an environment in which everyone can live in peace and security, on the basis of mutual solidarity and fraternity, both in Turkey and throughout the Middle East. Everyone needs to understand this opportunity correctly. When historic opportunities are used wisely, countries can emerge from crises and move toward democracy.”


She added: “Rallying around the Peace and Democratic Society Process, moving forward together, and building peace and democracy through collective effort will be a step that shapes the course of the coming century. This process is not limited to the democratic rights of the Kurdish people. The Kurdish issue concerns the shared future of both Turkey and the Middle East.


It is a process of building a shared democracy, establishing a legal order that prioritizes the rights of all peoples, guaranteeing freedoms through law, strengthening local democracy, and fully opening the channels of democratic political participation in the most inclusive way possible. The peace process is a shared guarantee for Kurds, Turks, Alevis, and all segments of society with different identities and beliefs.”


“Conditions for Öcalan to work freely must be established immediately”


Buldan continued: “First, we expect the National Security Council to adopt a decision urgently so that the framework law can enter into force, the relevant bodies can begin operating, and the process can move forward. We also emphasize that a monitoring committee must be established in Parliament as soon as possible and begin its work. At the same time, I would like to state that we expect Mr. Öcalan to assume the role of coordinator within the Peace and Politicization Council, which is to be established under his leadership.


This process must advance through reciprocal steps. Just as Mr. Öcalan has played a role in the disarmament phase, his serving as coordinator during the political and democratic reconstruction phase would help the council achieve its objectives. In this context, I would also like to emphasize that the conditions necessary for Mr. Öcalan to work freely must be established as soon as …

title: Compulsory expropriation approved for oil extraction in Amed
content:
Two plots of land in the Kocaköy district of Amed (Diyarbakır) are to be expropriated for oil extraction. The land will be used by the state-owned Turkish Petroleum Corporation (TPAO) for the Çobantepe-5 drilling site and its associated infrastructure. The decision by the General Directorate of Mining and Petroleum Affairs (MAPEG) under Turkey’s Ministry of Energy was published in the Official Gazette.


The expropriation affects two plots of land covering a total area of 23,333.56 square meters. The plot designated as parcel 143/1 covers 12,926.76 square meters, while the second, designated as parcel 152/2, covers another 10,406.80 square meters.


Previous attempts to acquire the land through mutual agreement had failed because, according to the authorities, the landowners had demanded compensation exceeding market value. Court orders authorizing early possession of both plots had already been issued by the Diyarbakır Court of First Instance.


MAPEG justified the expropriation on the grounds of public interest in oil extraction, citing Article 10, Paragraph 2 of Turkish Petroleum Law No. 6491.

title: A linha direta de Vorcaro dentro do Grupo Globo: “Quer que peça pra corrigir?”
content:
Um ano antes de se tornar “radioativo”, na tarde de uma quarta-feira de abril de 2024, Daniel Vorcaro recebeu uma oferta de Frederic Kachar, até então CEO da Editora Globo e do Sistema Globo de Rádio: “Quer que a gente o entreviste no Valor?”. A mensagem se referia a Alexandre Afrange, CEO da Veste – antiga Restoque, que detém marcas como Dudalina, John John e Le Lis Blanc –, empresa da qual o banqueiro do Master tinha controle acionário desde 2022. “Não sabia que a Veste tinha esse ceo”, escreveu Kachar, para então oferecer espaço editorial a Vorcaro no jornal de economia do grupo. 


O diálogo faz parte das mensagens interceptadas pela Polícia Federal (PF) a partir do celular de Daniel Vorcaro e apontam que a relação dos dois, nas palavras do próprio banqueiro, em julho do mesmo ano, seria uma “amizade que supera negócios”.

 Os diálogos mostram que o ex-controlador do Banco Master, preso desde março deste ano como principal investigado pela Operação Compliance Zero, tinha acesso direto ao executivo, onde fazia solicitações diretas e reclamava sobre a linha editorial dos jornais do grupo Globo.


O vazamento das mensagens ganhou força nesta quarta-feira (14), momento delicado para a própria Globo. Isso porque no Auditório Ibirapuera, em São Paulo, a Rede Globo promovia um de seus eventos publicitários mais importantes do ano, o Upfront Globo. Na ocasião, os executivos mais influentes do Grupo Globo, a exemplo de Fred Kachar, como é conhecido, se reúnem com vários dos artistas mais famosos do conglomerado junto a representantes do mercado publicitário para detalhar os planos das empresas Globo para o ano seguinte. Talvez por isso, a reação ao vazamento, já conhecido nos bastidores da empresa, não tenha sido mais imediato. Nesta quinta (15), Kachar foi desligado, segundo nota oficial do Grupo.


Nota Grupo Globo


Grupo Globo comunica desligamento de Frederic Kachar e reforça independência editorial de seus veículos

O Grupo Globo comunicou hoje o desligamento do diretor-geral de Mídia Impressa e Rádio, Frederic Kachar. O conteúdo das conversas privadas mantidas com Daniel Vorcaro entre outubro de 2023 e julho de 2025, às quais a empresa teve acesso ontem, revela uma relação inadequada do executivo com um anunciante.


A Editora Globo reforça seu compromisso com a ética e a transparência e reafirma a absoluta independência editorial do jornalismo de seus veículos, premissa essencial de sua atuação. O protagonismo da cobertura crítica, isenta e independente que tem feito do caso Master é a demonstração concreta do compromisso inegociável de seus veículos com os Princípios Editoriais do Grupo Globo.


A empresa reconhece os 29 anos de dedicação de Kachar ao desenvolvimento de seus negócios de mídia e informa que o nome de seu substituto à frente da Editora Globo e do Sistema Globo de Rádio será divulgado em breve.


Comunicação Globo

Rio de Janeiro, 15 de outubro de 2026

Mais informações

https://imprensa.globo.com/


Relação delicada


Vorcaro chegou a solicitar, no dia 12 de outubro de 2024, a capa da revista Vogue Brasil para a então namorada, Martha Graeff, que acabara de lançar a Happy Aging, empresa de suplementos voltada à longevidade feminina, lançada nos Estados Unidos à época. “De presente pra ela”, justificou. 


O pedido não foi plenamente atendido por Kachar, que alegou inviabilidade da agenda de produção da revista. Cinco dias depois, no entanto, as versões online de

Vogue Brasil

,

Marie Claire

 e

Ela

 destacavam Graeff, cujos links foram enviados pelo ex-diretor-geral a Vorcaro: “Depois me diz se faltou algo”. O banqueiro agradeceu: “ficaram ótimas”, disse, antes de fazer a ressalva: “só a Marie Claire deu uma batidinha no final rsrs esses repórteres são uma bênção”, concluiu o banqueiro. Kachar apenas assentiu: “o próximo passo é capa na Ela ou Marie Claire, só precisamos de um fato novo”.

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Trump Administration Reportedly Trying to Denaturalize and Deport Ilhan Omar
content:
Officials conducted a raid on her home and have issued over a dozen subpoenas to her family members.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

The Trump administration is working to build a case against Rep. Ilhan Omar (D-Minnesota) with the hopes of ultimately denaturalizing and deporting the progressive Somali American lawmaker, The Wall Street Journal reports.

The alarming, unprecedented effort — denounced as outright fascism by critics — is wide-ranging, encompassing several federal agencies. U.S. officials and other sources familiar with the investigation told the Journal that the effort is focused, in part, on unearthing information about her deceased father, the circumstances surrounding her arrival in the U.S. when she was a child, and her citizenship.

The Justice Department has issued over a dozen subpoenas in relation to the investigation to Omar’s family, including to her sister and other relatives. The New York Times reported this week that federal officials are attempting to establish a case that Omar’s father lied or omitted information on his immigration forms when he came to the U.S. with Omar in 1995.

Other reports also say that the Trump administration is also looking into whether she lied on papers to obtain legal status and citizenship, and specifically on whether she or her father intentionally misstated her birthdate to obtain citizenship as a minor alongside her father when she was naturalized. The Department of Homeland Security looked into similar allegations of immigration fraud under the Biden administration, but did not move forward because of a lack of evidence, the Times reported.

In a drastic escalation on Monday, agents from Homeland Security Investigations conducted a predawn raid on Omar’s house in Washington, D.C. Officers seized her phone, notebooks, personal computers, and passport.

“President Trump would love to eliminate one of the most effective progressive voices in Congress. There is no basis for this,” Omar told the Journal.

Omar was 12 years old when she arrived as a refugee in the U.S. Her family had fled a bloody civil war and a “human rights disaster,” as dubbed by Amnesty International, in Somalia. She became a U.S. citizen at the age of 17, in the year 2000.

Omar has weathered racist and bigoted personal attacks against her by President Donald Trump and other political figures for years. The Trump administration’s latest attacks on the Minnesota representative have been widely condemned by Democrats as a naked attempt to go after a political opponent just weeks before the midterm elections, in which Omar is up for reelection; as well as a tyrannical, fascist act by the increasingly bold and out-of-control Trump administration.

The allegation that Omar was actually 18 when she was naturalized originally gained traction on conservative social media through a viral video posted in 2019. Her congressional office had her birth year changed on official paperwork from 1981 to 1982, which conservative conspiracy theorists framed as suspicious.

However, her office said it was already in the process of getting her biographical information changed through official channels. Further, it is common for people from war-torn and underresourced countries to put an approximate date on immigration paperwork because they have no official record of their births; a 2020 report found only 6 percent of births are registered with the government in Somalia.

After the raid on Monday, Trump once again spewed racist rhetoric against Omar and Somalis.

“She comes in from a country without laws, without police, without military, where all they do is shoot each other, and she comes into our country and she says, ‘I have a constitutional right,’” Trump said at a rally in Ohio. “She’s telling us about the Constitution, and she comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet.”

The crowd chanted “deport” as he incited violence against Somalis. Just last Friday, Trump openly encouraged a race war against Somalis in Minnesota in a post on Truth Social, telling followers to “fight back.”

Omar has stood up against Trump’s attacks. “Make no mistake: this is an attempt to target political enemies and weaponize federal law enforcement,” said Omar on Monday following the raid. “For ten years, Trump has targeted me with baseless lies and smear campaigns. This is just the latest …

author: Nehaa Bimal
title: Proposed federal lands act amendment could complicate devolution: premier
content:
Ottawa’s tinkering with its Territorial Lands Act could throw a wrench in Nunavut’s devolution work, says Premier John Main.


He was speaking to a

Senate Standing Committee on Indigenous Peoples Oct. 6 during a hearing about mineral rights in the territory.


Nunavut is preparing the legislative framework that will allow the territorial government to take control of a vast majority of its Crown land. To do so, it’s mirroring several federal acts, including the Territorial Lands Act, to finalize devolution, which is set to happen April 1, 2027.


The act governs use of Crown land in the Northwest Territories and Nunavut, including its sale or lease,

 

mining rights and environmental regulations.


But the Territorial Lands Act could change as its being mirrored.


Working its way through Senate hearings is Bill C-31, which proposes amendments the act that would

allow Canada’s federal cabinet, on the recommendation of the northern affairs minister, to cancel or restrict mineral rights on Crown land in Nunavut if it determines doing so is in the national interest.


“The timing of Bill C-31 creates a particular challenge,” said Main in his opening remarks to the committee.


“The Government of  Nunavut cannot mirror federal provisions that have not yet been enacted.”


If Nunavut were to delay its work until the passage of Bill C-31, it would create a “significant risk” to the territory’s ability to ready itself for the April 1 devolution deadline, Main said.


The mirrored legislation in Nunavut, called the Public Lands Act, was tabled in draft form during the spring sitting of Nunavut legislature and is scheduled for formal introduction during the fall sitting, which is scheduled to start on Oct. 22.


Also discussed during the hearing was implications of foreign investment in Nunavut, including the potential sale of the Mary River iron mine on north Baffin Island.


Baffinland Iron Mines Corp.

sought creditor protection

 in May. In June, a

judge approved

 a $660-million loan from Export Development Canada so the Mary River Mine could remain operational through this year’s shipping season.


Nunavut Senator Nancy Karetak-Lindell raised concerns about potential foreign ownership of mining projects and infrastructure, including the Mary River mine, should it be put up for sale as part of the creditor protection process.


“It’s important for us to be open to investment from foreign interest,” Main said in response.


“If we restricted access in terms of mining or industrial development in Nunavut to only to Canadian companies, we would be seen as not a very attractive jurisdiction to invest in.”


That said, Main acknowledged the territory’s lack of infrastructure could leave

 the territory vulnerable to foreign interests.


“If there’s a vacuum there in terms of investment, it could look like an opportunity for foreign actors,”

 Main said.


While the court has approved a sale and investment solicitation process, no buyer has been selected and no sale approved, said Baffinland spokesperson Peter Akman in an email to Nunatsiaq News.


“It would be premature to speculate about potential bidders or transaction terms,” said.


At a Sept. 29 committee meeting on the same topic, Karetak-Lindell questioned the lack of a definition for “national interest” in the proposed changes to the lands act, and the potential for uncertainty this could cause as Nunavut prepares for devolution.


But the amendment won’t affect decision making over the land being transferred to Nunavut under devolution, said 

Georgina Lloyd, assistant deputy minister of northern affairs.


After devolution, the Territorial Lands Act will remain in place for the “small amount of Crown land that will still be under Canada’s jurisdiction,” she said.


Bill C-31 remains under consideration by the House of Commons Standing Committee on Finance.

title: Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στους εξεγερμένους στην Γαλλία, Παρασκευή 16/10 12:00 Γαλλικο Ινστιτούτο
content:
Συγκέντρωση αλληλεγγύης στους εξεγερμένους στην Γαλλία


Παρασκευή 16/10 12:00, Γαλλικο Ινστιτούτο


«Συγγνώμη για την αναστάτωση… έχουμε να σώσουμε το μέλλον μας!»


Έχουν περάσει περίπου δύο εβδομάδες, όπου το μαθητικό κίνημα έχει ξεσηκωθεί από άκρη ως άκρη της Γαλλίας, παρασύροντας με ταχύτητα ολοένα και μεγαλύτερα κομμάτια της κοινωνίας σε έναν αγώνα που παίρνει διαρκώς μεγαλύτερες διαστάσεις. Καταλήψεις σχολικών κτιρίων, που ξεκίνησαν αυθόρμητα από τις 22 Σεπτέμβρη από πρωτοβουλίες σε σχολεία των προαστίων του Παρισιού, ξεκινώντας από το λύκειο Saint- Exupéry στο Κρετέιγ, μέσα σε λίγες μόνο μέρες άρχισαν να μετουσιώνονται σε κίνημα που έχει φέρει σε αδιέξοδο την κυβέρνηση, λίγους μάλιστα μήνες πριν από τις προεδρικές εκλογές του 2027.


Οι διεκδικήσεις των μαθητών αφορούν την συνολικότερη επίθεση που δέχεται η δευτεροβάθμια εκπαίδευση και κατ’ επέκταση την ίδια την υποβάθμιση των ζωών τους μέσω της απροκάλυπτης βίας που έχουν δεχτεί οι κινητοποιήσεις. Αφενός, την ίδια στιγμή που το γαλλικό κράτος επενδύει τα μέγιστα στην πολεμική προετοιμασία, το ποσοστό του κρατικού προϋπολογισμού που δίνεται στην εκπαίδευση είναι φανερά μειωμένο, με χαρακτηριστικό παράδειγμα την περικοπή πάνω από 3 χιλιάδων θέσεων εκπαιδευτικών σε εθνικό επίπεδο για το έτος. Μάλιστα, την κατάσταση έρχεται να οξύνει η πραγματικά άνιση κατανομή του ποσού αυτού ανά τα ιδρύματα της χώρας, που εντείνει τους ταξικούς φραγμούς μέσω της περαιτέρω εξαθλίωσης των ήδη υποβαθμισμένων σχολείων φτωχότερων περιοχών και των τεχνικών σχολείων. Την στιγμή που τα ωράρια παραμένουν εξουθενωτικά και το σύστημα άκρως ανταγωνιστικό, ένα ανησυχητικά μεγάλο ποσοστό των σχολείων υπολειτουργεί με βασικά κενά από καθηγητές, στοίβαξημαθητών σε τάξεις των 30-35 ατόμων, επικίνδυνες υγειονομικά και υλικοτεχνικά συνθήκες (σαπισμένα ταβάνια, ποντίκια, έλλειψη θέρμανσης, υπολειτουργική σχολική καντίνα, έλλειψη σε θρανία και καρέκλες…). Και συγχρόνως, το σύστημα πρόσβασης στην τριτοβάθμια εκπαίδευση που καθιερώθηκε το 2018 (Parcoursup), έρχεται να αποκρυσταλλώσει μια λογική διαλογής και αποκλεισμού, όπου οι μαθητ(ρι)ές μετατρέπονται σε αριθμούς και τα σχολεία τους σε δείκτες αξιολόγησης για την τελική τους εισαγωγή ή όχι στο ίδρυμα της επιλογής τους.


«Ένα κράτος που εξοργίζεται από το κάψιμο των κάδων αλλά αποδέχεται να χτυπάει παιδιά, είναι ένα κράτος που πρέπει να πολεμηθεί. Και να καταστραφεί»


Τις τελευταίες μέρες, περισσότερα από τα μισά σχολεία στο σύνολο της χώρας έχουν προχωρήσει σε κατάληψη και κινητοποίηση ασχέτως, βέβαια, που η γαλλική κυβέρνηση αρέσκεται να διατυμπανίζει ότι 9 στα 10 σχολεία λειτουργούν κανονικά. Ξεκινώντας την κλιμάκωση ήδη από τις 29/09, οι εκπαιδευτικοί αγώνες γρήγορα συνδέθηκαν με την γενική απεργία δημοσίων υπαλλήλων για τον κρατικό προϋπολογισμό αλλά και με τον αγώνα των πυροσβεστών ενάντια στην παντελή αδιαφορία του κράτους για την διαχείριση των πυρκαγιών το καλοκαίρι, που παραδόθηκαν δεκάδες χιλιάδες εκτάρια δάσους στις φλόγες. Στις 06/10 οι πορείες μέτρησαν περίπου μισό εκατομμύριο διαδηλωτών σε κάθε γωνία της Γαλλίας, ενώ οι μαζικές πορείες και οι γενικευμένες συγκρούσεις με τους μαθητές και τις μαθήτριες στην πρώτη γραμμή είναι καθημερινές και στοχεύουν σε περαιτέρω κλιμάκωση, στο γενικό κάλεσμα της 17ης Οκτώβρη. Στο πλευρό των μαθητών βρίσκονται και οι εκπαιδευτικοί,οι οποίοι δημιουργώντας ανθρώπινες αλυσίδες απέναντι στους μπάτσους προστατεύουν τους/ις μαθητές/ριες και διεκδικούν τα αυτονόητα, αλλά και γονείς όπως και η υπόλοιπη κοινωνία, που προσπαθούν με αυτοσχέδιες συλλογικές κουζίνες, νομικές συμβουλές και φαρμακεία να ενισχύσουν και να θωρακίσουν τον αγώνα. Την ίδια στιγμή, από το δικό τους μετερίζι οι φοιτητ(ρι)ές έχουν ξεκινήσει τις καταλήψεις των κτιρίων και ορθώνουν οδοφράγματα σε αλληλεγγύη στους μαθητές, εκφράζοντας την γενικευμένη οργή ενάντια στις περικοπές και την κρατική βία, την άνοδο της ακροδεξιάς την εισβολή μπάτσων στα πανεπιστήμια, τις συνεργασίες των πανεπιστημίων με εταιρείες ισραηλινού κεφαλαίου και την αύξηση των διδάκτρων για φοιτητές εκτός ΕΕ.


Το εξεγερσιακό κλίμα στην Γαλλία αποτυπώθηκε χαρακτηριστικά στις 08/10 όπου με σύνθημα «Παίρνουμε τη Βαστίλη» εκατοντάδες χιλιάδες νέοι εκδήλωσαν την οργή τους στην πρωτεύουσα, όσο παράλληλα στις υπόλοιπες πόλεις συνεχίζονται οι κινητοποιήσεις, αντιστεκόμενοι επί ώρες στην σφοδρή καταστολή του κράτους και θέτοντας ως αιχμιακά στοιχεία του κινήματος την εναντίωσή στο κράτος, την καταστολή, την εξαθλίωση και την άνοδο του φασισμού. author: Mohanad El-Hemrawi
title: Gaza Child Amputees Are Outgrowing Their Prosthetics Amid Israel’s Restrictions
content:
WHO estimates that over 5,000 people in Gaza have lost limbs since October 2023, and one in five of them is a child.

Truthout is an indispensable resource for activists, movement leaders and workers everywhere. Please make this work possible with a quick donation.

Abdul-Rahman al-Nashash, 11, holds onto the edge of a chair and pushes his left leg into a plastic prosthetic that doesn’t fit him anymore. The bone that was cut two years ago has kept growing inside, and it presses painfully against his skin.

His doctors told him to stop wearing it. He wears it anyway, every morning, pulling the straps tight and rolling his pants down so no one sees the plastic before he takes his first step. He bites his lip when it hurts and holds his shoulders straight so no one can tell he is limping.

“He forces himself to wear it,” his mother said, “just so no one knows he has a disability.”

Before the genocide, al-Nashash played for a local soccer club, and he would chase the ball across a dirt field until the sun went down. He is the eldest son in his family, and he was the one his mother leaned on at home. When she needed water, he was the one who ran to carry the heavy gallon of water, and he never got tired. Now, he is not able.

When he finally takes the prosthetic off, he sits curled up. He is waiting for his third surgery, and his mother said he will need one every year.

As a child grows, the bone in the amputated leg grows too, but the prosthetic doesn’t. At some point it stops fitting, and sometimes the child needs another operation before he can get a new one. In Gaza, that often means starting over with surgery, then rehabilitation, then a new limb if one can be made at all, because Israel restricts the parts and materials needed to make and repair them. Some children in Gaza have outgrown their limbs and are waiting for new ones. Others never received one, because there are none in Gaza that fit them.

Al-Nashash’s family was forced to evacuate from al-Bureij refugee camp in Central Gaza in 2023 and took shelter in UNRWA schools. His father stayed behind. Two days after they left, on October 20, the house was struck, and his father was killed along with several relatives. The three-wheeled motorcycle that had been the family’s only source of income was parked in the storeroom and was destroyed in the same strike.

From there, the family moved from school to school and tent to tent. They spent about three months in Rafah, then moved to schools in Nuseirat. With no money coming in, his mother opened a small stall with her brother-in-law, selling a variety of canned beans.

Around noon on July 16, 2024, her sister asked her to come light a fire and cook, so she left her son to mind the stall in her place. An Israeli airstrike hit the tents in the middle of al-Razi school, a UNRWA shelter in Nuseirat camp, killing 23 people, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office. A piece of shrapnel struck his leg directly. His mother said his injured left foot was split in two, the bones of his toes exposed, and she kept screaming that her son had been killed.

At first, she said, she was told doctors hoped to fix the leg with metal plates rather than amputate. At Al-Aqsa Hospital, one doctor told her the leg would have to be amputated, and she asked them to cut off her own leg and give it to him, because he was the one who took care of her. He was then taken by an ambulance to a hospital by the sea in Deir al-Balah where a foreign medical team was working. There they told her nothing more could be done. The amputation needed her consent. She signed, because there was no other choice.

When al-Nashash woke from the anesthesia, he kept staring at himself as if he were losing his mind. It was only after counselors came and he began to see other children like him that he slowly started to adjust.

After the amputation, therapists from local rehabilitation programs came to work with him regularly. But his natural childhood growth worked against his recovery. “My son grows fast,” his mother said. By March 2025, just eight months after he lost his leg, the bone had already grown too long.

They traveled to Jordan, where surgeons cut the bone back and fitted him with his first prosthetic, the one he still wears today. The trip lasted five months. When al-Nashash returned to Gaza, the boy who used to sprint on the soccer field had to start physical therapy from scratch, learning how to balance and walk all over again.

Today, that same …

author: labor4pal
title: Inside the fight to stop Israel-bound weapons at the East Coast’s biggest port (Mondoweiss)
content:
At Port Newark-Elizabeth, activists are escalating their tactics to stop weapons shipments to Israel. Mondoweiss reports from the port’s front lines.

By Joseph Mogul October 15, 20262

Activists with the Port of Elizabeth Movement block ZIM trucks carrying weapons components from entering the port on the morning of May 22, 2026. (Port of Elizabeth Movement)

A line of trucks rounded the bend toward Port Newark-Elizabeth on October 3, 2025. Inside the trailers were combat boots and weapons components — including 61 tons of forging rings used for military jets — bound for Israel via a Maersk vessel departing that morning.

But before the truckers could enter the port and the Maersk Sentosa could be loaded, 100 activists organized under the banner “Port of Elizabeth Movement” (POEM) sprang into action.

“It was ass o’clock in the morning. The sun was far from up. It was pitch black. Everyone was tired. Someone yelled, ‘Go, go, go, go!’” said Danny Creamer, who was later arrested at the POEM action.

Port Newark-Elizabeth is the third-largest port in the U.S. and the largest on the East Coast. And it has become a recurring target for activists concerned with the weapons supply chain to Israel. About 900 tons of sea cargo — comprising 91% of all military cargo bound for Israel that does not pass through a military base — originates from a nearby warehouse and is transported through Port Newark-Elizabeth.

The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey has jurisdiction over the port, with commissioners appointed by the governors of each state. Organizers claim that this power structure makes the organizing landscape less conducive to pressuring elected officials because of the Port Authority’s insulation from the local community.

“We don’t get into that kind of politics. If it’s local, if it was the city of Newark then maybe it would be worth a shot,” said Tova Fry, a long-time organizer with Port Workers and Communities for Palestine, a group focused on facilitating worker solidarity at ports across the U.S.

Instead of electoral or legislative strategies, the battle for Port Newark-Elizabeth is fought on different terrain: the dual threat of labor organizing by Port Workers and Communities for Palestine, and escalated direct actions by POEM. The two groups work autonomously and share the same goal — preventing vessels at Port Newark-Elizabeth from shipping U.S.-made weapons to assist Israel’s genocide in Gaza.

Back at the October 2025 action, Creamer and his fellow activists ran into the street, unfurled banners and laid 15 shrouds representing babies killed by Israel in Gaza. At one point somebody started playing the bagpipes. The activists blocked the road for about one hour with traffic cones and their bodies, obstructing the truckers’ entry and delaying the departure of the Maersk vessel. “It felt momentous, like ‘shit something’s happening here,’” said Creamer.

Eventually, the Port Authority Police responded with a dispersal order. Four people who refused to comply, including Creamer, were arrested and charged with disorderly conduct. Almost one year later, the four were found guilty of a violation (which Creamer compared to a traffic ticket) and sentenced to community service.

“We didn’t dismantle the U.S. imperialism shtick in one action, but we’ve at least inconvenienced it a little bit,” said Creamer. According to Creamer, this initial action demonstrated POEM’s animating principle. While large-scale rallies and marches show opposition and “serve as a threat, if we don’t follow through, then we can lose our leverage,” explained Creamer. “So we decided to try and stop the weapons shipments ourselves.”

AdvertismentAt Port Newark-Elizabeth, this means using bill of lading data to track when Maersk and ZIM ships — the two major logistics companies that supply U.S.-made weapons to Israel — are set to depart and to coordinate timely escalations.

Maersk, an international Danish shipping company, is an integral player in this supply chain, and has been a target of the Palestine solidarity movement since the Palestinian Youth Movement (PYM) launched the “Mask Off Maersk” campaign in June 2024. Recent research by Oxfam and PYM found that regular Maersk shipments out of Port Newark-Elizabeth include components for bullets, bombs, and mortars. Between October 2023 and July 2025, Maersk transported approximately 3,000 tons of weapons components to Israeli weapons manufacturer Elbit Systems.

ZIM, the other cargo …

author: Shams Eddin Essam
title: Will Supply Ministry’s wheat intervention really rein in cost of unsubsidized bread?
content:
As the grain and bakery industries petition the government for permission to increase bread prices in order to protect their profits, the Supply Ministry has

announced

 it is injecting wheat onto the national commodity exchange to bring prices down and cut production costs.


The move came after calls for a government review of bread pricing guidelines in

August

 and

September

. Producers said they needed to increase consumer prices to compensate for rising production costs, particularly of flour.

Despite talks between ministry and industry representatives, the government has held the price caps and loaf weight specifications

steady

, announcing the supply release instead.


However, sources from the grain, milling and bakery industries who spoke to Mada Masr expressed doubt that the mechanism would meaningfully reduce production costs, indicating that the last time the ministry undertook a similar supply allocation in 2023, the move only fuelled profiteering on a secondary market that emerged in parallel to the commodity exchange.


The ministry has not said how much wheat it will offer via the commodity exchange, though ministry spokespeople

explained

 that the extra supply would be enough to bring costs down across the supply chain.


Speaking on condition of anonymity, two grain industry sources told Mada Masr that the imported wheat is expected to be available via the Egyptian Commodities Exchange either this week or next. Sales are to be capped at 500 tonnes per mill, and, as per the agreement with the ministry, two trading sessions would be held weekly, the sources said.


The CEO of the commodity exchange

told

 financial newspapers on Tuesday that trading had begun this week.


The ministry aims to sell wheat at LE16,500-LE16,700 per tonne. The sources said supplies will be available to all licensed mills, allowing more flour for bakeries that produce commercial bread, such as fino and “tourist” loaves.


However, the announced prices alone are not enough to convince mills to buy wheat through the exchange, said another grain industry chamber member.


A tonne of wheat currently costs LE16,800-LE17,200 on the open market, depending on quality.


But once the additional costs of participating in trading on the commodity exchange are factored in, the gap between the exchange price and the open market price narrows.


The source said that mills remain skeptical about the value of going to the exchange under its current system, given the registration and trading fees involved — costs they do not necessarily incur when purchasing directly from traders.


The source added that it would be difficult to assess whether the government’s price is competitive or not before learning more about the specifications and quality of the wheat being offered. When buying directly from private sector suppliers, mills can inspect a shipment before completing a purchase.


A mill owner said that there are questions beyond the immediate cost of the wheat: can the government ensure a steady supply of wheat through the commodity exchange to control costs and justify the cost of switching to the exchange?


Until the government’s mechanism proves capable of consistently meeting market demand, dealing with established suppliers is the more transparent option, he said. 


Global wheat prices have risen amid Russia’s escalating war on Ukraine, disrupting Black Sea shipping and ultimately pushing costs up in Egypt, the world’s largest wheat importer.


While the government says it has bought more domestically grown wheat, Egypt is still heavily reliant on wheat imports from both Russia and Ukraine. The cost pressures have become increasingly evident in Egypt’s domestic flour market over recent months. The price of a tonne of imported wheat stood at around LE12,500 in June, with a ton of unsubsidized flour at around LE17,000. Now, a ton of unsubsidized flour stands at around LE21,000.


Flour, in turn, accounts for between 60-70 percent of the production cost of commercial bread, according to an estimate from an anonymous General Bakeries Division source. This makes rising flour prices a direct strain on bakeries’ profit margins, particularly alongside

increases

 in other operating costs.


A bakeries division member told Mada Masr that resuming wheat sales through the exchange would not be an adequate solution to the gap between the production costs of unsubsidized bread and the prices set by the Supply Ministry. The …

author: Unknown
title: У политзаключённого анархиста Никиты Уварова умерла тётя: поддержите его письмом!
content:
На днях в семье Никиты Уварова случилось горе — умерла Татьяна, сестра его мамы Анны. По сообщению группы поддержки, семьи были очень близки, Татьяна поддерживала Никиту и вместе с его мамой приезжала к нему на свидания. Никита уже знает о её смерти.

«Мы выражаем глубокие соболезнования Никите, Анне и всем родным и близким Татьяны, - пишет группа поддержки. - Переживать потерю близкого человека особенно тяжело в заключении, вдали от семьи. Сейчас Никита находится в одиночной камере СИЗО-1 Красноярска. При этом возможности общаться с родными у него практически нет: из-за того, что следствие сделало его маму свидетельницей по новому уголовному делу, им запрещены свидания и телефонные разговоры».

8 октября суд в очередной раз продлил Никите содержание под стражей ещё на два месяца. Напомним, он должен был выйти на свободу 19 марта, полностью отбыв 5-летний срок по «делу канских подростков», но незадолго до освобождения против него возбудили новое уголовное дело. В августе обвинение ужесточили — теперь ему вменяют сразу две статьи за один и тот же разговор с другим заключённым.

Адрес для писем: 660075, РФ, г. Красноярск, ул. Республики, 72, СИЗО-1, Уваров Никита Андреевич 2005 г. р. Отправить письмо можно через сервисы «Ф-письмо», «Зонателеком» и PrisonMail.Online (для зарубежных карт).

title: Ekrem İmamoğlu hakkında yeni bir soruşturma daha açıldı: Akın Gürlek'le telefon görüşmesini anlatmıştı
content:
İstanbul Büyükşehir Belediyesi Başkanı Ekrem İmamoğlu hakkında İBB Davası'nda kürsüde savunma yaparken soruşturma başlatıldı. Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı tarafından başlatılan soruşturmada gerekçe olarak “kamu görevlisine görevinden dolayı aleni hakaret” gösterildi.

Soruşturma nedeninin İmamoğlu'nun savunması esnasında Adalet Bakanı Akın Gürlek ile telefon görüşmesini anlatması ve bunu anlatırken taklit yapması olarak gösterildi.

Başsavcılık tarafından yapılan açıklamada şu ifadelere yer verildi:

“İstanbul 33. Ağır Ceza Mahkemesi’nin 2026/208 Esas sayılı dosyasının sanıklarından olan Ekrem İMAMOĞLU’nun 15/10/2026 tarihli duruşmadaki, kamu davasına esas soruşturmayı yürüten yargı mensuplarını hedef alan ifadeleri nedeniyle, “kamu görevlilerine görevi nedeniyle aleni hakaret” suçundan, Bakırköy Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığınca resen soruşturma başlatılmıştır. Kamuoyunun bilgisine saygıyla duyurulur.”

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: David Venn
title: President, community director roles up for grabs in QIA election
content:
The Qikiqtani Inuit Association is looking for its next president.


It’s also looking for community directors in Iqaluit, Igloolik, Kimmirut, Sanirajak, Clyde River, Pond Inlet and Sanikiluaq, said a news release issued Thursday by Markoosie Qaunirq, spokesperson for QIA.


Each position carries a four-year term.


The nomination period for the election runs from Nov. 9 to 13.


Eligible voters must be Inuit, enrolled under the Nunavut Agreement; at least 16 years old; and have resided in the Qikiqtani Region for one year or more, according to the release.


The current QIA president Olayuk Akesuk

won

 the 2022 election over Paul Okalik, with 61.2 per cent of the vote. He had served in the role since the fall of 2021, when he took over from P.J. Akeeagok, who resigned to run for MLA.


Election day is set for Dec. 14.

author: Goktug Caliskan
title: Why China won’t build its own Wagner in Africa
content:
Attacks on Chinese workers in Mali are testing Beijing’s reliance on African security forces. Russia’s experience there gives China little reason to take on the fighting itself.


On 9 May, fighters from Jama’at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM), al-Qaeda’s affiliate in the Sahel, stopped buses and trucks at Zambougou, in the Ségou region of Mali about 60 kilometres from Bamako, ordered the passengers out and burned at least 40 civilian vehicles. One passenger 

told Human Rights Watch

 that the fighters sent the travellers on towards the capital on foot, saying they had declared an embargo on Bamako. HRW found no Malian troops in the area.


On 12 May, the Chinese embassy in Bamako 

published a warning

 urging Chinese nationals to leave several mining districts, citing armed attacks and the government’s campaign against unlicensed mining. The incidents occurred in different parts of Mali, but both exposed the limits of state protection beyond Bamako. A 

second notice in July

 reported attacks on foreigners around Kenieba, Bougouni and Foulou. An embassy can tell its citizens to leave. It has far less to offer those who stay.


A 

BBC Monitoring review

 counted 38 Chinese citizens among the 89 foreigners abducted in high-profile cases across Africa in 2025, many of them working in the gold industry of south-western Mali. The figures cover foreign nationals and offer no comparable measure of the kidnappings experienced by Malians. Russia, meanwhile, has become directly involved in Mali’s military campaign, committing personnel to combat operations alongside Malian forces.


What fighting costs Russia


On 10 September, JNIM fighters overran the army camp at Dioura in central Mali. Military, security and local sources 

told AFP

 that at least 100 Malian soldiers and five members of Russia’s Africa Corps had been killed. The Malian authorities published no toll of their own. Bamako had already lost its defence minister, Sadio Camara, who was 

killed in an attack on his residence

 in Kati on 25 April.


Less than a month after Dioura, separatists announced what they called a temporary withdrawal from Kidal, and Malian forces backed by Russian fighters 

returned to the northern town

. The recapture was a significant political and military gain for Bamako, though JNIM’s attacks on civilian transport farther south remained a separate security challenge.


Wagner arrived in late 2021, as Mali’s relations with France broke down. When it announced its departure in June 2025, 

Africa Corps, which answers to Russia’s Defence Ministry, stayed on

, and Russian personnel remain part of the war. On 31 July, Human Rights Watch 

reported

 that Russian-controlled Africa Corps aircraft had struck Kyrnia, in the Mopti region, on 15 June. Eight civilians, including three children, were killed in what the organisation described as an apparently unlawful attack. Russia’s direct involvement has made its military reputation inseparable from the conduct of operations in Mali, including attacks that have harmed civilians.


Contractors outside the fighting


Chinese security companies have taken a much narrower role. When fighting trapped about 330 Chinese workers in Juba in July 2016, DeWe Security Service Group helped organise their evacuation despite having no armed personnel of its own. The company, founded by former officers of the People’s Liberation Army and the People’s Armed Police, hired armed South Sudanese as backup, told the workers to stay put and waited for Ugandan forces to secure the airport before the evacuation could begin, as 

Carnegie’s research on the episode

 records.


The pattern holds elsewhere. Chinese contractors assess threats and train guards, as DeWe has done for Kenya’s Chinese-financed Standard Gauge Railway, and rely on host-country police and soldiers to carry the weapons. These arrangements allow Chinese companies to organise protection while leaving combat operations to local forces. They also make effective oversight difficult when those forces commit abuses.


The Cité Chinoise in the outskirts of Bamako: one of the signs of China’s economic presence in Mali (Wikimedia Commons).


Control and cost


Beijing has its own reasons to keep armed force under tight political command. From 1 January 2018, 

the People’s Armed Police

 came under the command of the Communist Party’s Central Committee and the Central Military Commission and was no longer under the authority of the State Council …

author: Chris Walker
title: Americans’ Confidence in Food Safety Plummets Amid Summer of Recalls
content:
Experts have expressed deep concern over Trump administration cuts to federal food monitoring systems.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

Americans’ confidence in the safety of the food supply has plummeted, as has their belief in federal food safety standards, according to a new poll from Gallup.

When asked about their confidence in the safety of food in grocery stores across the country, only 65 percent of respondents said they are either “very confident” or “somewhat confident.” While that figure represents a majority of respondents, it’s the lowest confidence rating that Gallup has recorded since it began asking the question in 2019, when 81 percent expressed confidence that the food they were buying was safe.

Additionally, the poll found that respondents are skeptical of how well the Trump administration is ensuring the safety of the food supply. According to the poll, only 47 percent of Americans have a “great deal” or “fair amount” of confidence that the federal government is making sure the food supply is safe, while 53 percent say their confidence levels reach the “not much” or “none” levels.

It’s the first time in the poll’s history that the confidence level in the federal government’s ability to keep food safe has dipped below 50 percent.

The lack of confidence in the government’s ability to monitor and keep food safe comes amid a spate of food warnings this past summer, including recalls of jalapeños, berries, beef, alfalfa sprouts, and more items. A record-breaking cyclosporiasis outbreak relating to lettuce sales sickened thousands with intense bouts of diarrhea, including at least two documented deaths.

One week in August this year saw recalls of 12 different food products. That number is four times higher than it was during a similar period last year, and six times higher than it was in 2024.

Some disease researchers have blamed the Trump White House for the increases in foodborne illness outbreaks and recalls, noting that cuts by the administration, stemming mainly from its so-called “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) initiative, have made monitoring difficult and response time slower.

Indeed, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) lost around one-fifth of its staff since President Donald Trump returned to office, and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has lost around 25 percent, including most members of a food parasite-tracking team.

Microbiologist and founder of Food Safety Strategy Jennifer McEntire told Stateline earlier this year that there are “valid questions around the timing of the response” from the administration to the cyclosporiasis crisis, including “the time it took for agencies to recognize the outbreak and to start to investigate it.”

Susan Mayne, an adjunct professor at the Yale School of Public Health and former head of the FDA, has also questioned the Trump administration’s cuts to food safety standards.

“We had a national advisory committee, a committee that advised FDA and [the U.S. Department of Agriculture] on how to prevent microbial contamination in food,” Mayne said back in July. “That advisory committee was disbanded. We used to convene meetings with our Mexican counterparts on how we can work together to improve food safety. That entire team was let go.”

author: Jake Johnson
title: “Because of the Price of Oil … We’re Making a Fortune,” Trump Says at Rally
content:
Trump, who has profited massively from his second term in the White House, is a major investor in oil and gas companies.

Truthout is a vital news source and a living history of political struggle. If you think our work is valuable, support us with a donation of any size.

President Donald Trump attempted to spin high oil prices as a boon for the United States at a rally in Arizona on Wednesday, just hours after new federal data showed that inflation reached its highest level in months in September.

“Because of the price of oil, Texas and Oklahoma and North Dakota and all these places, we’re making a fortune,” Trump declared, referring to states that produce large amounts of crude oil. Those states are home to major fossil fuel companies that have reported windfall profits amid Trump’s illegal war on Iran.

Trump insisted that gas prices — currently at an average of $4.33 per gallon for regular gas and $6.32 for diesel — would tumble once the Iran war ends, but his administration has repeatedly given false timelines for the deadly conflict and has shown no indication that it is willing to reach a lasting diplomatic agreement.

Trump, who has profited massively from his second term in the White House, is a major investor in oil and gas companies. According to one recent analysis, the president’s investments in fossil fuel stocks have boosted his net worth by up to $15.5 million since January.

Working-class Americans, meanwhile, are struggling to make ends meet as high gas prices compound a broader affordability crisis that extends to food, housing, and other necessities. A tracker maintained by the Watson School of International and Public Affairs estimates that American consumers have paid an extra $135 billion combined in fuel costs since the start of the Iran war — roughly $1,030 per household.

Wage growth has not kept up with inflation, which rose to an annualized rate of 3.7% last month.

“Workers are losing the race between wages and prices,” Elise Gould, senior economist at the Economic Policy Institute, wrote on Wednesday. “Nominal wage growth continues to decelerate as workers lose bargaining power at work. Workers simply don’t have the leverage to bid up their wages. Reduced leverage and higher prices translated into falling [year-over-year] real wages for six months in a row.”

“Workers have seen zero progress on affordability compared to January 2025,” Gould added. “Real wages are essentially stagnant as workers’ leverage has declined and prices have risen. It’s no wonder workers feel left behind in the current economy.”

A Harris poll published by The Guardian on Thursday shows that three-quarters of US voters are concerned about a recession, and a “vast majority of Americans agreed that there is an affordability crisis, including 96% of Republicans.”

author: Pauline Ertel
title: Brazil Abolishes Six-Day Workweek Ahead of Presidential Run-Off
content:
Brazil’s senate has approved a constitutional amendment ending the country’s six-day workweek, delivering a key pledge by president Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva just days before an election run-off. 


The reform, passed on Wednesday, shortens the working week from 44 hours to a maximum of 40 hours and is set to

improve working conditions

 for more than 37 million people. That includes 16 million who work six-day weeks and are now guaranteed two days of rest each week without a reduction to their wages.


The amendment primarily affects workers in low paid industries such as retail and hospitality, one of the groups from which Lula has

lost suppor

t since defeating far-right incumbent Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. Bolsonaro is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a failed coup in the wake of his defeat. 


Informal and gig economy workers, including app-based drivers without employment contracts, will not be covered by the new law.


Lula, who will face far-right Flávio Bolsonaro, the jailed former president’s son, for a second round on 25 October,

called the reform

 a “victory for the working class”. 


He

said on X

 the vote was “a historic achievement for millions of workers, who will now have more time to rest, be with their family, take care of themselves and live,” 


The victory may give Lula a much-needed boost; the leftwing incumbent came second behind Bolsonaro in the first round of voting on 4 October and is still trailing him in the polls, albeit by a

small margin

.


Brazilian trade unions and labour federations

welcomed the amendment,

which they said followed months of widespread

 strikes and protests by workers

. Advocates have been calling for the policy for years, but it gained

 more traction in 2023 thanks to a viral TikTok video by

 pharmacy clerk-turned-influencer Rick Azevedo.  


Bolsonaro long opposed the proposal, calling it an “opportunistic” attempt by Lula to appeal to working-class voters. But he reversed course shortly before the 4 October vote,

telling journalists

 that “most Brazilian workers ‌want to ⁠see the end of the six-day workweek.” 


Seventy-five senators, including Bolsonaro allies, voted in favour of the amendment. The only one to vote against it was former vice-president Hamilton Mourão, who worked under Jair Bolsonaro.

author: Gustavo Faleiros
title: Povos da floresta e do mar contra a extrema direita
content:
Quer receber os textos desta coluna em primeira mão no seu e-mail? Assine a newsletter Ligando os pontos, enviada toda quinta-feira. Para receber as próximas edições,

inscreva-se aqui

.


Em 1987, quando o Brasil acabava de sair das sinistras décadas de ditadura militar, surgiu uma união de forças sociais que até então pareciam distantes. Comunidades extrativistas e indígenas da Amazônia, vítimas históricas dos grileiros,

criaram a Aliança dos Povos da Floresta

. O momento não poderia ter sido mais propício pois, deste grupo, que contava com lideranças como Chico Mendes e Ailton Krenak, saíram propostas que influenciaram a nova Constituição, promulgada em 1988.


O impacto político daquele encontro não pode ser esquecido neste momento em que a extrema direita, representada pela candidatura de

Flávio Bolsonaro (PL)

, busca privatizar o patrimônio natural brasileiro. Se na década de 1980 a suposta direita conciliatória cedia terras públicas a empreendimentos agropecuários, hoje a direita quer privatizar as praias e abrir as terras indígenas para a mineração. 


A partir da união de seringueiros e indígenas, a luta dos povos da Amazônia foi projetada para o mundo, levando preocupação aos chefes dos bancos de desenvolvimento internacionais. O Banco Mundial e o Banco Interamericano de Desenvolvimento (BID) estavam liberando empréstimos para a criação de pólos de produção pecuária e financiando a abertura de estradas que cortavam os territórios tradicionais. Chico Mendes, em uma viagem emblemática a Washington, em 1987, conseguiu congelar alguns destes financiamentos e, como sabemos, pagou com a vida por sua coragem.


Mas sua luta sobreviveu: da profusão de ideias e da resistência criada surgiram outras lideranças, entre elas Marina Silva, a mais jovem senadora a ser eleita pelo Acre, na década de 1990, e depois a ministra de Meio Ambiente nas gestões de Lula. Ela levou a política ambiental para o coração do governo e conseguiu, com o apoio dos melhores cientistas e gestores, provar que é possível conter o desmatamento.


No momento em que escrevo estas linhas, saem notícias mostrando que, em

2025, as taxas de derrubadas

 no Brasil atingiram nova baixa histórica. E o melhor, estes resultados já não estão se restringindo à Amazônia. Os dados do Deter, o sistema de alertas de desmatamento do INPE, mostraram

uma redução de 30% em setembro

 no Cerrado. Uma notícia fantástica, uma vez que este é o bioma sob maior pressão, onde a ilegalidade e invasão de terras prosperaram nos últimos anos. 


Um dos alicerces da política de Lula e Marina para barrar a sanha destruidora é exatamente o combate à grilagem de terras e a promoção da regularização fundiária.

Estudos de renomadas organizações não governamentais

 como o Instituto de Pesquisas da Amazônia (IPAM) têm mostrado que, nos últimos anos, com os embargos e a repressão ao desmatamento em propriedades privadas, os criminosos passaram a fazer mais queimadas e derrubadas em unidades de conservação e terras indígenas.


A grilagem de terras e a invasão de territórios indígenas definem muito o que é o Brasil. Nossa história colonial foi brutal contra os povos da floresta e seus efeitos sobre o nosso cotidiano perduram até hoje, como a persistência da violência no campo e as ameaças constantes sofridas por comunidades rurais.

Nesta polarização tremenda que vive o país, temos falado muito do interior e como a cultura do agro tem ajudado a definir os votos. Mas somos um país atlântico, com identidade litorânea e com uma conexão muito forte com as praias. Por isso, enquanto alertamos para o que está ocorrendo na floresta, não podemos deixar de apontar a especulação imobiliária que pode vir a transformar a costa brasileira.


A Proposta de Emenda Constitucional para regularizar a venda dos terrenos da Marinha

gerou enorme polêmica em 2024

. E agora, nesta eleição, voltou ao debate, pois ninguém menos do que Flávio Bolsonaro é o relator da proposta, que ficou conhecida como a PEC da Privatização das Praias. A ideia é permitir a venda de terras que ficam numa faixa que começa a 33 metros dos pontos mais altos de maré e que pertencem historicamente à União. O argumento dos defensores da proposta é de que isso levaria mais investimentos, em forma de condomínios e resorts, ao nosso litoral. Na prática, isso pode se tornar uma forma de fechar acessos e criar praias exclusivas para os donos do dinheiro.


Diante desta ameaça, fiquei imaginando se não seria o momento da Aliança …

author: Gastbeitrag
title: Das Schweigen brechen – Wie eine Konferenz sexistischer Polizeigewalt den Kampf ansagt
content:
Am 18.10. findet in Berlin Kreuzberg eine Konferenz gegen sexualisierte Polizeigewalt statt. Die Organisator:innen sind vor allem politisch aktive Frauen aus unterschiedlichen Organisationen, wie ZORA oder der Prisoners Voice Platform (TSP). Wir haben mit ihnen über ihre konkreten Erfahrungen, das Programm der Konferenz und über die größeren Ziele gesprochen.


Interview: Osa Udushesheri


Könnt ihr euch einmal vorstellen und sagen, was euch dazu gebracht hat, die Konferenz gegen sexualisierte Polizeigewalt zu organisieren?


Erstmal lieben Dank für das Interview! Wir sind vor allem politisch aktive Frauen aus unterschiedlichen Organisationen wie ZORA und Prisoners Voice Platform (TSP – Tutsakların Sesi Platformu), aber wir werden in der Vorbereitung von vielen unterschiedlichen Genoss:innen und Organisationen begleitet, die schon in der Vergangenheit solche Konferenz z.B. in der Türkei gegen Vergewaltigung in Haft organisiert haben und im Kampf dagegen erfolgreich waren. Die Konferenz ist also ein Ergebnis vieler Genoss:innen, ein Ergebnis der Erfahrungen, die Frauen schon vor uns gesammelt haben.

Das hat uns aber vor allem dazu gebracht diese Konferenz zu planen: Auf Palästinademonstrationen in Berlin sehen wir auf fast jeder Aktion wie Frauen an die Brüste gefasst wird, wie Frauen der Hijab abgerissen wird, wie vor allem Polizisten ihre Macht gegenüber Frauen ausnutzen. Denken wir auch an die Aktionen des Rheinmetall-Entwaffnen-Camps. Auf der Großdemo 2025 wurden Aktivist:innen 12 Stunden im Kessel gehalten und die Polizei ging äußerst brutal gegen Frauen vor. Auch dieses Jahr bei den Blockadeaktionen des RME-Camps berichteten uns viele von Griffen in die Hose oder an die Brust, von sexistischen und abwertigen Kommentare und anderen Formen sexualisierter Polizeigewalt. Was besonders auffiel sind die Nacktdurchsuchungen die grundlos von Polizisten durchgeführt werden hier in Deutschland, es scheint fast so als solle das zur Normalität werden, in Fällen von Blockadeaktionen oder ähnlichem.


Vor allem nach den Veröffentlichungen im Dezember 2025 von Anna Liedtke zu der Vergewaltigung in israelischer Haft, kam es zu vielen weiteren Berichten der Flotilla-Aktivist:innen, die von sexualisierter Gewalt und Folter seitens der IDF berichtet haben. Auch während der People’s Caravan, die Anfang des Jahres nach Kobane reisen wollte, um von den Geschehnissen zu berichten folgten Veröffentlichungen zu körperlicher und sexualisierter Folter. Die Aktivistin der Föderation Klassenkämpferischer Organisationen Paula Maier machte im August dieses Jahres eine Veröffentlichung, bei der sie bekannt machte, dass sie bei der Jugenddelegation nach Bakur mit vielen anderen Aktivist:innen festgenommen wurde und dann in einer Einzelzelle von einem türkischen Beamten vergewaltigt wurde.

Das sind alles Fälle, die sich in den letzten Jahren gehäuft haben und zum Thema gemacht werden sollten. Wir sehen also wie unsere eigenen Körper als Waffe gegen uns selbst genutzt werden. Uns ist natürlich bewusst, dass überall da wo Frauen Widerstand leisten der Staat mit Repression antwortet. Obwohl das Thema jetzt aktuell ist, haben wir es als Frauenbewegung und linke Bewegung nicht geschafft, dass es Teil unserer Antirepressionsarbeit wird oder auch ein bewusster Kampf dagegen stattfindet.

Die Konferenz dient also als ein Ort, an dem wir als Bewegung zusammenkommen, uns austauschen über internationale Erfahrungen von Genoss:innen, über die Probleme, die wir aktuell haben und vor allem wie wir dagegen kämpfen können. Es soll für alle Menschen sein, die politisch interessiert sind, schon aktiv sind, Betroffene oder einfach jene, die was lernen möchten.


Was ist sexualisierte Polizeigewalt? Inwiefern spiegelt sexualisierte Gewalt die Strukturen der Polizei wider? Gibt es Unterschiede zu anderen Formen der Repression und der Polizeigewalt?


Die letzten Jahre haben uns deutlich gezeigt, dass die Polizeigewalt im Allgemeinen gegen alle, die gegen Krieg, Genozid, Ausbeutung und gegen dieses System kämpfen, sehr stark zugenommen hat. Der Staat hat vor allem auf eine starke Palästinabewegung mit brutaler Polizeigewalt und staatlicher Verfolgung geantwortet. Diese Repressionen, die wir in allen Bewegungen und Kämpfen erleben haben das Ziel durch Angst und Gewalt Einzelpersonen, aber auch ganze Kollektive von ihrem politischen Gedanken und Aktivismus abzubringen. Sexualisierte Polizeigewalt wurde bisher in Deutschland häufig auf eine Kontinuität der steigenden …

title: İklim krizi ve kötü hava: Risk kuryede, kâr platform şirketlerinde
content:
14 Ekim’de ben de sahadaydım. Eminönü, Balat, Alibeyköy ve Maslak hattında teslim etmem gereken siparişler vardı. Hava bir bastırıyor, bir normale dönüyordu; ara ara sağanak geliyor, sonra kesiliyordu. Sağanağın en sert anına Sirkeci’de yakalandım. Ana arterler kullanılamaz haldeydi, her yer göle dönmüştü. Motosikletle yol almaktan çok suda yüzüyor gibiydik.


Haberleri takip etmek için bile sığındığımız benzinlikler motosikletçilerle doluydu. Duraklara sığınan insanlar bankların üstüne çıkmıştı. Bot da olsa yağmurluk da olsa, üzerimizdeki ekipmanın hiçbiri o yağmura dayanmadı. Bazı bölgeler tamamen kilitlenmişti. Motosikletin her zaman bulduğu dar aralar bile kapanmıştı ve suyun içinde kaldığımız çok an oldu. Böylesini ilk kez gördüm.


14 Ekim bize bir kez daha şunu gösterdi. Kötü havada kurye ya çalışıp canını riske atıyor ya da çalışamayıp gelirini kaybediyor. Her iki durumda da faturayı kurye ödüyor.


Kuryelerin karlı havada çalışma koşulları: Tehlikeler, baskılar ve haklar


24 Şubat 2025


Sağanağı sele çeviren kent


Vali Davut Gül’ün açıklamasına göre İstanbul’da metrekareye 261 kilogram yağış düştü. Bu, Meteoroloji’nin ölçüme başladığı 1942'den bu yana kentte görülen en yüksek değer. Önceki rekor 200 kilograma yakındı. Valilik bugün 3 kişinin hayatını kaybettiğini, 2 bin 722 kişinin kurtarıldığını açıkladı.


Aşırı sıcaklar, ani sağanaklar ve fırtınalar artık istisna değil. İklim krizi bu olayları sıklaştırıyor. Ama aşırı yağışın sele, selin de afete dönüşmesi kaçınılmaz bir doğa olayı değil. Bunu büyük ölçüde kentin nasıl kurulduğu belirliyor. Betonlaşan kentte yağmur suyu toprağa sızamıyor. Dere yataklarına yerleşim alanları kuruluyor. Altyapı, büyüyen kentin gerisinde kalıyor. Ana arterlerde aşırı yağışa karşı alternatif tahliye sistemleri bulunmuyor. Sonuçta yollar dakikalar içinde göle dönüyor.


Bu tablo tek bir kurumun ya da tek bir dönemin eseri değil. İmar kararlarını veren merkezi yönetim de altyapıdan sorumlu yerel yönetimler de bu sonuçta pay sahibi. İklim krizi bir etken ama altyapı yeterli olsa, kent bu kadar betonlaşmasa ve dere yatakları yapılaşmaya açılmasa aynı yağış bu kadar büyük bir yıkıma yol açmazdı.


Kurye için trafik iş yeridir


Bu tablonun en ağır yükünü açık havada çalışanlar taşıyor. Kuryeler, inşaat, temizlik, tarım ve belediye işçileri… Çoğumuz için trafik, bir yerden bir yere gitmek için kullandığımız bir ulaşım alanı. Kurye için ise trafik iş yerinin ta kendisi. Ofiste çalışan biri için kötü hava, işe gidip gelirken katlanılan bir zorluk, kurye içinse ise iş yerinin baştan sona tehlikeli hale gelmesi demek. Görüş mesafesinin düşmesi, kaygan ve su basmış zemin, artan kaza riski, kuryenin iş yerindeki çalışma koşullarıdır.


Bu yüzden kötü havayı bir hava durumu haberi olarak değil bir iş sağlığı ve güvenliği meselesi olarak konuşmamız gerekiyor. Göle dönen bir cadde, kurye için su basmış bir iş yeridir. Yazın aşırı sıcak, kışın buzlanma da aynı meselenin parçası.


Uyarı vardı, tedbir gün içinde geldi


Kuryeler 14 Ekim’de gün boyu sağanak ve fırtına altında sipariş taşıdı.

Kurye Haber

’e gün boyunca çok sayıda kaza ihbarı ulaştı. Beşiktaş’ta bir kuryenin motosikleti suya gömüldü. Bir başka görüntüde bir kurye, sele kapılmamak için devrilen motosikletine tutunuyordu. Kocaeli, Sakarya ve Antalya’daki kuryeler de benzer koşullarda çalıştıklarını gösteren video ve tanıklıklarını doğrudan Kurye Haber’e iletti.


Vali Gül ertesi gün, vatandaşların meteorolojik uyarıları dikkate almasının can kaybını ve zararları azalttığını söyledi. Bu açıklama, uyarıların önceden yapıldığını resmi ağızdan teyit ediyor. Meteorolojik veriler tedbirin çok önceden alınmasını gerektirse de motosiklet yasağı ancak gün içinde, hava çoktan kötüleşmişken, saat 18.30 sularında açıklandı. Yasak ise 21.00'de başladı. Kuryeler yasağın açıklandığı andan uygulanmaya başladığı saate kadar bile şiddetli yağış altında çalışmak zorunda kaldı. Önleyici tedbir, zorluklar yaşandıktan sonra değil, yaşanmadan önce alınmalı.


Ama sorumluluk yalnızca valilikte değil. Platform şirketleri, uyarıları herkes kadar bilmesine rağmen sistemlerini kapatmak için valilik kararını bekledi ve yasak gelene kadar sipariş almaya devam etti. Kuryelerin can güvenliği kuryeleri çalıştıran şirketlerin değil, valiliğin kararına bırakıldı.


Yasak geldiğinde de herkes uymadı. Kurye Haber’e özellikle mahalle aralarındaki işletmelerle ilgili şikâyetler ulaştı. Kısa mesafelerde denetim olmayacağını düşünen bazı yerel işletme sahipleri …
