title: Second death sentence for Warisha Moradi
content:
Warisha Moradi, a Kurdish political prisoner and women’s rights activist, has been sentenced to death for a second time by Branch 15 of Tehran’s Revolutionary Court. This time, the charge is of “membership in a rebel group”.


Her lawyers say the court issued the new sentence without completing the investigations requested by the Supreme Court, and simply changed the charge. The Supreme Court had overturned her first death sentence because of incomplete investigations and procedural violations. Her lawyers say there is insufficient evidence to support the charge and will appeal within the 20-day deadline.


Moradi has been in detention since the summer of 2023.

title: Talabani receives Bakırhan, reaffirms PUK’s support for the peace process in Turkey
content:
Bafel Jalal Talabani, President of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), received Tuncer Bakırhan, Co-Chair of the DEM Party, in Dabashan.


The meeting on Wednesday was attended by Shanaz Ibrahim Ahmed and Dr Yousif Goran, members of the PUK Political Bureau, and Salar Lala Sarhad, Head of the Kurdistani Relations Board. Discussions focused on continuing joint coordination and cooperation and strengthening bilateral relations in pursuit of shared interests and greater regional stability.


The two sides also exchanged views on the peace process in Turkey. Bafel Talabani reaffirmed the PUK’s support for this historic initiative, stating: “We will continue to follow the same policy pursued by President Mam Jalal until this vital and decisive process succeeds. We believe that peace and coexistence enable us to serve our people, whereas war and division bring nothing but destruction. I therefore hope that everyone will turn a new page and work towards lasting peace.”


For his part, Bakırhan thanked Talabani and the PUK for their efforts to advance the peace process, saying: “We highly value your role and appreciate your steps in support of stability and peaceful coexistence in the region.”


Photos: PUKMEDIA

title: Savary-Borioli: If Turkey wants peace, it must release Öcalan
content:
Swiss politician and emergency physician Dr. Beppe Savary-Borioli believes that a lasting resolution to the Kurdish question is hardly conceivable without Abdullah Öcalan’s freedom and the fundamental democratization of Turkey. Speaking to ANF, the member of the Ticino cantonal parliament expressed serious doubts about the Turkish government’s willingness to secure the current peace process through binding political and legal guarantees. At the same time, he sees Öcalan’s concept of democratic confederalism as offering a perspective that extends beyond the Kurdish question.


Since Öcalan’s February 27, 2025, Call for Peace and Democratic Society, the Kurdish freedom movement has taken far-reaching steps toward ending the armed struggle against Turkey. According to Savary-Borioli, however, the future of this process depends crucially on whether Ankara is prepared to establish the political conditions necessary for a negotiated settlement on equal terms.


https://1649452211.rsc.cdn77.org/20261013215028_2026-10-14-habermerkezi-dr-beppe-savary-isvicreli-siyasetci-baris-icin-ocalan-ozgur-olmali-1.mp4


“If Turkey truly wants peace, it must release Öcalan”


Savary-Borioli described Öcalan’s continued imprisonment as a fundamental contradiction within the peace process. He stated that a government genuinely seeking a political settlement must allow the Kurdish side’s most important negotiating partner to fulfill his role freely.


“The crucial question for me is this: If Turkey truly wants peace, it must release Öcalan. As long as it fails to do so, everything else lacks credibility,” Savary-Borioli stated.


The politician criticized the authoritarian system of government under President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, comparing his approach to power to that of a sultan. By contrast, he described Öcalan as one of the most important figures capable of making a shared, peaceful future possible for the Kurdish and Turkish populations. Savary-Borioli also referred to the experience of South Africa’s peace process, noting that negotiations to end apartheid gained decisive momentum only after Nelson Mandela’s release. He sees a similar prerequisite for Turkey.


“We cannot speak of negotiations on equal terms when one side is represented by a prisoner and the other by a president who behaves like a sultan. That is simply impossible.”


Doubts about the Turkish government’s guarantees


Savary-Borioli considers the Kurdish freedom movement’s strategic decision to end the armed struggle in favor of political and diplomatic means an important step. However, he believes, a unilateral change in strategy cannot guarantee lasting peace. In particular, he doubts that the Turkish government will actually fulfill its obligations toward former PKK members. A state that disregards international legal norms must first demonstrate that its commitments are credible and reliable, he underlines.


In this context, Savary-Borioli recalled the symbolic burning of weapons by the Kurdish freedom movement in July 2025, which he had personally attended. He said the action had demonstrated the movement’s political will but had not prompted any immediate corresponding steps from the state.


“I remain skeptical. Will a state like Turkey, which does not respect international law, actually honor the guarantees it gives to PKK members after they lay down their weapons?” Savary-Borioli asked. He therefore continues to observe current developments with considerable caution. What matters, he stressed, is not political announcements but verifiable changes to the legal and democratic framework.


Democratization as the foundation for coexistence


Savary-Borioli sees the democratization of the Turkish state as another prerequisite for a lasting political settlement. He argued that the political system is heavily centered on the presidency, while parliament has only limited influence over fundamental decisions.


“Under these conditions, any peace agreement would remain politically uncertain, as its implementation would depend on the position of the country’s leadership at any given time. As long as Turkey does not become a genuinely democratic state, it is extremely difficult to imagine real peace between the Kurdish and Turkish peoples,” Savary-Borioli stated.


He explicitly distinguished between the Turkish population and the government or military. He remarked that the people of both societies could and should live together peacefully. However, this would require …

title: Îstixbarata Sûriyeyê ragihand ku wan Mihraç Ural zeft kiriye
content:
Ajansa nûçeyan a fermî ya Sûriyeyê SANAyê ragihand ku Mihraç Uralê ku li Sûriyeyê bi navê ‘Elî Kiyalî’ tê nasîn, dema hewl dida ji sînor bireve hat zeftkirin.


Dezgehên Sûriyeyê derbarê wê yekê de hûrgilî parve nekirin ku operasyon li ser kîjan xeta sînorî hat encamdan.


SANAyê destnîşan kir ku Mihraç Ural ji aliyê Servîsa Sîxuriyê ya Giştî ya Sûriyeyê ve hat zeftkirin ku ev jî “bi operasyoneke taybet ku di nav koordînasyona MİTê de hat encamdan”. Her weha fotografê Ural jî hate parve kirin.


المجرم علي كيالي، المعروف بـ"معراج أورال"، في قبضة جهاز الاستخبارات العامة، وذلك في عملية نوعية نُفذت بالتنسيق مع جهاز الاستخبارات التركي. #سانا https://t.co/DvgQn5ojMu


— الوكالة العربية السورية للأنباء - سانا (@Sana__gov)

October 15, 2026


Hat îdiakirin li nêzî Beyrûtê revandine


Di çapemeniya Libnanê de jî derbarê cihê ku Ural lê hatiye zeftkirin û awayê encamdana operasyona hatiye kirin de agahiyên cuda cih girtin.


Televizyona MTVyê ya ku navenda wê li Libnanê ye îdia kir ku Ural ji mala xwe ya li Mansuriyeyê ku li bakurê rojhilatê Beyrûtê girêdayî herêma Metnê ye, ji aliyê kesên nasnameya wan nediyar ve hatiye revandin û paşê ew birine Sûriyeyê.


MTVyê ragihand ku di dema serdegirtinê de hevjîn û kurê Ural hatine girêdan û Şaxa Îstixbaratê ya serbi Hêzên Ewlehiya Navxweyî ya Libnanê derbarê bûyerê de lêpirsîn daye destpêkirin.


Malbenda Çavdêriyê ya Mafên Mirovan a Sûriyeyê (SOHR) ku navenda wê li Londonê ye jî, li ser bingeha agahiyên ku ji çavkaniyên xwe wergirtine ragihand ku Ural piştî ku ji Nexweşxaneya Resulu’l-Azam a li Beyrûtê vegeriyaye, bi ser mala wî ya li Mansuriyeyê girtine û ew zeft kirine.


Malbendê ragihand ku kesên ku operasyon pêkanîne bi devoka Libnanê bi erebî axivîne, lê belê nasnameya wan hîn nehatiye diyarkirin.


Parvekirinên Balyozê Şamê Nuh Yilmazî


Balyozê Tirkiyeyê ê Şamê Nuh Yilmaz jî piştî nûçeyên girtina Ural, parvekirina xwe ya 4ê Cotmehê ji nû ve parve kir û nivîsî: “Elhamdulillah! Qehr û xezeba me li dijmin bibe malwêranî! eûzubillâh, eûzubillâh. xudâ ya şukr-i bihad!”


Yilmaz di 4ê Cotmehê de di parvekirina xwe de ragihandibû alîkarê Ural ê ku wekî Cemal Trablusi tê zanîn ji aliyê hêzên ewlehiyê yên Sûriyeyê ve hat zeftkirin û weha gotibû, “Gav bi Gav!!”.


Elhamdülillah! Kahrımız, gazabımız düşmana ziyân! eûzubillâh, eûzubillâh. hüdâ'ya şükr-i bihad!


— Nuh Yılmaz (@nuhyilmaz)

October 15, 2026


Banga SOHRê ya ji bo darizandina li Baniyasê


Dezgehên Sûriyeyê Mihraç Ural di nav berpirsiyarên komkujiyên ku di sala 2013an de li Baniyasê hatine kirin de nîşan didin.


Di gundê El-Beyda ê bajarê Tartusê ya Sûriyeyê û taxa Ras el-Nebe ya Baniyasê de, di 2-3ê Gulana 2013an de di êrişên ku ji aliyê hêzên girêdayî rêveberiya Esad ve hatin kirin de gelek sivîlan jiyana xwe ji dest dan.


Rêxistina Şopandinê a Mafên Mirovan (HRW) di Îlona 2013an de raporek weşandibû û li gorî wê raporê, hêzên hikûmetê û komên çekdar ên ku bi wan re, li du herêman herî kêm 248 kes kuştin.


Komîsyona Lêpirsîna Navneteweyî ya Serbixwe ya Sûriyeyê ya Neteweyên Yekbûyî jî di rapora xwe ya sala 2013an de cih da tespîtên ku nîşan didin hêzên hikûmetê û komên çekdar ên ku bi wan re ji komkujiyan berpirsiyar in.


Raporên HRW û Komîsyona Lêpirsînê ya NYyê derbarê berpirsiyariya takekesî ya Ural a di êrişan de li xwe nagire. title: Νεολαιίστικη εξέγερση στη Γαλλία:Τον κόσμο ή τίποτα! Νέο ραντεβού στις 17 Οκτώβρη
content:
Παρίσι – Ανταπόκριση: Ηρώ Σιαφλιάκη


Περισσότεροι από 500.000 υπολογίζονται οι διαδηλωτές στη Γαλλία κατά την 5η πράξη των κινητοποιήσεων, την Τρίτη 13 Οκτώβρη. Η διαδήλωση των μαθητών, αρκετών φοιτητών, καθηγητών και πολλών άλλων ξεκίνησε από το Δημαρχείο

H

ô

tel de Ville  υπό

τους ήχους μιας Ορχήστρας διακοσίων ατόμων. Η πορεία, με την αναγνωρίσιμη πια χαρούμενη αποφασιστικότητά της, πέρασε το ποτάμι και κατέληξε στην πλατεία

Invalides

, όχι μακριά από το 

Matignon

,

στο 7ο διαμέρισμα του Παρισιού, επίσημη κατοικία και ο τόπος εργασίας του αρχηγού της γαλλικής κυβέρνησης. Εκεί, και επί μία ώρα, οι αστυνομικοί, αφού έκλεισαν κάθε έξοδο, πλημμύρισαν την πλατεία με δακρυγόνα.


Μια δεύτερη διαδήλωση, των συνδικάτων (αυτή μόνο είχε δηλωθεί) ξεκίνησε από την

Place d

’

Italie

 με ίδια κατάληξη.


Επεισόδια σημειώθηκαν σε αρκετές περιοχές, με την ίδια πάντα σκληρή στάση της αστυνομίας

1

, αλλά προφανώς το κίνημα δεν φαίνεται να πτοείται. Αντίθετα, όλοι περιμένουν την 17η Οκτώβρη. Εδώ και δύο περίπου μήνες, ένα κάλεσμα που θυμίζει Κίτρινα γιλέκα διαδίδεται παντού, προσδιορίζοντας μόνο αυτή τη μέρα ως αρχή γενικευμένων κινητοποιήσεων.


Κάλεσμα σε γενική απεργία


Μέσα στον γενικό πανικό ένα δακρυγόνο αστυνομικών

έπεσε ανάμεσα

 σε άλλους αστυνομικούς

2

.


Το 90% των Πανεπιστημίων παρέμειναν και την Τετάρτη έως τις 14.10, κλειστά. Επίσης, περισσότερα από 200 λύκεια παραμένουν μπλοκαρισμένα. Σε πολλές περιπτώσεις τα μαθήματα που προσπάθησαν να γίνουν μέσω ιντερνέτ χακαρίστηκαν.


Και οι φοιτητές των ελίτ πανεπιστημίων στους δρόμους


Ένα από τα πιο αξιοσημείωτα χαρακτηριστικά του κινήματος η συμμετοχή φοιτητών από ελίτ και ιδιωτικά εκπαιδευτικά ιδρύματα, όπως το HEC Paris, το Stanislas, το Καθολικό Πανεπιστήμιο της Λιλ, το Καθολικό Ινστιτούτο του Παρισιού, το Audencia και τα Sciences Po. Οι αποκλεισμοί και οι εκδηλώσεις αλληλεγγύης σε αυτά τα ιδρύματα αποτελούν ένδειξη ότι η εξέγερση υπερβαίνει τα παραδοσιακά κοινωνικά και ταξικά όρια. Ακόμη και νέοι από προνομιούχα περιβάλλοντα συντάσσονται με τους μαθητές των λαϊκών συνοικιών, αμφισβητώντας την κοινωνική ανισότητα και τις υπάρχουσες δομές εξουσίας.


Εγκαταλείψτε τη σύγχρονη εποχή


Κυβέρνηση και κυρίαρχα μέσα ενημέρωσης επιχειρούν να αποδώσουν τις κινητοποιήσεις στο αριστερό κόμμα La France Insoumise και στον Ζαν-Λυκ Μελανσόν, σε μία προσπάθεια να υποτιμήσουν τη δυναμική και την αυτονομία του κινήματος.Παράλληλα, οργανώσεις Καθολικών και Προτεσταντών προσκόπων εκφράζουν την υποστήριξή τους, ζητώντας να ακουστούν οι νέοι και να συμμετέχουν ουσιαστικά στη δημοκρατική ζωή.


Παρακάτω ένα κείμενο από καθηγητή λυκείου στο προάστιο του Παρισιού, Μοντρέιγ:


Μια χειροβομβίδα απεμπλοκής κοστίζει 52 ευρώ. Ένα σχολικό εγχειρίδιο μαθηματικών της «

Seconde

» (Β’ Λυκείου) κοστίζει κατά μέσο όρο 33 ευρώ. Το βιβλίο είναι επαναχρησιμοποιούμενο.


Ένας εκτοξευτής

LBD

 για να τυφλώνουν τα παιδιά μας κοστίζει 1280 ευρώ·Που ισοδυναμεί με 20 καλούς ανεμιστήρες για να «δροσιστούν» οι σχολικές αίθουσες.


Ένα δακρυγόνο κοστίζει περίπου 30 ευρώ, Ενώ ένα γεύμα στη σχολική καντίνα στην περιοχή της Ιλ-ντε-Φρανς κοστίζει το πολύ 9,80 ευρώ.


Μια διμοιρία

CRS

 (μονάδα καταστολής) κοστίζει 40.000 ευρώ την ημέρα, Που ισοδυναμεί με 576 ώρες αναπλήρωσης ενός/μιας εκπαιδευτικού.


Και το πιο σοκαριστικό είναι το συνολικό κόστος μιας ημέρας καταστολής, και ακόμη κι αν για τις διαδηλώσεις των μαθητών λυκείου δεν έχει ακόμη υπολογιστεί, μπορούμε να το συγκρίνουμε με τις διαδηλώσεις στη Σαιντ-Σολίν (

Sainte

–

Soline

) το 2023. Η αστυνομική δύναμη κόστισε 3,4 εκατομμύρια ευρώ για μόλις 3 ημέρες.


Σήμερα λέγεται ότι αυτές οι μαθητικές διαδηλώσεις κοστίζουν ακριβά, αλλά συχνά ξεχνάμε να υπενθυμίσουμε ότι η αστυνομία είναι υπεύθυνη για ένα πολύ μεγάλο μέρος αυτών των καταστροφών, ΔΙΟΤΙ μια βίαιη απάντηση από την πλευρά της αστυνομίας προκαλεί πάντα κλιμάκωση της βίας.


1


Μεταξύ άλλων, μπορούμε να αναφέρουμε πως στην Τουλούζη αστυνομικός πέταξε δακρυγόνο σε μπαλκόνι πολυκατοικίας. Το 2018, ακριβώς έτσι σκοτώθηκε η

Zineb


Redouane

, στο διαμέρισμά της στη Μασσαλία, κατά τη διάρκεια διαδήλωσης των Κίτρινων Γιλέκων.


O μακρονισμός φαίνεται να χάνει την κοινωνική νομιμοποίησή του στους νέους. Μια ολόκληρη γενιά διεκδικεί ένα διαφορετικό μέλλον, με αιτήματα που δεν αφορούν μόνο σε συγκεκριμένα προβλήματα της εκπαίδευσης, αλλά κυρίως την αναγνώρισή τους ως ενεργών υποκειμένων της δημοκρατικής ζωής.

content:
“There’s so much power in this fight,” says Saul Levin.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Across the country, communities are fighting back against the construction of AI data centers and winning. In this episode of Movement Memos, Kelly Hayes talks with Saul Levin, host of The Hum, about the growing movement against Big Tech’s infrastructure boom and the strategies organizers are using to stop these projects. They discuss how unlikely coalitions are building power, sharing tactics, and challenging the political and corporate forces seeking to override local communities.

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik health board developing local rehabilitation services
content:
Nunavik residents could have greater access to specialized rehabilitation services closer to home through a new partnership aimed at providing orthotics, prosthetics and positioning services within the region.


The Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services announced the partnership Oct. 13 in a news release with Quebec Health Centre-West-of-Montreal University and the Constance-Lethbridge Rehabilitation Centre.


With the initiative, residents will have access to equipment fitting and follow-up care without needing to travel outside the region for some services.


Orthotics are devices, such as braces or specially fitted supports, that help stabilize or protect parts of the body. Prosthetics are artificial limbs or other devices that replace a missing body part. Positioning services involve selecting and adapting equipment, such as wheelchairs, seating systems and other supports.


A technologist specializing in orthotics, prosthetics and orthopedic care will be regularly present in Nunavik, the release said.


Assessments and moulding will be conducted in local communities, allowing patients to receive some services without travelling south.


When devices must be manufactured in Montreal, they will be transported back to Nunavik for fitting and delivery to patients.


The initiative is intended to improve access to specialized care, support continuity of treatment and provide services adapted to the realities of Nunavik’s communities, the release said.


The announcement does not specify when the services will begin, which communities will be served first or how frequently the specialized technologist will visit the region.


Nunatsiaq News reached out to the health board for further information but did not receive a response at the time of publication.

title: Imprisoned journalist Ahmed Polad’s father: Don’t leave him alone
content:
Journalist Ahmed Polad, who was abducted and detained by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS) on 18 January 2026 while covering events in Syria, was handed over to Turkey on 9 September 2026 after spending eight months in HTS prisons. Polad was subsequently arrested in Turkey. His father, Adil Aslan, appealed to the public to draw attention to his son's situation.


Ahmed Polad and Eva Maria Michelmann, who had been working as journalists in Rojava for many years, were abducted on 18 January 2026 during HTS attacks on Raqqa. Following a prisoner exchange on 11 April 2026, testimonies from people held in HTS prisons revealed that both journalists were in detention.


Once their whereabouts became known, campaigns demanding their release were organised in Turkey, Kurdistan and around the world. Following public pressure, HTS handed German journalist Eva Maria Michelmann over to Germany on 18 June 2026.


Eight months of torture in HTS prisons and a padded cell at MIT


Polad's whereabouts were finally confirmed on 9 September 2026. He was handed over to Turkey by HTS and subsequently remanded in custody by a court. In a report documenting his eight months in detention, Polad's lawyers stated that the journalist had been subjected to months of torture by HTS and had contracted scabies because of the unsanitary conditions and inadequate nutrition in prison.


The report also stated that immediately after being handed over to Turkey, Polad was interrogated for two days by the National Intelligence Organisation (MIT) and held in a padded cell for two days.


Polad described his experiences to his lawyers in the report: “On 18 January 2026, my German journalist colleague Eva Maria Michelmann and I were covering events in the Raqqa region of Syria when the building we were in was surrounded. We were detained after security forces entered the building. We were taken to a police station that I would describe as the Aleppo General Security Headquarters. The place where we were held was underground. It was a cell with no light, no fresh air and no ventilation. It measured one metre by two and a half metres. I was never taken outside. I never saw fresh air or daylight. The only exception was one week when I was held in a ward with around 190 to 200 people, including members of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). For the first month, I was tortured every day. Three or four times a day, groups of people would enter my cell and start beating me. They tortured me by kicking me in the head, forcing me to the ground and crushing my head. Later, the torture became predominantly psychological. They would come at night and say things like, ‘Be ready in the morning, you will be executed,’ or ‘Be ready tomorrow, you will be beheaded.’”


Held in solitary confinement in Silivri


Polad is currently being held in a solitary cell at Marmara L-Type Prison in Silivri. His lawyers have said that his health is poor and that he urgently needs medical treatment. Polad's father, Adil Aslan, spoke to ANF about what the family had experienced over the past eight months and called on the public to show solidarity with his son.


‘We received no reliable information for eight months’


Adil Aslan said the family learned of Polad's abduction on 28 February and had lived in constant fear for his safety. Aslan also said: “He was detained by HTS gangs in Raqqa on 18 January, together with German journalist Eva Maria. We learned about it on 28 February, when the news became public. Naturally, we became extremely worried because the people who took them were truly brutal. If they had any humanity, we would not have been so distressed. We were constantly afraid. I kept saying, ‘These are barbaric people. They will murder our son. They will torture him to death or make him disappear.’ That fear was always with us, and we lived with it. For eight months, we received no reliable information whatsoever. Around 6 April, one or two eyewitnesses came forward. They claimed that Ahmed and Eva had been taken out of the same building together. We were told that they had been put into another vehicle and taken somewhere else. But those holding them refused to acknowledge it. They kept claiming, ‘We do not have anyone by that name.’ Despite repeated attempts by the lawyers, they never admitted holding him.”


‘They also interrogated our lawyer in Damascus’

title: Cahit Berkay: Justice will strengthen trust in the peace process
content:
Artists continue to express their support for the Peace and Democratic Society Process through ANF. Musician Cahit Berkay welcomed the silencing of weapons and said swift, concrete steps were needed to advance the process. He stressed that justice was fundamental to peace and drew attention to the importance of freedom to use one's mother tongue.


‘The guns have fallen silent, now further steps must follow’


Musician Cahit Berkay told ANF: “The most important thing was for the guns to fall silent. This was a very welcome decision. Now further steps must follow. The way has been opened for that. It seems this process will be pursued more seriously than previous ones. I hope it achieves its goal.”


Berkay, who described love as his philosophy of life, continued: “My approach to these issues, my philosophy of life, is that love lies at the heart of everything. Peace is something that can be achieved by people who are capable of genuinely and properly feeling, building and experiencing love. Love begins with a person's respect and love for themselves. It then extends to their loved ones, friends, country, the world and the universe. Love also keeps our conscience alive.


When this becomes the foundation, every approach, every word you speak and every intention you feel is rooted in sincerity. As a result, nobody deceives anyone or sets traps for one another. Love is the foundation of everything. Since we are on the subject, let me ask: What was the central theme of Selvi Boylum Al Yazmalım (The Girl with the Red Scarf)? Love is effort. That energy, too, is a manifestation of the love a person carries within them. If you want that love to survive, you must make an effort. Nothing can be achieved without effort.”


‘Music brings people in Edirne and Batman together’


Berkay spoke about the powerful role music plays in bringing different peoples together.


Berkay said: “I have experienced this effect personally, and I still do. For example, I always play Al Yazmalım at every concert. I have played it in Batman (Êlih), Diyarbakır (Amed) and Edirne. I have also performed it in many European countries. Kurdish and Turkish people come together through the same song. They applaud the same notes. Twenty years ago, I performed at a voluntary event in Diyarbakır and Batman. As soon as the first notes of Al Yazmalım began, a wave of zılgıt (traditional celebratory ululation) erupted. I got goosebumps and started trembling. I cannot describe that feeling.”


‘Peace comes through justice’


Cahit Berkay also spoke about the relationship between art and peace: “Art makes an enormous contribution to building and sustaining peace. Most artists are thoughtful, sincere people who carry love within them and care about humanity. I believe peace is one of the central themes of art. Sculptors, painters and musicians all take peace as a theme in their work.


For decades, we have been struggling desperately, if you'll excuse the expression, to achieve peace. We must establish peace and restore our inner tranquillity as soon as possible. But of course, this can only happen through rights, the rule of law and justice. Without these, nothing else works.


Without justice, there will be plots and attempts to undermine peace, as well as crimes against humanity. That is why it is so important for the justice system to function properly. Justice will also strengthen trust in this process.


There are deeply rooted issues and memories surrounding the Kurdish question. This applies to all sides. Those memories are still alive. Justice and the law are also the remedies for the experiences that have left such deep wounds.”


‘Mother tongues must be free’


Berkay also spoke about the importance of freedom to use one's mother tongue: “Freedom to use your mother tongue is extremely important. If you cannot freely use the language you learned from your mother and grandmother, something fundamental is missing. That language is part of who you are. You can express your spirit, identity and love most fully in your mother tongue. Whether it is Kurdish or Laz, it makes no difference.


What unites us all is our humanity. Your beliefs, language or religion do not matter. If we approach one another with love, we will have taken the biggest step. Any remaining obstacles will be easier to overcome. Love and justice are also the foundations of peace.


Çetin Altan had a wonderful saying: ‘Never miss out on love.’ In relation to the issue we are discussing, that …

title: Öcalan sends message to EUTCC conference: There is much that you, too, can do
content:
The following is the message sent by Abdullah Öcalan to the 20th Kurdish Conference, held this year at the European Parliament in Brussels, organized by the EUTCC:


“I extend my greetings to the participants and organizers of your 20th Conference, entitled ‘The European Union, Turkey, the Middle East and the Kurds.’


Undoubtedly, you have carried out—and continue to carry out—very valuable work, for which I offer my thanks and respect.


On 15 February 1999, I was brought to Imralı as a result of an international conspiracy. I am here today because of the influence of NATO’s Gladio network. I will not refrain from criticizing this at this point. They had said of me that ‘there is not a single patch of land in Europe where he could set foot.’ This conspiracy and these schemes were carried out in secrecy, hidden from the peoples of Europe. They were orchestrated according to the Gladio mentality. Undoubtedly, you are struggling against this situation. You are working to challenge it.


The European Union, which adopted this approach at the time, must today act in accordance with its own laws. It is of great importance that it take a constructive approach both to the democratization of Turkey and to the resolution of the Kurdish question. The fundamental way to resist the rising far right and the trend toward authoritarianism in Europe is to firmly uphold democratic values.


In particular, the support expressed through civil society and political initiatives such as your conference during the Peace and Democratic Society Process is support for peace and democracy. At the same time, your work and this conference need to become more enduring. New steps are needed. There is a need for internationalist cooperation. Such cooperation is important because it can bring together the democratic experiences and accumulated achievements of our regions and peoples, paving the way for a new paradigm of democracy and socialism.


The work we are carrying out in Turkey is valuable and important. We have launched a serious process aimed at finding political, fair and legal solutions to social problems in place of wars, massacres and the marginalization of others.


You can also discuss these issues at your conference. At present, there are many unanswered questions. Yet, despite these uncertainties, we are proposing a comprehensive model for a solution. This initiative represents a historic step for both Europe and the Middle East.


The success of our proposed Peace and Democratic Society project will make peace, stability and democratization in the Middle East possible. There is much that you, too, can do to help make this happen. I believe that valuable friends and comrades such as yourselves will help spread this initiative more widely.


Once again, I congratulate all those involved in the conference and send you my greetings and respects.


Abdullah Öcalan


Imralı


9 October"

title: PYD condemns the attack on party office in Hesekê
content:
The Democratic Union Party (PYD) condemned the vandalism of its office in the Xiwêran neighborhood of Hesekê and called for a comprehensive investigation into the attacks. In a statement issued on Wednesday, the party’s leadership described the attacks on Kurdish symbols and memorial portraits of fallen women as a threat to social peace, freedom of political activity, and coexistence among the different communities in northeastern Syria.


On Tuesday, unidentified individuals forcibly entered the PYD office, broke down doors, and vandalized the premises. Kurdish symbols, particularly memorial portraits of prominent women figures of the revolution, were targeted and stolen. Images of fallen women were subsequently desecrated in public, and footage of these acts was circulated on social media. According to the authorities, a suspect has since been arrested.


Connection with attack in Til Temir


The PYD recalled that the Center of the Council of Families of Martyrs in Til Temir had also been attacked just a few days earlier. The party views these incidents as part of a deliberate campaign targeting social coexistence. “The attacks in Til Temir and now in Hesekê, as well as the destruction of our office, indicate a systematic plan aimed at undermining coexistence,” the General Council stated.


PYD noted that the office in Xiwêran was not merely a party facility but also a center for community organizing and cooperation among different population groups. The attacks therefore threaten not only the PYD but also political organizing and coexistence in the region, it said. The party sees the attacks as reflecting a racist attitude reminiscent of the practices of the former Baath regime. “Its policies were based on the exclusion of other identities and the rejection of social diversity.”


Call for an investigation and protection of political institutions


The PYD called on the relevant authorities to ensure effective protection for party offices and civilian institutions, investigate the attacks, and hold those responsible accountable. It also demanded measures to prevent further attacks.


The party appealed to Syria’s political and social forces, as well as the wider population, to reject provocations and hatred and remain committed to dialogue.


“We call on everyone to uphold dialogue and coexistence and to protect social peace,” the statement concluded.

title: Kurdish Conference: No peace without democratization
content:
The 20th conference, organized by the European Union Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC) and patronized by Nobel Peace Prize laureate and Iranian human rights advocate Shirin Ebadi, human rights activist Bianca Jagger, and Kurdish politician Leyla Zana, recipient of the European Parliament’s Sakharov Prize for Freedom of Thought, began with a reception on October 14 at the European Parliament (EP) in Brussels.


The conference entered its second day with a packed program. The second and third sessions of the morning focused on geopolitical changes in the Middle East and women shaping the future.


Second session


The second session of the conference at the European Parliament was held under the title “The Middle East at a crossroads: Geopolitical shifts, democratic transformation, and the pursuit of peace.”


Moderated by journalist Dilek Odabaşı, the session featured Doğu Ergil from Ankara University, journalist Amed Dicle, and Colin Starger from the University of Baltimore in the United States as speakers.


Doğu Ergil: The conditions for lasting peace cannot be established without democratization


Academic Doğu Ergil questioned why so much investment in security had produced so little peace, drawing attention to the deep crises facing policies built around security.


Assessing global military, geopolitical, and political changes, Ergil argued that the emerging situation was not one of multipolarity but rather of overlapping security spheres.


Referring to the ongoing process in Turkey, Doğu Ergil said: “Democracy is the capacity to manage social differences and existential conflicts through political means. It does not eliminate political disagreements entirely. It enables parties that cannot reach agreement to coexist peacefully despite their differences. Leaving political issues unresolved eventually becomes a persistent source of insecurity.”


Emphasizing that democratic reforms should not be regarded as a luxury to be considered only after stability has been achieved, Doğu Ergil added: “Democracy is not merely a consequence of sustainable stability but also one of its prerequisites. Why do I say this? Because we frequently hear the following argument: First, let the most important agreement be reached, and then democratic reforms can follow. However, the conditions for lasting peace cannot be established without democratization.”


Proposing three transformations, Doğu Ergil said: “The first is a transition from regime-centered security to human-centered security. The second is a transition from an exclusionary understanding of national sovereignty to a cooperative security framework.”


As a third transformation, he emphasized the importance of resolutions accepted and sustained by societies themselves rather than imposed from outside.


Amed Dicle: Europe should encourage a resolution


Drawing attention to the Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey, journalist Amed Dicle said: “Negotiating with a government to reach a resolution does not mean endorsing its approach to governance. To secure their rights and their future, the Kurds are engaging in talks with those who currently hold decision-making power. The opposition’s responsibility should be to build on this opportunity to advance the democratization of the country.”


Highlighting the responsibilities of the European Union and European countries, Amed Dicle stated: “If the European Union wants a political resolution, it must go beyond welcoming the decisions of the Kurdish movement and also raise the steps that the state needs to take. Maintaining trade, investment, and security relations with Turkey does not prevent the recognition of Kurdish rights. These relations can continue with a Turkey that has made peace with the Kurds, while direct and long-term relations can also be developed with the Kurds, who play a significant role in the region’s future.


What the Kurds expect from Europe is for the diplomatic influence gained through its relations with Ankara to be used to advance peace. The close relations that once made it possible to support policies of war can now also be used to encourage a resolution.


Because the outcome of this process will not be confined to Turkey’s borders. The Middle East is being reshaped, and the Kurds are at the center of this transformation. It is impossible to establish a new political order in the region without the Kurds. Both Ankara and European capitals must take this reality into account in their …

cpi inflation calculator

FUN FACT: it’s now been so long since the dems were able to raise the minimum wage that today’s minimum wage is now functionally lower than than at any point since

1949

1968

58 years

title: Karneya tenduristî û avhewayê ya welatan: Tirkiye di rêza 47em de ye
content:
Hevpeymaniya Avhewa û Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanî (

Global Climate and Health Alliance

 ,GCHA), karneya tenduristiyê ya 132 welatan parve kiriye ku wan welatan peyman û sozên neteweyî yên avhewayê di çarçoveya Peymana Parîsê de weşandine.


Di “Karneya Beyana Tevkariya Neteweyî ya Tendurist” (The Healthy NDC Scorecard) de karneya tenduristî û hewaya paqij a beyanên tevkariya neteweyî di heşt kategoriyan de hat nirxandin. Di analîzê de bandorên li ser tenduristiyê, qirêjiya hewayê, çalakiyên di sektora tenduristiyê de, fêdeyên din ên di qada tenduristiyê de, veguhestinên edîl, birêvebirina entegreyê, aborî û fînans, şopandin û pêkanîn hatin lêkolînkirin.


Tirkiye di rêza 47em de ye


Encam bi wê yekê re hatin berhevkirin ku bê ka armancên avhewayê heta çi astê bi îdia ne û li wî welatî rêjeya mirinên ji ber qirêjiya hewayê çiqas e. Di encama analîzê de Tirkiye bi 14 pûanan di nav 132 welatan de di rêza 47em de cih girt:


Li Tirkiyeyê rêjeya mirinên ji ber qirêjiya hewayê di her sed hezar kesî de weke 83,6 hat tomarkirin. Armanca giştî ya avhewayê ya wî welatî ji bo senaryoyeke ku di bin 4°C’yî de ye wekî gelekî kêm hat nirxandin.


Di raporê de ev xal derketin pêş:


19 welatên ku karîn di nav 20 welatên destpêkê de cih bigirin, welatên xwedî dahata kêm û navîn in.


Pûana Tirkiyeyê (14) nêzî pûana Kanada (16), Efrîqaya Başûr (13) û Yekîtiya Ewropayê (12) ye. 


Kolombiya bi wê yekê derdikeve pêş ku mijara tenduristiyê di plansaziyên xwe yên neteweyî yên avhewayê de bi awayekî herî berfireh entegre kiriye(pûana wê di ser 32an de 29 e). Nijerya (25 pûan) û Kamboçya (24 pûan).


Japonya û Hindistan ku tenê karîn 2 pûanan bistînin, di nav welatên ku pûana herî kêm stendine de cih digirin.


Welatên din ên ku emîsyona wan bilind e jî, ji ber ku erka dikeve ser milê wan bi awayekî adil bi cih neanîn, li paş armancan man. Di nav van welatan de Brezîlya (7), Awistralya, Çîn û Brîtanya (bi giştî 9 pûan) cih digirin.


Tê destnîşankirin ku tenê di pênc welatan de (Kamboçya, Şîlî, Kolombiya, Kosta Rîka û Paraguay) armancên kêmkirina karbona reş hene ku yek ji sedemên sereke yên guherîna avhewayê û qirêjiya hewayê ye û dibe sedema pirsgirêkên tenduristiyê yên giran.


Bandorên krîza avhewayê yên li ser tenduristiyê


Bandorên krîza avhewayê yên li ser tenduristiyê gav bi gav diyar dibin. Îsal tenê li Nepalê ji ber hilweşîna berfa qeşagirtî zêdetirî hezar û 400 kes mirin û zêdetirî 6 hezar û 600 kes hîn jî winda ne.


Ji ber bûyerên ku peywendiya wan bi guherîna avhewayê re hene li Afrîkaya Rojhilat û Başûr heşt mîlyon zarok bi xetereya birçîbûnê re rûbirû ne.


Her wiha tê zanîn ku li Ewropayê pêlên germê yên di havînê de bûn sedema mirina zêdetirî 35 hezar kesan.


Li gorî Rêxistina Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanê (DSO), krîza avhewayê dikare di nava salên 2030-2050an de her sal bibe sedema zêdeyî 250 hezar mirinên din.


HEYAMA KU ÎKLÎM Û DINYA DIGUHERE... - 4


Bandora krîza îklîmê û sotemenîyên fosîlî li ser tendûristîya zarokan


10 Hezîran 2021


Ji sedî 92ê Tirkiyeyê hewaya qirêj dikişînin sîngê xwe


Li gorî Rapora Reş 2025an a Platforma Mafê Hewaya Paqij, ji sedî 92yê serjimêriya Tirkiyeyê li gorî pîvanên Rêxistina Tenduristiyê ya Cîhanê (DSO) hewaya qirêj dikişînin sîngê xwe.


Ew bajarê ku qirêjiya hewayê û rêjeya mirina ji ber qirêjiyê lê herî bilind e jî Colemêrg e.


Di raporê de tê diyar kirin ku heke qirêjiya hewayê dakeve asta ku DSO pêşniyar dike, li Tirkiyeyê di salê de dikare jiyana herî kêm 60 hezar kesî bifilite.


Ev nûçe bi hevkariya bianet û İklim Masasiyê(Maseya Avhewayê) hatiye weşandin. İklim Masasi servîseke nûçeyan e ku armanc dike agahiyên bawerpêkirî yên li ser krîza avhewayê di nav raya giştî de belav bike. Nivîskarên wê ji wan zanyaran pêk tên ku di mijarên dikin nûçe de xwedî pisporiyê ne.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Hyperscale": Paris Marx on Excess of Big Tech Data Empires & His Critique of Bernie Sanders' AI Bill
content:
We speak with tech journalist Paris Marx about his new book,

Hyperscale: The Ambition and Excess of Big Tech’s Data Empires

. In the book, Marx exposes the deceptive ways tech companies are taking resources from vulnerable communities in order to build massive AI data centers. “We have seen the tech companies that, back in 2019, 2020, wanted us to see them as climate leaders … completely throw their targets out the window in order to pursue generative AI and this data center buildout,” says Marx. He notes that after failing to connect to electrical grids in the locations where they were building data centers, some AI companies have pivoted to building “on-site gas plants,” further increasing dependency on fossil fuels.


Tech companies “want us to believe” that AI models are “starting to become so powerful that within 10 years they could decide that they want to wipe out humanity or a significant chunk of humanity,” says Marx. “That is a mix of science fiction and delusion … and it is also a very effective way to distract from the real harms that we’re seeing from these generative AI products.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: The Midterm Battle over Data Centers: Memphis House Candidate Justin Pearson Fights Elon Musk's xAI
content:
The energy needs of the AI boom and the construction of massive data centers in states across the country have created a backlash from both Democratic and Republican voters. The battle against data centers is at the heart of a campaign in Tennessee: Democratic state Representative Justin J. Pearson is opposed to the Colossus data centers built by Elon Musk’s xAI in the Memphis area. Pearson is running against Republican state Senator Brent Taylor in Tennessee’s 9th Congressional District, which, after recent redistricting, includes parts of Memphis, as well as rural and suburban counties.


“Across the 15 counties that I’ve traveled, I’ve yet to meet anyone, including folks who are Republicans who are voting for us, who want data centers,” says Pearson. “Gas is high; groceries are high; healthcare costs are high; wages are low. Yet the billionaire class continues to profit off of our pain and pillage our communities and our pocketbooks.”

author: Daron Letts
title: Carpentry to return to Victor Sammurtok School
content:
Woodworking will soon be back on the curriculum at Chesterfield Inlet’s Victor Sammurtok School following a three-year absence.


“There is so much value in a woodshop,” said principal Jacques Theriault during an interview earlier this semester. “With woodworking, we’re introducing a trade and there’s a lifetime career right there.”


The new woodshop is expected to be in operation in time to offer the program to students by mid-January, he added.


The school had a functioning woodshop in the past, but former staff converted the space into a weight room following the COVID-19 pandemic.


The room is still equipped with industrial ventilation and wiring to accommodate the electrical demands of a fully functioning shop.


When

Theriault became principal in January 2025, he immediately began searching for funders to reinstate the woodshop, though he admired the quality of the weight room, he said.


It boasts a state-of-the-art rowing machine that connects to other rowers online and other high-end exercise equipment. The exercise space will move into a smaller room across the hall, Theriault said.


Under the federal government’s Smart Cities Challenge, the Nunavut-based non-profit Katinnganiq Makerspace Network provided the approximately $100,000 needed to reinstate the woodshop.


The newly purchased equipment is currently in a sea can near the community dock.


The machines, all of which feature instant-stop safety functions and kill switches, include a table saw, drill press, router, bandsaw, table grinder, belt and disc sander, scroll saw, miter saw, jointer, plainer, and a wood lathe.


The school also purchased goggles and “every safety thing that you can buy for a woodshop,” he added.


The school even has a freshly trained instructor in longtime math and science teacher Glen Brocklebank.


Last year, Brocklebank, who previously taught woodworking at the school,

 completed eight months of professional development training in construction and renovation techniques at Georgian College in Owen Sound, Ont.


“I learned some new skills,” Brocklebank said in an interview. “It was a new course to me.”


Work on the woodshop is expected to begin by December,

Theriault said.

author: D.W.
title: What Psychiatry Missed: My Ferritin Level Was 6
content:
D

uring my late 40s, I began to experience bouts of utter exhaustion and brain fog, often around the time of my menstrual periods which were irregular. I would wake up feeling like I had not really slept and my memory was sluggish. There were times when even lifting a frying pan took a great deal of effort.


I spent much time on the couch during this time of the month, and did my motherly duties in spurts and with verbal instructions rather than being able to fully participate in the activities. I had experienced this at various times in the past, especially postpartum. Driving was a challenge, and familiar routes would no longer feel automatic as they had before. I would go to bed early thinking I just needed more rest, but at times I would not be able to sleep. My severe iron deficiency had not yet been identified.


I was already seeing a psychiatric provider, and I was waiting to see an endocrinologist because I had an autoimmune thyroid disease which had been diagnosed 16 years prior. I had moved and needed to wait for insurance to go through and get the referral. My mental health provider was a nurse practitioner and she thought I needed to take something for the insomnia and difficulty staying asleep.


Ambien was prescribed. I was told that it would help me fall asleep and possibly prevent waking up in the night. I started on 5 mg; the first month I took it on and off and thought it helped me fall asleep. I did notice that in the morning I felt like I was still not fully awake upon rising. I called my mom and told her and she said I should try coffee. I chose tea, and it provided some relief but I started having the jitters from the caffeine. This was a stressful period of time in my life and I trusted my provider. Unfortunately, a 20-minute appointment was not sufficient to make an informed prescribing decision. Then a couple months later she gave me another script and I started taking the Ambien more frequently.


I had nights when I actually got out of bed and was performing household duties like it was the day and I was awake but I did not realize it. I would wake up and not remember cleaning the bathroom partway or leaving food out on the counter. My awareness of my surroundings decreased, and daytime driving was extremely difficult. I would not remember my schedule for the day and had to keep checking what day it was. I was still exhausted and felt like my legs were heavy and I just needed to take breaks. I also felt on edge, and got triggered by some people questioning my health, as well as the upstairs neighbors who had left a candle burning and the fire trucks had to come. I shared this added anxiety with my provider, who then added a benzodiazepine and I began taking this at night also.


To the best of my recollection, that is when I started getting up more frequently at night and feeling like we were not safe. I found myself at a neighbor’s place, calling for help. I was able to carry on some conversation but it was not all logical and I knew my memory was not reliable enough to care for my children without assistance.


After being hospitalized, several months passed before I was seen by a neurologist. Blood tests revealed anemia and a ferritin level of 6 (optimum levels for women are said to fall between 50 and 100, with levels below 30 being considered clinically deficient). I was told that my insurance would not cover iron infusions or the special type of iron that was quickly absorbed, and so I was put on ferrous sulfate. That caused nausea and constipation no matter how much water I drank. My ferritin level did not go up much, and during this time I still had great fatigue and I was told I was depressed. Another symptom of a “mental illness.” No one told me that anemia could be contributing to the mental health issues that would not resolve. It is my belief that sleep deprivation led to the psychotic features I experienced. The providers put me on antipsychotics; meanwhile, my underlying iron stores remained depleted.


For years, I battled low iron stores and mental health symptoms. There were periods of clarity, but each time I had my menses I still had insomnia no matter what medications I took. I was also diagnosed with restless periodic limb movements, which the neurologist stated was a side effect of the antipsychotics. I was prescribed medication (gabapentin) to combat that.


There were stressors in my life at this time: I was separated from my youngest child completely and this …

content:

After being welcomed at the PYD headquarters, the delegation proceeded to the city municipality. This morning, the delegation first visited the Kongra Star headquarters, followed by visits to the university in Kobanê, the Kobanê Museum, the families of martyrs, the Martyrs’ Cemetery, and Miştenûr Hill.


The delegation consists of Devrim Demir, co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality and co-spokesperson of the Diplomacy Committee for Local Administrations; Safiye Aladağ, co-mayor of Amed’s Yenişehir Municipality; Sevim Bîçîçî, co-mayor of Silvan (Farqîn) Municipality; Belkize Beştaş Epözdemir, co-mayor of Tatvan Municipality; and Ruken Demir, a member of the Diplomacy Committee.


Rojava needs support


Devrim Demir, co-mayor of Mardin Metropolitan Municipality and co-spokesperson of the Diplomacy Committee for Local Administrations, stated that they would further develop their relations with Rojava in the coming period.


Explaining that, as a delegation of women working in local government, they had visited Qamishlo, Amûdê, Kobanê, and Dêrik, as well as many other cities, Demir said: “Our aim is to further strengthen relations between North Kurdistan and Rojava and, through these relations, develop joint initiatives. The issue of integration is currently on the agenda in Rojava, and institutions are being integrated. The situation is the same in Bakûr. As a result of this visit, it became clear that strong support is needed, particularly in the field of local government. Everything in this city, from infrastructure to construction and urban development, needs to be reorganized.”


Emphasizing that they would turn the notes taken during the visit into a report, Demir continued: “Everything was noted down: what is needed and which areas are experiencing difficulties. In the plans we have prepared for the coming period, we intend to maintain our relations and continue mutual visits. This was our first visit, and it was very meaningful, but it will not be our last. So far, we have held meetings with approximately 30 institutions. We hope to help establish a support network, and we will make every effort to provide this support. In addition to relations between Bakûr and Rojava, we can also bring Rojava to the attention of the international community through our international connections.”


Concluding her remarks, Devrim Demir stressed that Rojava needs support in every possible form and that this support must also be provided at the international level. She stated that they would work to fulfill this responsibility.

title: Provocations in Hesekê and the importance of self-defence
content:
Hesekê (al-Hasakah) is one of Syria's most diverse cities, home to Kurds, Arabs, Syriacs/Assyrians, Armenians and other communities living side by side. Kurds are concentrated mainly in the Mufti and Salihiyê neighbourhoods, while Arabs predominantly live in Xiwêran, Neşva and Tel Hacer. Different communities live together in Aziziyê and parts of the city centre.


The question of how the city is governed is directly linked to how this multi-ethnic population is represented. The Autonomous Administration model, established in Rojava and regarded as an example for the world, is based on shared governance in which different sections of society have a say. The current Syrian Interim Government in Damascus, however, advocates a return to the mentality of the Ba'ath regime. Although the 29 January Agreement initiated an integration process between Damascus and the Autonomous Administration, the current government continues to refuse to recognise the political will, identity and cultural rights of the Kurds. The murders, attacks on symbols, attempts to occupy Kurdish neighbourhoods and armed incidents witnessed in Hesekê recently have reflected this mentality in the city.


Attacks have continued


One of the first concrete steps in the integration process was the appointment of Nureddin Isa Ahmed as Governor of Hesekê. The Damascus administration appointed Brigadier General Ziyad al-Ayesh as Special Presidential Representative to oversee the implementation of the agreement.


It was agreed that three brigades formed from fighters of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) would be incorporated into the Syrian army's 60th Division. In May, integrated brigade structures were established under the 60th and 72nd Divisions, with new arrangements introduced in Hesekê, Qamishlo, Dêrik and Kobanê. Procedures were also initiated to bring the Internal Security Forces (Asayish) under the Syrian Ministry of Interior.


However, these military and administrative arrangements did not eliminate political tensions in the city. Anti-Kurdish rhetoric and attacks on Kurdish symbols continued, while Damascus's direct involvement in managing developments provoked criticism.


Murders and armed attacks


One of the most serious attacks against Kurds took place on 10 September, when Sîpan Hiznî, a fighter with the Hesekê Brigade, was abducted and murdered. His killing heightened concerns about the safety of fighters integrated into the army and Kurds living in the city.


On 20 September, an Asayish patrol escorting oil tankers near Qurtuba University on the Qamishlo–Hesekê road came under armed attack. Two people on a motorcycle opened fire, killing Abdulaziz Faysal Hasan and injuring two employees of an oil company. Developments during the first two weeks of October provided the clearest example of Damascus directly organising provocations.


Provocation involving flags


Calls were made through television channels and social media for all Arabs in Hesekê to join a march against Kurds after Friday prayers on 2 October.


A march subsequently took place in the Xiwêran and Neşva neighbourhoods after prayers. A Kurdish flag was burned in the city centre, while Kurdish symbols, signs and security cameras were targeted. The attacks thus escalated into a direct assault on Kurdish identity and the presence of Kurds in public spaces. In the following days, marches were organised in Raqqa (Reqa) and Serêkaniyê, calling on Damascus to take "full control" of Hesekê.


Provocations involving flags had also been planned in Kobanê and Afrin (Efrîn) before the incidents in Hesekê. Footage circulated showing the Syrian flag being taken down during Newroz celebrations in Kobanê. Asayish announced that one person involved in the incident had been detained and referred to the judicial authorities. It was pointed out that the footage was being used to heighten tensions in other areas. Around the same time, Kurds returning from Newroz celebrations in Afrin were also attacked.


ISIS's secret haven: Xiwêran


Over the past 15 years, Xiwêran has emerged as a neighbourhood that actively supported ISIS. It is predominantly inhabited by Arabs. The neighbourhood also occupies a significant place in Hesekê's security concerns because of the presence of ISIS cells, the arrest of numerous ISIS members and the fact that nearly 3,000 ISIS members were previously held in prisons in the area. The fact that the provocations were planned in this neighbourhood is therefore …

title: Kurdish Conference at the European Parliament: The current opening creates an opportunity
content:
The second day of the Kurdish Conference held at the European Parliament began with opening speeches. Kariane Westrheim of the University of Bergen in Norway, Chair of the EU Turkey Civic Commission (EUTCC), which organized the 20th conference, delivered the first speech.


EUTCC 20 years: A voice for Kurdish rights, peace and democracy


Speaking via live video link during the first session, moderated by EUTCC Board Member Dersim Dağdeviren, Kariane Westrheim thanked everyone who had contributed to the conference, saying: “When EUTCC was founded in 2004, Turkey was at an important crossroads. Discussions regarding Turkey's European Union membership had begun, yet the resolution of the Kurdish issue—a central matter of democracy—had not been addressed. We acted with the awareness that this political initiative, detached from reality, would neither democratize Turkey nor resolve the Kurdish issue.”


After outlining the political changes and forms of participation since the conference’s inception, Kariane Westrheim also addressed the ongoing Peace and Democratic Society Process in Turkey.


Drawing attention to the progress made, the EUTCC Chair said, “Mr. Öcalan's name is openly discussed in European institutions today in connection with peace and a political settlement. His 2025 call for peace and a democratic society has been discussed by the European Parliament, which described the developments that followed as a historic opportunity.”


Westrheim further stated the following:


“We should not claim that EUTCC caused this transformation. The history is much larger than any one organisation. Kurdish political movements, Turkish political actors, human-rights organisations, European institutions and, above all, those directly involved in the conflict and peace initiatives have shaped it.


But EUTCC has been part of that history, and its contribution deserves recognition. EUTCC was founded around a simple but far-reaching idea: Turkey's relationship with Europe could not be separated from the Kurdish question. If Turkey was seeking membership of the European Union, then democracy, human rights, the rule of law and political freedoms could not stop at the Kurdish question.


From the beginning, EUTCC brought together European parliamentarians, lawyers, academics, human-rights defenders, journalists and representatives of civil society. Its annual conferences in Brussels created a European meeting place where people could exchange views, challenge each other and, importantly, continue the discussion when the political climate was difficult.


Over twenty years, governments changed. EU-Turkey relations changed. The conflict went through escalation and ceasefire. A peace process began and collapsed.


But EUTCC remained a constant European forum for discussing the Kurdish question. In the early years, much of the work focused on human rights and European standards.


The message was that Kurdish cultural and political rights were not simply an internal Turkish matter. They were connected to the democratic values and obligations Turkey had accepted through its relationship with Europe. But the question inevitably became larger: How can the conflict itself be ended?


That meant political dialogue. And it meant addressing the role of Mr. Öcalan. For many years, the idea that Mr. Öcalan could participate in a political solution was highly controversial. EUTCC increasingly argued that a sustainable settlement required dialogue with the relevant political actors.


This became particularly significant during the Oslo process 2009-2011 and later during the Imrali process 2013–2015 peace process. That process collapsed, and conflict returned. But the experience demonstrated something important: a conflict of this depth cannot be resolved through security measures alone. It requires a political dimension. That principle remains central today.


There is another aspect of EUTCC's history that deserves emphasis. EUTCC has never viewed the Kurdish question only through the borders of Turkey. Its conferences and networks have brought together voices and perspectives from all four parts of Kurdistan -Turkey, Syria, Iraq and Iran. This has given European audiences a broader understanding of the Kurdish experience, while recognising that each part of Kurdistan has its own political circumstances, history and challenges.


It has also helped strengthen a sense of Kurdish solidarity across borders. That is particularly important today …

title: KJAR calls for freedom for Varisheh Moradi and international action against executions in Iran
content:
The Community of Free Women of East Kurdistan (KJAR) condemned the renewed death sentence against Kurdish political prisoner Varisheh Moradi as a deliberate act of revenge by the Iranian regime against the women’s movement. In a statement on Thursday, the organization described the decision as a continuation of state repression against women fighting for freedom and self-determination. It also demanded the immediate annulment of all death sentences and the release of political prisoners sentenced to death.


“The renewed death sentence against Varisheh Moradi reflects the regime’s fear of women’s political will and the ‘Jin, Jiyan, Azadî’ [Woman, Life, Freedom] movement,” KJAR stated, stressing that this determination would not bow to oppression, repression, or inhumane sentences such as the death penalty.


Resistance against the Iranian judiciary


Moradi, herself a member of KJAR, appeared again on Wednesday before Branch 15 of the Revolutionary Court in Tehran, presided over by the notorious judge Abolqasem Salavati, and was sentenced to death for alleged membership in an “insurgent group.” The women’s movement of Rojhilat views this as an attempt to suppress the political struggles of women resisting oppression through repeated court proceedings and death sentences.


Moradi has been imprisoned in Iran for more than three years. During this time, she has been subjected to severe physical and psychological torture. She has also been denied access to medical treatment and contact with her family. Despite the conditions of her imprisonment and the threat of execution, Moradi has remained steadfast in her convictions. She does not recognize Iran’s Revolutionary Courts as legitimate institutions, thereby also challenging the legality of the proceedings against her. KJAR praised her stance as an expression of revolutionary resistance that cannot be broken even by death sentences.


Call for international action


KJAR holds the Iranian judiciary and the regime’s security forces directly responsible for Moradi’s life and her physical and psychological well-being. It remarked that the repeated summonses and renewed imposition of the death penalty are part of a systematic policy of intimidation and retaliation against politically active women.


KJAR also issued an urgent appeal to international human rights organizations, women’s movements, and the democratic public: “We call on all international human rights organizations, women’s organizations, freedom-oriented forces, and the public not to remain silent in the face of the machinery of repression and executions, but to raise their voices to demand the immediate annulment of all death sentences and the unconditional release of Varisheh Moradi and all political prisoners sentenced to death.”


Background


Varisheh (also Warisha) Moradi, also known as Ciwana Sine, a member of the East Kurdistan Free Women’s Society (KJAR) from Sanandaj, Kurdistan Province, was arrested by the Ministry of Intelligence on 1 August 2023 at the entrance to Sanandaj upon her return from Kermanshah, Kermanshah Province, where she had been involved in political and organisational activities.


She spent the first 13 days of her detention in the detention centre of this security institution in Sanandaj, and was then transferred to Ward 209 of Evin Prison in Tehran.


During this period, she was subjected to pressure and threats to make forced confessions, and on 26 December 2023, after five months of solitary confinement, she was transferred to the women’s ward of Evin Prison.


On 10 October 2024, coinciding with the World Day Against the Death Penalty, Moradi went on a 20-day hunger strike in Tehran’s Evin Prison to protest the issuing and execution of death sentences by the Islamic Republic of Iran.


Due to digestive complications following the hunger strike, she was transferred to a medical facility outside the prison, and returned after spending one night under care.


The death penalty, handed down by Judge Abolghassem Salavati, followed two court hearings on 16 June and 5 October 2024, and the death sentence was formally notified to Moradi’s lawyers on 10 November 2024.


During the court hearings, Moradi was denied the right to defend herself, and the judge barred her lawyers from presenting a defence.


Additionally, the lawyers, who had previously been prevented from reviewing the case file, were only allowed a few hours to review the case after the second hearing.

title: U.S. Sanctions ICC in a Bid to Avoid "Criminal Liability": War Crimes Prosecutor Reed Brody
content:
The Trump administration on Friday placed sweeping sanctions on the International Criminal Court that target the institution as a whole. This comes on top of earlier sanctions against individual

ICC

 judges and personnel. The administration has been escalating attacks on the

ICC

 since the court issued arrest warrants in 2024 for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant. It announced the sanctions just hours after former

ICC

 Judge Navi Pillay — the South African jurist who led the United Nations commission of inquiry that concluded that Israel had committed genocide in Gaza — was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.


“This is really an insurance policy against accountability for crimes that the United States and its ally Israel are committing in plain sight,” says war crimes prosecutor Reed Brody, a member of the International Commission of Jurists. The sanctions, which prevent U.S.-based banks and companies from transacting with the

ICC

, constitute an “existential attack” on the court, he says.

title: A Massa Carrara maxi-corteo: 15mila in piazza contro l’ondata di denunce, “si cerca di limitare il dissenso impedendo le manifestazioni”
content:
Almeno 15mila persone

 hanno sfilato per le strade di Massa Carrara nella giornata di mercoledì 15 ottobre, giorno in cui si sarebbe dovuta tenere la

prima udienza

 a carico dei manifestanti colpiti dall’andata repressiva contro il movimento per la Palestina.


Da Radio Onda d’Urto


Il governo Meloni, a botte di

decreti sicurezza

, ha cercato di mettere un freno alla straordinaria partecipazione alle proteste che hanno attraversato in particolare l’autunno 2025 in Italia. A Massa uno

spropositato numero di denunce

 – almeno 37 – sono state comminate contro altrettanti attivisti e attiviste massesi. La prima udienza a carico dei manifestanti, che si sarebbe dovuta tenere ieri, è slittata a marzo 2027:


Quella di ieri, afferma il segretario generale della Cgil di Massa Carrara

Nicola Del Vecchio ai microfoni di Radio Onda d’Urto

, “è stata una manifestazione non solo per esprimere solidarietà agli indagati, ma anche per denunciare quello che sta accadendo nel paese.

Si cerca di limitare il dissenso impedendo le manifestazioni

. Dobbiamo continuare ad indignarci di fronte alle ingiustizie esattamente come facemmo lo scorso ottobre”. Di fronte a un genocidio, dice dalla piazza, “non possiamo voltarci dall’altra parte”.


“Viviamo in un contesto gravissimo,

un contesto segnato dalle disuguaglianze che stanno sempre più aumentando

”, e “c’è una deriva bellicista che toglie risorse alla sanità, ai trasporti, alla scuola per buttarle via nelle armi. Se di fronte a tutto questo le persone vogliono dissentire, vogliono manifestare pacificamente come previsto dalla Costituzione, ecco i Decreti Sicurezza: questo è inaccettabile”, ha detto Rossano Rossi, segretario generale della Cgil Toscana, alla partenza del corteo nell’ambito della giornata di sciopero generale regionale indetta dal sindacato.


Ai sindacati, si sono uniti migliaia di giovani, studenti e studentesse, organizzazioni e singoli cittadini.

title: Mobilitazioni studentesche in Albania
content:
Raccogliamo alcune testimonianze inviateci dall’Albania riguardo alle recenti mobilitazioni studentesche.


Ieri, a Tirana, il conflitto è proseguito non solo come il martedì, ma con un’intensità ancora maggiore. Fiamme e barricate. La giornata è iniziata con il boicottaggio delle lezioni da parte di studenti delle scuole superiori e universitari per scendere in strada. L’appuntamento studentesco per la manifestazione era fissato alle 14, ma spontaneamente la giornata è cominciata molto prima. Barricate, tentativi di sabotare i mezzi della repressione, ruote degli idranti lacerate. Prima tappa al Ministero dell’Istruzione, con un tentativo di incendiarlo. Scontri. L’atmosfera è elettrizzante, piena di entusiasmo, travolgente. Ragazze e ragazzi travisati salutano, in segno di rispetto, donne anziane che li sostengono.


Arrivano le 14. Vengono incendiate le sedi di istituti di credito privati che hanno rovinato famiglie intere, portando a suicidi. Si fa irruzione, a spinta, nei palazzi governativi, usando pali sradicati e improvvisati come arieti. Divampano incendi nel Ministero dell’Economia, nel palazzo del Primo ministro e in Parlamento: principi d’incendio, poi spenti. Fa eccezione il palazzo del Ministero della Giustizia, incendiato, tra video virali e una folla che esulta.


La protesta continua anche al calar del sole. Telecamere divelte. Nei quartieri popolari viene devastata la sede di Intesa Sanpaolo, che opera, né più né meno, come un istituto di credito oppressivo e neocoloniale. Distrutta la sede centrale della Banca di Tirana. Gli arresti vengono impediti. Ragazze con passamontagna che ballano con anziani in abito tradizionale. Scontri con le guardie: chi le dà, chi le prende. Scudi rubati, auto della polizia incendiate. Distrutto un commissariato, uno dei tanti in cui, in questi mesi, i manifestanti venivano portati senza alcun motivo né spiegazione. Trattenuti per ore, malmenati, mentre fuori li aspettavano amiche, solidali, compagni, gruppi di riferimento, familiari.


Gli studenti, che l’altro ieri hanno deciso di irrompere in questo modo sulla scena, hanno continuato a ripeterlo: hanno costretto il nostro popolo a fare così. E il popolo, anziché dissociarsi, sostiene la protesta e si unisce al livello di scontro o, quantomeno, lo sostiene. «Abbiamo manifestato pacificamente per oltre 130 giorni. Siamo stati sbeffeggiati dai poteri, mentre continuavano a emergere scandali di corruzione durante le proteste. Siamo stati totalmente silenziati dai media internazionali. Umiliati per anni. Il ricatto tra l’emigrazione all’estero, da stranieri, e gli abusi e le angherie nella propria terra. Il ricatto si spezza. Anche con il fuoco.» Ci tengono a dirlo: non siamo stati noi a volerlo. È conflitto, non violenza fine a sé stessa. Gente buttata in strada senza più una casa, morta nelle corsie degli ospedali, rimasta senza paga dopo mesi di lavoro per padroncini stranieri, costretta a emigrare. I palazzi istituzionali sono assediati. Un amico e compagno, oggi, mi ha detto: «Per forza, poi, fate i ministri AI!» Tirana, da ieri, è ingovernabile. Letteralmente.


Da Roberto Hajadari


136esimo giorno di protesta consecutiva oggi a Tirana. Oggi, però, con un’enorme novità: gli studenti avevano chiamato un grande sciopero con lo slogan “Istruzione, non emigrazione”. Sin dalla mattina, folle si sono riversate nelle strade. Ben presto il conflitto si è alzato a livelli altissimi: scontri, barricate, cassonetti incendiati. E’ andato virale un giovane che, da solo, ha affrontato sei guardie come un pugile, finchè non è stato fermato e massacrato. Idranti della polizia e cariche violentissime, ma i giovani, a ogni attacco, controattaccavano e controcaricavano. Così fino alle 18, quando la canonica protesta pomeridiana e serale, è scesa in strada convergendo con gli studenti. Il livello del conflitto, già altissimo nel corso della giornata, è rimasto tale, anzi, si è ulteriormente alzato.


Fin’ora la protesta, questi 100 e passa giorni, è stata pacifica e determinata, conflittuale ma entro i perimetri della resistenza agli abusi e alle angherie di guardie private e statali. Oggi Tirana è un’enorme barricata illuminata dalle fiamme da stamattina, e la notte è lunga, e la situazione è ingovernabile. Egli studenti hanno chiamato, per domani, un enorme boicottaggio delle lezioni.


Come detto, sin dall’inizio è una protesta ambientalista e di classe, decoloniale e per l’autonomia. Auto organizzata e senza partiti. E oggi, in …

title: Mahir Çayan’ı anlatan kitap hakkında toplatılma kararı
content:
Türkiye Halk Kurtuluş Partisi-Cephesi (THKP-C) kurucusu Mahir Çayan’ın fikir ve görüşlerinin yanı sıra Abdullah Öcalan başta olmak üzere pek çok ismin Çayan ile ilgili anı ve duruşuna dair yaptığı değerlendirmelerden oluşan kitap hakkında toplatılma kararı alındı. 


Dipnot Yayınları’nın Haziran’da yayımladığı “Mahir Çayan Kitabı: Toplu yazılar ve üzerine yazılar” isimli kitap hakkında Ankara 8’inci Sulh Ceza Hâkimliği toplatma kararı aldı. Kararda, “örgüt propagandası” yapıldığı ileri sürüldü. 


Dipnot Yayınları Genel Yayın Yönetmeni Emirali Türkmen hakkında da “örgüt propagandası” gerekçesiyle dava açıldı. Duruşma 23 Şubat 2027'de. 


"Kitaplar suç aleti, düşünceler suç delili değildir"


Dipnot Yayınları da konuya dair açıklama yaptı. Şöyle dedi:


“Bir kitabın toplatılması, yalnızca basılı bir eserin okurla buluşmasının engellenmesi değil, aynı zamanda düşüncenin dolaşımına, tarihte olan bitenlerin tartışılmasına ve toplumun kendi geçmişiyle yüzleşme hakkına yönelik bir müdahaledir. Oysa kitaplar suç aleti, düşünceler suç delili değildir.”


  “Ülkemiz tarihinin belli bir dönemine damgasını vuran toplumsal ve siyasal hareketleri yasaklarla unutturmaya çalışmak, bu hareketlerin bugüne uzanan tarihsel sonuçlarını toplatma kararlarıyla ortadan kaldırmak mümkün değildir. Hiçbir yasak, fikirlerin toplum içinde dolaşımını ve tartışılmasını bütünüyle engelleyemez; hiçbir baskı, hakikat arayışını durduramaz. Halkın eleştirel ve muhalif fikirlere erişiminin engellenmesine, kitapların suç unsuru gibi gösterilmesine ve yayıncılığın baskı altına alınmasına sessiz kalmayacağız. Biz, kitapların ve fikirlerin yasaklanmadığı, özgürce tartışıldığı bir toplumdan yanayız. Geçmişi sorgulayan, bugünü anlamaya çalışan ve özgürlükçü/eşitlikçi/ barışçıl bir toplumun ancak fikirlerin özgürce tartışılması temelinde kurulabileceğine inanıyoruz.”

title: Анархиста Алексея Григорьева избили во время этапа в Верхнеуральскую тюрьму
content:
Он ждал осмотра врача полгода и это время похудел на 20 килограммов. Ему нужна помощь адвоката, сообщает проект «Огни Свободы».

Григорьев осужден на 20 лет лишения свободы по обвинению в приготовлении к поджогу релейного шкафа и расклейку в Новотроицке Оренбургской области листовок с призывом к российским солдатам сдаваться в плен. В марте 2026 года Григорьева избили во время этапа из СИЗО-5 Екатеринбурга в Верхнеуральскую тюрьму (Т-1) — предположительно, за разговор с военнопленными на украинском языке. После этого у Григорьева образовалась паховая грыжа.

Осмотра хирурга в Т-1 анархист дожидался полгода. По его словам, за это время он похудел на 20 килограммов. Григорьев говорит о «вываливающемся кишечнике» (при паховой грыже содержимое брюшной полости выпячивается через паховый канал или рядом с ним) и постоянных болях в животе. После осмотра 1 октября хирург выдал Алексею направление в тюремную больницу. Чтобы добиться лечения, ему нужны юридические консультации по вопросам условий содержания и оказания медицинской помощи. На работу адвоката, который будет посещать Алексея в тюрьме, нужно собрать 70 тысяч рублей.

title: Babil Kuleleri 19 Ekim’de Maltepe’de sahnelenecek: Sınıf eşitsizliğini sahneye taşıyor
content:
Babil Kuleleri adlı oyundan bir sahne.

Bakırköy Belediye Tiyatroları (BBT), yeni sezonun ilk turnesinde 8. Uluslararası Maltepe Tiyatro Festivali’ne katılacak. Ebru Nihan Celkan’ın yazdığı, Fidan Tek Koşar’ın yönettiği Babil Kuleleri, 19 Ekim’de Maltepe Belediyesi Türkan Saylan Kültür Merkezi’nde sahnelenecek.

Bakırköy Belediye Tiyatroları, yeni sezonda yenilenen görsel kimliği ve repertuvarıyla seyirci karşısına çıkıyor. 8 Ekim’de sezonu açan tiyatronun yeni sezondaki ilk turne durağı, 8. Uluslararası Maltepe Tiyatro Festivali olacak.

Genel Sanat Yönetmeni Ragıp Savaş yönetiminde çalışmalarını sürdüren BBT, festival kapsamında Babil Kuleleri oyununu sahneleyecek. Ebru Nihan Celkan’ın kaleme aldığı, Fidan Tek Koşar’ın yönettiği oyun, 19 Ekim Pazartesi günü saat 20.00’de Maltepe Belediyesi Türkan Saylan Kültür Merkezi’nde izleyiciyle buluşacak.

Bir şantiye alanından lüks bir gökdelenin satış ofisine uzanan Babil Kuleleri, iş cinayetlerini ve farklı toplumsal sınıflar arasındaki görünmez ilişkileri ele alıyor. Yükselen binaların gölgesinde kalan emekçilerin yaşamlarını odağına alan oyun, modern kent yaşamındaki eşitsizlikleri ve sınıfsal çelişkileri sorguluyor.

Genel Sanat Yönetmeni Ragıp Savaş, tiyatronun yeni sezonuyla ilgili değerlendirmesinde dönüşümün yalnızca görsel bir değişiklik olmadığını belirtti. Savaş, amaçlarının tiyatronun sesini, enerjisini ve sahnede ele aldığı meseleleri sanatseverlerle buluşturmak olduğunu ifade ederek, geçmişten gelen birikimi çağdaş bir kimlikle sürdürmeyi hedeflediklerini söyledi.

Oyunun dekor tasarımını Ali Yenel, ışık tasarımını İlker Dursun, müziğini Melih Yüzer, ses tasarımını ise Uğur Çerkezoğlu üstleniyor. Yapımda Alper Altuner, Burak Dur, Çetin Etili, Doğuş Can Uzun, Gözde Ayar, İrem Sultan Cengiz ve Özge Çatak rol alıyor.
